set-algebra.definition:
集合论里最基础的运算是并、交、补。给定全集 $X$（例如 $\mathbb{R}$），我们常常只关心一部分子集，希望它们在运算下「自给自足」。**集合列的上下极限**是极限概念的集合版本：设 $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ 是 $X$ 的一列子集，称点 $x$ 属于**上极限** $\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n$，如果 $x$ 属于无穷多个 $A_n$；称 $x$ 属于**下极限** $\liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n$，如果除有限多个 $n$ 外，$x$ 属于所有 $A_n$。用集合运算写出来就是 $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\qquad \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.$$ 直观上，$\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ 是「第 $k$ 项以后至少命中一次」的点，再对所有 $k$ 取交，就是「每一段尾巴都命中」，即无穷多次命中；对偶地，$\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ 是「从第 $k$ 项起一直命中」的点，对所有 $k$ 取并就是「迟早一直命中」。显然恒有 $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$；当两者相等时，称集合列有极限 $\lim A_n$。

**$\sigma$ 代数**（读作 sigma 代数）是测度论中「可以测量的集合」的合法范围。$X$ 的子集族 $\mathcal{A}$ 称为 $\sigma$ 代数，如果 (1) $X\in\mathcal{A}$（含全集）；(2) $A\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow A^{c}=X\setminus A\in\mathcal{A}$（对补封闭）；(3) 若 $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{A}$，则 $\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal{A}$（对**可数并**封闭）。注意第三条只要求可数并，不要求任意并。由德摩根律 $\left(\bigcup_n A_n\right)^{c}=\bigcap_n A_n^{c}$，对补封闭加上对可数并封闭立刻推出对**可数交**也封闭。由 (1)(2) 又得到 $\varnothing\in\mathcal{A}$，所以公理也可以等价地表述为：含全集、对补封闭、对可数并封闭。最简单的例子是 $\{\varnothing,X\}$ 与幂集 $2^X$，它们分别是「最粗」与「最细」的 $\sigma$ 代数，而它们中间的族才是有用的。

给定任意一个子集族 $\mathcal{E}$，包含 $\mathcal{E}$ 的所有 $\sigma$ 代数之交仍是 $\sigma$ 代数，称为由 $\mathcal{E}$ **生成**的 $\sigma$ 代数，记作 $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$——它是让 $\mathcal{E}$ 中每个集合都可测的「最省」的选择。实数轴上最重要的例子是由全体开集生成的 **Borel $\sigma$ 代数** $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$。之所以先谈 $\sigma$ 代数：测度正是定义在它上面的集函数，只有先确定「哪些集合可测」，才谈得上「这个集合有多大」。
set-algebra.definitionEn:
Union, intersection and complement are the elementary operations on sets. Given a universal set $X$ (say $\mathbb{R}$), one usually singles out a family of subsets that is self-contained under these operations. **Limits of a sequence of sets** are the set-theoretic analogue of limits: for subsets $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ of $X$, a point $x$ lies in the **limit superior** $\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n$ if it belongs to infinitely many of the $A_n$, and in the **limit inferior** $\liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n$ if, apart from finitely many indices, it belongs to all of them. In set notation, $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\qquad \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.$$ Intuitively $\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ consists of the points that hit at least once after term $k$, and intersecting over all $k$ means hitting in every tail, i.e. infinitely often; dually, $\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ consists of the points that stay in from term $k$ onwards, so the union over all $k$ means 'eventually always'. Always $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$; when the two coincide the sequence is said to have a limit $\lim A_n$.

A **$\sigma$-algebra** is the legitimate universe of 'measurable sets' in measure theory. A family $\mathcal{A}$ of subsets of $X$ is a $\sigma$-algebra if (1) $X\in\mathcal{A}$; (2) $A\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow A^{c}=X\setminus A\in\mathcal{A}$ (closed under complements); (3) $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal{A}$ (closed under **countable unions**). Only countable unions are required, not arbitrary ones; by De Morgan's law $\left(\bigcup_n A_n\right)^{c}=\bigcap_n A_n^{c}$, closure under complements and countable unions yields closure under **countable intersections**. From (1) and (2) also $\varnothing\in\mathcal{A}$. The simplest examples are $\{\varnothing,X\}$ and the power set $2^X$, the coarsest and the finest $\sigma$-algebras on $X$.

For any family $\mathcal{E}$, the intersection of all $\sigma$-algebras containing $\mathcal{E}$ is again a $\sigma$-algebra; it is called the $\sigma$-algebra **generated** by $\mathcal{E}$ and written $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ — the smallest choice making every set in $\mathcal{E}$ measurable. On the real line the key example is the **Borel $\sigma$-algebra** $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$, generated by all open sets. $\sigma$-algebras come first because a measure is a set function defined on them: one must know which sets are measurable before asking how large they are.
derivation:
设 $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ 是 $X$ 的子集列，定义
$$\begin{aligned}\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n&=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n&=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.\end{aligned}$$
对点 $x$：$x\in\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ 当且仅当存在 $n\ge k$ 使 $x\in A_n$，所以 $x\in\limsup A_n$ 当且仅当对每个 $k$ 都存在 $n\ge k$ 使 $x\in A_n$，即 $x$ 属于无穷多个 $A_n$。同理，$x\in\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ 当且仅当所有 $n\ge k$ 都满足 $x\in A_n$，故 $x\in\liminf A_n$ 当且仅当存在 $k$ 使 $x$ 从第 $k$ 项起一直在 $A_n$ 中，即 $x$ 至多漏掉有限多个 $A_n$。结论：上极限是「无穷多次命中」，下极限是「最终一直命中」。

设 $x\in\liminf A_n$。由第 1 步，存在 $k_0$ 使 $x\in A_n$ 对所有 $n\ge k_0$ 成立。任取 $j\ge1$，令 $n=\max(j,k_0)$，则 $n\ge j$ 且 $x\in A_n$，故 $x\in\bigcup_{n\ge j}A_n$。由于 $j$ 任意，$x\in\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge j}A_n=\limsup A_n$。所以 $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$。反向一般不成立：取 $A_n=[0,2]$（$n$ 偶）、$A_n=[1,3]$（$n$ 奇），则 $[0,3]$ 中每点都落在无穷多个 $A_n$ 中，故 $\limsup A_n=[0,3]$；而 $x\in\liminf A_n$ 要求 $x$ 从某项起同时属于两类集合，故 $\liminf A_n=[1,2]\subsetneq[0,3]$。方向的记忆：下极限更小。

若 $A_n\uparrow$，即 $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$，则对每个 $k$，$\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n$，且 $\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n=A_k$。于是
$$\begin{aligned}\limsup A_n&=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\\&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n,\\ \liminf A_n&=\bigcup_{k\ge1}A_k\\&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n,\end{aligned}$$
两者相等。若 $A_n\downarrow$，则 $\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n=A_k$、$\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n=\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n$，故上下极限都等于 $\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n$。结论：单调集合列必有极限，递增时 $\lim A_n=\bigcup_n A_n$，递减时 $\lim A_n=\bigcap_n A_n$。这一步只用单调性，不涉及任何测度。

$X$ 的子集族 $\mathcal A$ 称为 σ 代数，若 (i) $X\in\mathcal A$；(ii) $A\in\mathcal A\Rightarrow A^c\in\mathcal A$；(iii) 若 $A_n\in\mathcal A$（$n\ge1$），则 $\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal A$。由 (i)(ii) 得 $\varnothing=X^c\in\mathcal A$。有限并：若 $A_1,\dots,A_N\in\mathcal A$，令 $A_n=\varnothing$（$n>N$），则 $\bigcup_{n\le N}A_n=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal A$。可数交：$\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n=\bigl(\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n^c\bigr)^c\in\mathcal A$。差：$A\setminus B=A\cap B^c\in\mathcal A$。特别地，若 $A_n\in\mathcal A$，则 $\limsup A_n$ 与 $\liminf A_n$ 作为可数并、交仍在 $\mathcal A$ 中。但 (iii) 只承诺可数并：在 $\mathbb R$ 上，令 $\mathcal A$ 为所有自身可数或补集可数的子集组成的族，则 $\mathcal A$ 是 σ 代数（可数并若有一项余可数则余可数，否则仍可数；补集互换两种情形），却不对任意并封闭——每个单点集 $\{x\}$ 都属于 $\mathcal A$，而 $\bigcup_{x\in[0,1]}\{x\}=[0,1]$ 既不可数、补集也不可数，故 $[0,1]\notin\mathcal A$。

设 $\mathcal E\subseteq2^X$。先证任意多个 σ 代数之交仍是 σ 代数：若 $\{\mathcal A_i\}_{i\in I}$ 都是 σ 代数，令 $\mathcal A=\bigcap_{i\in I}\mathcal A_i$。$X$ 属于每个 $\mathcal A_i$，故 $X\in\mathcal A$；若 $A\in\mathcal A$，则 $A\in\mathcal A_i$ 对所有 $i$ 成立，故 $A^c\in\mathcal A_i$ 对所有 $i$ 成立，即 $A^c\in\mathcal A$；对可数并同理。因此所有包含 $\mathcal E$ 的 σ 代数之交
$$\sigma(\mathcal E)=\bigcap_{\mathcal A\supseteq\mathcal E}\mathcal A$$
仍是 σ 代数；该族非空（含幂集 $2^X$），故交有意义，且它是包含 $\mathcal E$ 的最小 σ 代数。取 $\mathcal E$ 为 $\mathbb R$ 的全体开集，得 Borel σ 代数 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$。注意两个 σ 代数之并一般不是 σ 代数：在 $X=\{1,2,3\}$ 上，$\mathcal A_1=\{\varnothing,\{1\},\{2,3\},X\}$ 与 $\mathcal A_2=\{\varnothing,\{2\},\{1,3\},X\}$ 都是 σ 代数，但 $\{1\},\{2\}\in\mathcal A_1\cup\mathcal A_2$，而 $\{1,2\}\notin\mathcal A_1\cup\mathcal A_2$。

设 $\mathcal A$ 是 $X$ 上的有限 σ 代数。对 $x\in X$ 令 $A_x=\bigcap\{A\in\mathcal A:x\in A\}$。这是有限多个 $\mathcal A$ 中集合之交（该族非空，因 $X\in\mathcal A$），故 $A_x\in\mathcal A$，且 $x\in A_x$。若 $y\in A_x$，则 $y$ 属于每个含 $x$ 的 $A\in\mathcal A$；又若某个 $A\in\mathcal A$ 含 $y$ 而不含 $x$，则 $x\in A^c\in\mathcal A$，故 $y$ 应属于 $A^c$，但 $y\in A$，与 $y\in A_x$ 矛盾。故 $x,y$ 属于完全相同的 $\mathcal A$ 中集合，从而 $A_x=A_y$。于是不同的 $A_x$ 构成 $X$ 的有限划分（原子）。每个 $A\in\mathcal A$ 若含 $x$ 便含 $A_x$，故 $A$ 等于所含原子之并；反之有限个原子之并属于 $\mathcal A$。所以 $\mathcal A$ 恰由 $k$ 个原子的一切并组成，$|\mathcal A|=2^k$。
derivationEn:
Let $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ be a sequence of subsets of $X$, and set
$$\begin{aligned}\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n&=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n&=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.\end{aligned}$$
For a point $x$, $x\in\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ iff $x\in A_n$ for some $n\ge k$. Hence $x\in\limsup A_n$ iff for every $k$ there is some $n\ge k$ with $x\in A_n$, i.e. $x$ belongs to infinitely many $A_n$. Likewise, $x\in\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ iff $x\in A_n$ for all $n\ge k$, so $x\in\liminf A_n$ iff $x$ stays in $A_n$ from some index $k$ onward, i.e. $x$ misses at most finitely many of the $A_n$. Conclusion: the superior limit means "hit infinitely often" and the inferior limit means "eventually always hit".

Let $x\in\liminf A_n$. By Step 1 there is $k_0$ with $x\in A_n$ for all $n\ge k_0$. Given any $j\ge1$, put $n=\max(j,k_0)$; then $n\ge j$ and $x\in A_n$, so $x\in\bigcup_{n\ge j}A_n$. Since $j$ was arbitrary, $x\in\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge j}A_n=\limsup A_n$. Hence $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$. The reverse inclusion fails in general: take $A_n=[0,2]$ for even $n$ and $A_n=[1,3]$ for odd $n$. Every point of $[0,3]$ lies in infinitely many $A_n$, so $\limsup A_n=[0,3]$; but a point of $\liminf A_n$ must belong to both types of sets from some index on, so $\liminf A_n=[1,2]\subsetneq[0,3]$. Direction to remember: the inferior limit is the smaller one.

If $A_n\uparrow$, i.e. $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$, then for every $k$, $\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n$ and $\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n=A_k$. Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\limsup A_n&=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\\&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n,\\ \liminf A_n&=\bigcup_{k\ge1}A_k\\&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n,\end{aligned}$$
so the two coincide. If $A_n\downarrow$, then $\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n=A_k$ and $\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n=\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n$, so both limits equal $\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n$. Conclusion: every monotone sequence of sets has a limit, namely $\bigcup_n A_n$ when increasing and $\bigcap_n A_n$ when decreasing. Only monotonicity is used here; no measure is involved.

A family $\mathcal A$ of subsets of $X$ is a $\sigma$-algebra if (i) $X\in\mathcal A$; (ii) $A\in\mathcal A\Rightarrow A^c\in\mathcal A$; (iii) $A_n\in\mathcal A$ for $n\ge1$ implies $\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal A$. From (i) and (ii), $\varnothing=X^c\in\mathcal A$. Finite unions: if $A_1,\dots,A_N\in\mathcal A$, set $A_n=\varnothing$ for $n>N$; then $\bigcup_{n\le N}A_n=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal A$. Countable intersections: $\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n=\bigl(\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n^c\bigr)^c\in\mathcal A$. Differences: $A\setminus B=A\cap B^c\in\mathcal A$. In particular, if $A_n\in\mathcal A$, then $\limsup A_n$ and $\liminf A_n$, being countable unions and intersections, still lie in $\mathcal A$. But (iii) promises only countable unions: on $\mathbb R$, the family $\mathcal A$ of all subsets that are countable or have countable complement is a $\sigma$-algebra (a countable union is co-countable if one term is, and countable otherwise; complementation swaps the two cases), yet it is not closed under arbitrary unions: every singleton $\{x\}$ lies in $\mathcal A$, while $\bigcup_{x\in[0,1]}\{x\}=[0,1]$ is neither countable nor co-countable, so $[0,1]\notin\mathcal A$.

Let $\mathcal E\subseteq2^X$. First, the intersection of any family of $\sigma$-algebras is again a $\sigma$-algebra: if $\{\mathcal A_i\}_{i\in I}$ are $\sigma$-algebras and $\mathcal A=\bigcap_{i\in I}\mathcal A_i$, then $X$ belongs to every $\mathcal A_i$, hence to $\mathcal A$; if $A\in\mathcal A$, then $A\in\mathcal A_i$ for all $i$, so $A^c\in\mathcal A_i$ for all $i$, i.e. $A^c\in\mathcal A$; countable unions are handled in the same way. Therefore the intersection of all $\sigma$-algebras containing $\mathcal E$,
$$\sigma(\mathcal E)=\bigcap_{\mathcal A\supseteq\mathcal E}\mathcal A,$$
is a $\sigma$-algebra. The family is nonempty (it contains the power set $2^X$), so the intersection is defined, and it is the smallest $\sigma$-algebra containing $\mathcal E$. Taking $\mathcal E$ to be the family of all open subsets of $\mathbb R$ gives the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$. Note that the union of two $\sigma$-algebras is usually not a $\sigma$-algebra: on $X=\{1,2,3\}$, both $\mathcal A_1=\{\varnothing,\{1\},\{2,3\},X\}$ and $\mathcal A_2=\{\varnothing,\{2\},\{1,3\},X\}$ are $\sigma$-algebras, but $\{1\},\{2\}\in\mathcal A_1\cup\mathcal A_2$ while $\{1,2\}\notin\mathcal A_1\cup\mathcal A_2$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite $\sigma$-algebra on $X$. For $x\in X$ put $A_x=\bigcap\{A\in\mathcal A:x\in A\}$. This is a finite intersection of members of $\mathcal A$ (the family is nonempty since $X\in\mathcal A$), so $A_x\in\mathcal A$ and $x\in A_x$. If $y\in A_x$, then $y$ lies in every $A\in\mathcal A$ that contains $x$; and if some $A\in\mathcal A$ contained $y$ but not $x$, then $x\in A^c\in\mathcal A$, so $y$ should lie in $A^c$ although $y\in A$, contradicting $y\in A_x$. Thus $x$ and $y$ belong to exactly the same members of $\mathcal A$, whence $A_x=A_y$. Therefore the distinct sets $A_x$ form a finite partition of $X$ into atoms. Every $A\in\mathcal A$ that contains $x$ also contains $A_x$, so $A$ is the union of the atoms it contains; conversely, a finite union of atoms lies in $\mathcal A$. Hence $\mathcal A$ consists exactly of all unions of its $k$ atoms, and $|\mathcal A|=2^k$.

formulas.note: 上极限：属于无穷多个 $A_n$ 的点全体，等价于对每个 $k$ 都在第 $k$ 项以后的并中出现。
formulas.noteEn: Limit superior: the set of points lying in infinitely many $A_n$, i.e. in the tail union for every $k$.

formulas.note: 下极限：至多漏掉有限多个 $A_n$ 的点全体（「最终一直命中」）。
formulas.noteEn: Limit inferior: points that miss at most finitely many of the $A_n$ ('eventually always in').

formulas.note: 下极限总包含在上极限里；两者相等时称集合列收敛，单调集合列必收敛。
formulas.noteEn: The inferior limit is always contained in the superior limit; equality defines convergence of the set sequence, which always holds for monotone sequences.

formulas.note: 德摩根律：配合对补封闭，σ 代数的可数并公理自动带来对可数交封闭。
formulas.noteEn: De Morgan's law: together with closure under complements, the countable union axiom yields closure under countable intersections.

formulas.note: σ 代数三条公理：含全集、对补封闭、对可数并封闭。
formulas.noteEn: The three axioms of a σ-algebra: contains $X$, closed under complements, closed under countable unions.

properties: 上极限由「属于无穷多个 $A_n$」刻画，下极限由「至多漏掉有限多个 $A_n$」刻画，且恒有 $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$。
σ 代数对补、可数并封闭，因而也对可数交、可数差封闭，并且必含 $\varnothing$ 与 $X$。
任意多个 σ 代数之交仍是 σ 代数，所以由集合族 $\mathcal{E}$ 生成的最小 σ 代数 $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ 总存在；但两个 σ 代数之并一般不是 σ 代数。
有限 σ 代数恰由 $X$ 的某个有限划分生成，其元素个数为 $2^{k}$（$k$ 为划分的块数）。
单调集合列必收敛：$A_n\uparrow$ 时上下极限都等于 $\bigcup_n A_n$；$A_n\downarrow$ 时都等于 $\bigcap_n A_n$。
propertiesEn: The limit superior consists of the points in infinitely many $A_n$, the limit inferior of those missing at most finitely many; always $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$.
A σ-algebra is closed under complements and countable unions, hence also under countable intersections and countable differences, and contains both $\varnothing$ and $X$.

The intersection of any family of σ-algebras is again a σ-algebra, so the smallest σ-algebra $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ generated by a family $\mathcal{E}$ always exists; a union of two σ-algebras usually is not a σ-algebra.
A finite σ-algebra is generated by a finite partition of $X$ and has exactly $2^{k}$ elements, where $k$ is the number of blocks.
Monotone sequences always converge: if $A_n\uparrow$ both limits equal $\bigcup_n A_n$, and if $A_n\downarrow$ both equal $\bigcap_n A_n$.

examples.problem: 设 $A_n=[0,2]$（$n$ 为偶数），$A_n=[1,3]$（$n$ 为奇数），求 $\limsup A_n$ 与 $\liminf A_n$。
examples.solution: $x\in\limsup A_n$ 当且仅当 $x$ 属于无穷多个 $A_n$。若 $x\in[0,2]$，则所有偶数项都含 $x$，故 $x\in\limsup A_n$；同理 $x\in[1,3]$ 时所有奇数项都含 $x$。反之若 $x\notin[0,3]$，则 $x$ 不属于任何 $A_n$。让两部分合起来得 $\limsup A_n=[0,3]$。而 $x\in\liminf A_n$ 要求从某一项起所有 $A_n$ 都含 $x$；从某项起既有偶数项也有奇数项，故 $x$ 必须同时属于 $[0,2]$ 与 $[1,3]$，即 $x\in[1,2]$；反之 $x\in[1,2]$ 时每个 $A_n$ 都含 $x$。因此 $\liminf A_n=[1,2]$，它严格包含于 $[0,3]$。

逐条验证公理。含全集：$\{1,2,3\}\in\mathcal{A}$。对补封闭：$\{1\}^{c}=\{2,3\}$、$\{2,3\}^{c}=\{1\}$、$\varnothing^{c}=X$ 都仍在 $\mathcal{A}$ 中。对有限并封闭（有限族只需验证有限并）：$\{1\}\cup\{2,3\}=X$，与 $\varnothing$ 或 $X$ 的并仍是自身或 $X$，故封闭。所以 $\mathcal{A}$ 是 σ 代数，它就是由划分 $\{\{1\},\{2,3\}\}$ 生成的 σ 代数。对照：$\mathcal{A}'=\{\varnothing,\{1\},\{2\},X\}$ 不是 σ 代数，因为 $\{1\}\cup\{2\}=\{1,2\}\notin\mathcal{A}'$。

expression.text: limsup Aₙ = ∩_{k≥1} ∪_{n≥k} Aₙ，liminf Aₙ = ∪_{k≥1} ∩_{n≥k} Aₙ（「∪ 与 ∩ 交替」即可记忆）
expression.note: σ(ℰ) 是包含集合族 ℰ 的一切 σ 代数之交，也是让 ℰ 中集合全部可测的最小 σ 代数。
expression.noteEn: σ(ℰ) is the intersection of all σ-algebras containing ℰ, the smallest one in which every set of ℰ is measurable.

outer-measure.definition:
对任意集合 $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$，我们想给它一个「长度」。直接沿用几何直觉对一般集合无从下手，但任何集合总可以被可数多个开区间盖住；这些区间的长度总和提供了 $E$ 大小的一个上界，而这个上界越小就越贴近真正的长度。

**定义**：$E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 的**勒贝格外测度**为 $$m^{*}(E)=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k| : E\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k\Bigr\},$$ 这里的 $I_k$ 取遍开区间，$|I_k|$ 表示其长度（有限区间 $I=(a,b)$ 时 $|I|=b-a$，空区间长为 $0$）。有限个区间的覆盖只要补上若干个空区间就变成可数覆盖，所以「可数覆盖」已包含「有限覆盖」的情形；又因为每个 $E$ 都有覆盖（例如用 $\mathbb{R}$ 自身），下确界总是对非空集合取的，取值于 $[0,+\infty]$。

这个定义抓住了「用简单形状从外面逼近」的思想，由此立刻得到一串性质：非负性 $m^{*}(E)\ge0$；**单调性** $E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$（覆盖 $F$ 的区间族当然也覆盖 $E$，下确界只会更小）；平移不变性 $m^{*}(E+t)=m^{*}(E)$；以及最关键的**可数次可加性** $$m^{*}\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^{*}(E_n).$$ 证明的思路是把每个 $E_n$ 的覆盖拼起来、再用 $2^{-n}\varepsilon$ 控制总长度。注意这里只有单侧不等式，因为「从外面盖」天然只能给上界。

必须强调：外测度**一般不是可加的**。取区间内一个维塔利集 $E$，则 $E$ 与它的补集 $[0,1]\setminus E$ 不交，却有 $m^{*}(E)+m^{*}([0,1]\setminus E)>1=m^{*}([0,1])$，即 $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$。修补这一缺陷正是引入**可测集**的动机：把满足卡拉西奥多里条件的集合挑出来，外测度限制在它们身上才是真正的测度。所以可以说，外测度是打补丁的工具，可测集才是正式的测度。
outer-measure.definitionEn:
For an arbitrary set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ we want to assign a 'length'. Geometric intuition does not tell us what to do for a general set, but any set can be covered by countably many open intervals; the sum of their lengths is an upper bound for the size of $E$, and the smaller this bound the closer we are to the true length.

**Definition.** The **Lebesgue outer measure** of $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is $$m^{*}(E)=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k| : E\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k,\ I_k\ \text{open intervals}\Bigr\},$$ where $|I_k|$ is the length of $I_k$ ($|I|=b-a$ for $I=(a,b)$, and $0$ for an empty interval). A finite cover becomes a countable one by adding empty intervals, so the infimum is taken over a nonempty family for every $E$, and the values lie in $[0,+\infty]$.

The construction captures approximation from outside by simple shapes, and it immediately yields: nonnegativity $m^{*}\ge0$; **monotonicity** $E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$, since a cover of $F$ also covers $E$; translation invariance $m^{*}(E+t)=m^{*}(E)$; and most importantly **countable subadditivity** $$m^{*}\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^{*}(E_n),$$ proved by pasting together covers of the single sets and controlling the total length by an $2^{-n}\varepsilon$ argument. Only one-sided inequalities appear here, because covering from outside can only produce upper bounds.

It must be stressed that outer measure is **not additive in general**. Take a Vitali set $E$ inside $[0,1]$; then $E$ and its complement are disjoint and yet $m^{*}(E)+m^{*}([0,1]\setminus E)>1=m^{*}([0,1])$, i.e. $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$ for disjoint sets. Repairing this defect is precisely the motivation for **measurable sets**: one singles out the sets satisfying Carathéodory's condition, and on them the outer measure becomes a genuine measure. Thus the outer measure is the patch, while the measurable sets are the real thing.
derivation:
对 $E\subseteq\mathbb R$ 定义
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(E)=\inf\Bigl\{&\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|:\\ &E\subseteq\bigcup_k I_k\Bigr\},\end{aligned}$$
其中 $I_k$ 取遍开区间。覆盖族非空，例如 $E\subseteq\mathbb R=(-\infty,+\infty)$，因此下确界在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中有定义。有限覆盖可通过补入空区间（长度 $0$）化为可数覆盖，所以定义已包含有限覆盖。若 $E=\varnothing$，对任意 $\varepsilon>0$ 取 $I_1=(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$、其余 $I_k$ 为空区间，则长度和为 $2\varepsilon$，故 $m^*(\varnothing)\le2\varepsilon$ 对一切 $\varepsilon>0$ 成立，令 $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ 得 $m^*(\varnothing)=0$。

设 $E\subseteq F\subseteq\mathbb R$。记 $\mathcal C(E)$ 为覆盖 $E$ 的可数开区间族之集。任何覆盖 $F$ 的族也覆盖 $E$，故 $\mathcal C(F)\subseteq\mathcal C(E)$。在更大的族上下确界只会更小：
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(E)&=\inf_{c\in\mathcal C(E)}\sum_k|I_k|\\&\le\inf_{c\in\mathcal C(F)}\sum_k|I_k|=m^*(F).\end{aligned}$$
所以 $m^*$ 单调。此步未用可加性，对任意集合都成立。

设 $E_n\subseteq\mathbb R$。若某个 $m^*(E_n)=+\infty$，则右端为 $+\infty$，不等式自动成立。以下设所有 $m^*(E_n)<+\infty$，任取 $\varepsilon>0$。由下确界定义，对每个 $n$ 存在开区间覆盖 $\{I_{n,k}\}_{k\ge1}$ 使
$$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_{n,k}|<m^*(E_n)+\frac{\varepsilon}{2^n}.$$
全体 $I_{n,k}$（$n,k\ge1$）是可数族，且覆盖 $\bigcup_n E_n$，故
$$\begin{aligned}m^*\Bigl(\bigcup_n E_n\Bigr)&\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_{n,k}|\\&<\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^*(E_n)+\varepsilon.\end{aligned}$$
令 $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ 得可数次可加性 $m^*(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^*(E_n)$。这里没有假设 $E_n$ 两两不交。取 $E_n=\{x_n\}$ 并用长度 $\varepsilon/2^n$ 的开区间覆盖，即知任何可数集的外测度为 $0$。

先算 $[a,b]$（$a<b$）。上界：对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，$[a,b]\subseteq(a-\varepsilon,b+\varepsilon)$，故 $m^*([a,b])\le b-a+2\varepsilon$，令 $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ 得 $m^*([a,b])\le b-a$。下界：设 $\{I_k\}$ 是任一可数开区间覆盖。因 $[a,b]$ 紧，由 Heine–Borel 定理存在有限子覆盖 $I_{k_1},\dots,I_{k_N}$。有限个区间之并的长度不超过各长度之和（对个数归纳，用 $|J\cup I|\le|J|+|I|$），且该并包含 $[a,b]$，故
$$\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|&\ge\sum_{j=1}^{N}|I_{k_j}|\\&\ge\Bigl|\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}I_{k_j}\Bigr|\ge b-a.\end{aligned}$$
对一切覆盖取下确界得 $m^*([a,b])\ge b-a$。两方向合并：$m^*([a,b])=b-a$。端点不影响长度，故 $(a,b)$、$(a,b]$、$[a,b)$ 的外测度同样是 $b-a$。

在 $[0,1]$ 上定义等价关系 $x\sim y\iff x-y\in\mathbb Q$。由选择公理，从每个等价类取一个代表元，组成 $V\subseteq[0,1]$。对 $q\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$ 令 $V_q=V+q$。若 $V_{q_1}\cap V_{q_2}\ne\varnothing$，则有 $v_1,v_2\in V$ 使 $v_1+q_1=v_2+q_2$，于是 $v_1-v_2=q_2-q_1\in\mathbb Q$，即 $v_1\sim v_2$；同一类只取一个代表元，故 $v_1=v_2$、$q_1=q_2$。所以 $\{V_q\}$ 两两不交，且都含于 $[-1,2]$。另一方面，任取 $x\in[0,1]$，设 $v\in V$ 是 $x$ 所在类的代表元，则 $x-v\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$，故 $x\in V_{x-v}$，即 $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_q V_q$。
假设 $m^*$ 对不交集合有限可加，令 $\alpha=m^*(V)$。平移不变性来自区间长度在平移下不变：覆盖 $V$ 的区间族平移后覆盖 $V+q$，长度和不变，反之亦然。任取 $N$ 个互不相同的 $q_1,\dots,q_N\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$，于是 $m^*(V_{q_j})=\alpha$，故
$$N\alpha=m^*\Bigl(\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}V_{q_j}\Bigr)\le m^*([-1,2])=3.$$
若 $\alpha=+\infty$，则 $N\alpha=+\infty$，与 $N\alpha\le3$ 矛盾；故 $\alpha<+\infty$，令 $N\to\infty$ 得 $\alpha=0$。再由可数次可加性，
$$1=m^*([0,1])\le\sum_q m^*(V_q)=0,$$
矛盾。因此存在不交的 $E_1,E_2$ 使 $m^*(E_1\cup E_2)<m^*(E_1)+m^*(E_2)$（反向的 $\le$ 由次可加性自动成立），即外测度不是测度。

可数次可加性不能加强为不可数次可加。以 $[0,1]=\bigcup_{x\in[0,1]}\{x\}$ 为例。每个单点集的外测度为 $0$（第 3 步），若不可数次可加性成立，则
$$1=m^*([0,1])\le\sum_{x\in[0,1]}m^*(\{x\})=0,$$
矛盾（不可数族的和非负项时按有限子和的上确界定义，这里仍为 $0$）。所以外测度只对可数并给出次可加估计，而且一般不可加。把外测度限制到一个合适的 σ 代数上、使它成为真正可数可加的测度，正是 Carathéodory 条件的作用。
derivationEn:
For $E\subseteq\mathbb R$ define
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(E)=\inf\Bigl\{&\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|:\\ &E\subseteq\bigcup_k I_k\Bigr\},\end{aligned}$$
where the $I_k$ range over open intervals. The family of covers is nonempty, e.g. $E\subseteq\mathbb R=(-\infty,+\infty)$, so the infimum is defined in $[0,+\infty]$. A finite cover becomes a countable one by adding empty intervals of length $0$, so finite covers are already included. If $E=\varnothing$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ take $I_1=(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ and all other $I_k$ empty; the total length is $2\varepsilon$, so $m^*(\varnothing)\le2\varepsilon$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, and letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives $m^*(\varnothing)=0$.

Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal C(E)$ be the set of countable open-interval covers of $E$. Every cover of $F$ also covers $E$, so $\mathcal C(F)\subseteq\mathcal C(E)$. Taking the infimum over a larger family can only decrease the value:
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(E)&=\inf_{c\in\mathcal C(E)}\sum_k|I_k|\\&\le\inf_{c\in\mathcal C(F)}\sum_k|I_k|=m^*(F).\end{aligned}$$
Thus $m^*$ is monotone. No additivity is used, so this holds for arbitrary sets.

Let $E_n\subseteq\mathbb R$. If some $m^*(E_n)=+\infty$, the right-hand side is $+\infty$ and the inequality is automatic. Otherwise all $m^*(E_n)<+\infty$; fix $\varepsilon>0$. By definition of the infimum, for each $n$ there is an open-interval cover $\{I_{n,k}\}_{k\ge1}$ with
$$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_{n,k}|<m^*(E_n)+\frac{\varepsilon}{2^n}.$$
The family of all $I_{n,k}$ ($n,k\ge1$) is countable and covers $\bigcup_n E_n$, hence
$$\begin{aligned}m^*\Bigl(\bigcup_n E_n\Bigr)&\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_{n,k}|\\&<\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^*(E_n)+\varepsilon.\end{aligned}$$
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives countable subadditivity $m^*(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^*(E_n)$. No disjointness of the $E_n$ is assumed. Taking $E_n=\{x_n\}$ and covering each point by an interval of length $\varepsilon/2^n$ shows that every countable set has outer measure $0$.

First compute $[a,b]$ with $a<b$. Upper bound: for every $\varepsilon>0$, $[a,b]\subseteq(a-\varepsilon,b+\varepsilon)$, so $m^*([a,b])\le b-a+2\varepsilon$; letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives $m^*([a,b])\le b-a$. Lower bound: let $\{I_k\}$ be any countable open-interval cover. Since $[a,b]$ is compact, the Heine–Borel theorem gives a finite subcover $I_{k_1},\dots,I_{k_N}$. The length of a finite union of intervals is at most the sum of their lengths (induct on the number of intervals, using $|J\cup I|\le|J|+|I|$), and this union contains $[a,b]$, so
$$\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|&\ge\sum_{j=1}^{N}|I_{k_j}|\\&\ge\Bigl|\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}I_{k_j}\Bigr|\ge b-a.\end{aligned}$$
Taking the infimum over all covers gives $m^*([a,b])\ge b-a$. Combining both directions, $m^*([a,b])=b-a$. Endpoints do not affect length, so $(a,b)$, $(a,b]$ and $[a,b)$ have outer measure $b-a$ as well.

On $[0,1]$ define the equivalence relation $x\sim y\iff x-y\in\mathbb Q$. By the axiom of choice, choose one representative from each class; let $V\subseteq[0,1]$ be the set of representatives. For $q\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$ put $V_q=V+q$. If $V_{q_1}\cap V_{q_2}\ne\varnothing$, then $v_1+q_1=v_2+q_2$ for some $v_1,v_2\in V$, so $v_1-v_2=q_2-q_1\in\mathbb Q$, i.e. $v_1\sim v_2$; since only one representative is chosen per class, $v_1=v_2$ and $q_1=q_2$. Hence the $V_q$ are pairwise disjoint and all lie in $[-1,2]$. On the other hand, for $x\in[0,1]$, let $v\in V$ be the representative of its class; then $x-v\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$, so $x\in V_{x-v}$, i.e. $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_q V_q$.
Suppose $m^*$ were finitely additive on disjoint sets, and let $\alpha=m^*(V)$. Translation invariance follows because interval lengths are unchanged by translation: a cover of $V$ translates to a cover of $V+q$ with the same total length, and conversely. Choose any $N$ distinct indices $q_1,\dots,q_N\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$; then $m^*(V_{q_j})=\alpha$, so
$$N\alpha=m^*\Bigl(\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}V_{q_j}\Bigr)\le m^*([-1,2])=3.$$
If $\alpha=+\infty$, then $N\alpha=+\infty$, contradicting $N\alpha\le3$; hence $\alpha<+\infty$, and letting $N\to\infty$ gives $\alpha=0$. Countable subadditivity then yields
$$1=m^*([0,1])\le\sum_q m^*(V_q)=0,$$
a contradiction. Therefore there are disjoint $E_1,E_2$ with $m^*(E_1\cup E_2)<m^*(E_1)+m^*(E_2)$ (the reverse inequality follows from subadditivity): outer measure is not a measure.

Countable subadditivity cannot be strengthened to uncountable subadditivity. Consider $[0,1]=\bigcup_{x\in[0,1]}\{x\}$. Every singleton has outer measure $0$ (Step 3), so if uncountable subadditivity held, then
$$1=m^*([0,1])\le\sum_{x\in[0,1]}m^*(\{x\})=0,$$
a contradiction (for a nonnegative uncountable family the sum is defined as the supremum of finite subsums, which is still $0$ here). Thus outer measure gives subadditive estimates only for countable unions, and it is not additive in general. Restricting it to a suitable $\sigma$-algebra so that it becomes a genuinely countably additive measure is precisely the role of Carathéodory's condition.

formulas.note: 定义：所有可数开区间覆盖的长度和的下确界；把开区间换成闭区间或半开区间得到的值相同。
formulas.noteEn: Definition: the infimum of the total lengths of all countable covers by open intervals; using closed or half-open intervals gives the same value.

formulas.note: 非负性与单调性：覆盖 $F$ 的区间族同样覆盖 $E$。
formulas.noteEn: Nonnegativity and monotonicity: any cover of $F$ also covers $E$.

formulas.note: 可数次可加性：不要求 $E_n$ 两两不交，这是外测度最常用的性质。
formulas.noteEn: Countable subadditivity: no disjointness is required; this is the most used property of outer measure.

formulas.note: 区间的外测度就是长度；外测度在平移下不变。可数集的（外）测度为 $0$，例如稠密的 $\mathbb{Q}$。
formulas.noteEn: An interval has outer measure equal to its length, and the outer measure is translation invariant. Countable sets such as the dense $\mathbb{Q}$ have outer measure 0.

formulas.note: 一般不可加：存在不交集合使次可加性取严格不等号，这正是引入可测集的原因。
formulas.noteEn: Not additive in general: disjoint sets can violate additivity strictly, which motivates measurable sets.

properties: 外测度对 $\mathbb{R}$ 的每个子集（包括病态集合）都有定义，取值在 $[0,+\infty]$ 内。
非负且单调：$E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$，并且 $m^{*}(\varnothing)=0$。
可数次可加：$m^{*}(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^{*}(E_n)$，不需要 $E_n$ 两两不交。
平移不变，且 $m^{*}([a,b])=b-a$；可数集的（外）测度为 $0$，尽管它可以很稠密（如 $\mathbb{Q}$）。
一般不可加：存在不交集合 $E_1,E_2$ 使 $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$，这是可测集概念出场的原因。
propertiesEn: Defined for every subset of $\mathbb{R}$, pathological ones included, with values in $[0,+\infty]$.
Nonnegative and monotone: $E\subseteq F$ implies $m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$, and $m^{*}(\varnothing)=0$.
Countably subadditive: $m^{*}(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^{*}(E_n)$, with no disjointness assumption.
Translation invariant, with $m^{*}([a,b])=b-a$; countable sets (such as the dense set $\mathbb{Q}$) have outer measure 0.
Not additive in general: there are disjoint $E_1,E_2$ with $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$, which brings measurable sets onto the stage.

examples.problem: 证明任意可数集 $E=\{x_1,x_2,\dots\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 的外测度为 $0$。
examples.solution: 任取 $\varepsilon>0$。对每个 $k$ 取开区间 $I_k=\left(x_k-\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k+1}},\ x_k+\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k+1}}\right)$，则 $|I_k|=\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k}}$，且 $E\subseteq\bigcup_{k\ge1}I_k$。由定义 $$m^{*}(E)\le\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|=\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-k}=\varepsilon.$$ 由于 $\varepsilon>0$ 任意，$m^{*}(E)\le\inf_{\varepsilon>0}\varepsilon=0$；又外测度非负，故 $m^{*}(E)=0$。特别地 $m^{*}(\mathbb{Q})=0$：有理数虽然稠密，总长度却是零。

上界：对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，$[0,1]\subseteq(-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)$，故 $m^{*}([0,1])\le1+2\varepsilon$，令 $\varepsilon\to0^{+}$ 得 $m^{*}([0,1])\le1$。下界：设 $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k$ 是任一可数开区间覆盖。由海涅-博雷尔有限覆盖定理，存在有限子覆盖 $I_{k_1},\dots,I_{k_N}$，而有限多个区间的并的长度不超过长度之和（用归纳法即可证明），因此 $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|\ge\sum_{j=1}^{N}|I_{k_j}|\ge\Bigl|\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}I_{k_j}\Bigr|\ge1.$$ 于是任何覆盖的长度和都 $\ge1$，取下确界得 $m^{*}([0,1])\ge1$。两方向合起来 $m^{*}([0,1])=1$。

expression.text: m*(E) = inf { Σₖ|Iₖ| : E ⊆ ∪ₖ Iₖ，Iₖ 为开区间 }
expression.note: 外测度对每个 E ⊆ ℝ 都有定义，但一般不满足可加性，「长度」的正式版本要等到可测集。
expression.noteEn: The outer measure is defined for every subset of ℝ, but is not additive in general; the official version of 'length' waits for measurable sets.

measurable-sets.definition:
外测度对一切集合都有定义，但一般不可加。为了让「长度」变成真正好用的测度，卡拉西奥多里给出了一个巧妙的判据：**把所有集合都当作「尺子」来检验**。集合 $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 称为**可测的**，如果对**任意** $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 都有 $$m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c}).$$ 注意 $A$ 是任意的「测试集」，只验证 $A=\mathbb{R}$ 这一个情形是不够的；又由次可加性 $m^{*}(A)\le m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})$ 自动成立，所以实际只需验证 $\ge$ 方向。

这个条件的意义是：$E$ 能把任何集合 $A$ 干净利落地「切开」，两侧的外测度相加而不漏水。可以证明，满足条件的集合类 $\mathcal{M}$ 构成一个 σ 代数：$\varnothing,\mathbb{R}\in\mathcal{M}$；条件本身关于 $E$ 与 $E^{c}$ 对称，故对补封闭；并且对可数并封闭。于是把 $m^{*}$ 限制在 $\mathcal{M}$ 上，记 $m=m^{*}|_{\mathcal{M}}$，就得到**勒贝格测度**，它满足 σ 可加性：对 $\mathcal{M}$ 中两两不交的集合列 $\{E_n\}$，$$m\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m(E_n).$$

哪些集合可测？开区间可测，从而一切开集、闭集以及它们的可数并、交、补（即一切 Borel 集）都可测；特别地所有区间都可测，且 $m([a,b])=b-a$。此外勒贝格测度是**完备的**：若 $m(N)=0$，则 $N$ 的任何子集也可测且测度为 $0$——这是黎曼积分理论无法提供的性质，它让「忽略零测集」成为合法的操作。

康托尔集是最著名的例子：从 $[0,1]$ 出发，每一步把每个剩余区间中间的 $1/3$ 开区间挖去。剩下的集合 $C$ 不可数，但挖去的总长度为 $\frac13+\frac29+\frac4{27}+\cdots=1$，所以 $m(C)=0$。它说明「不可数」推不出「测度为正」，也说明实数轴上有大量「看不见」的零测集。可测集类把这些病态集合隔离出来，使分析可以在干净的舞台上进行。
measurable-sets.definitionEn:
Outer measure is defined for every set but is not additive. To turn 'length' into a genuinely useful measure, Carathéodory found a clever test: use **all** sets as rulers. A set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is called **measurable** if for **every** $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, $$m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c}).$$ The test set $A$ is arbitrary — checking only $A=\mathbb{R}$ is not enough — and by subadditivity the inequality $\le$ is automatic, so only the direction $\ge$ has to be verified.

The condition means that $E$ cuts every set $A$ cleanly into two parts whose outer measures add up with no loss. One proves that the class $\mathcal{M}$ of measurable sets is a σ-algebra: $\varnothing,\mathbb{R}\in\mathcal{M}$; the condition is symmetric in $E$ and $E^{c}$, so $\mathcal{M}$ is closed under complements; and it is closed under countable unions. Restricting $m^{*}$ to $\mathcal{M}$, written $m=m^{*}|_{\mathcal{M}}$, gives **Lebesgue measure**, which is countably additive: for pairwise disjoint $E_n\in\mathcal{M}$, $$m\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m(E_n).$$

Which sets are measurable? Every open interval is; hence so are all open sets, closed sets, and their countable unions, intersections and complements — i.e. all Borel sets. In particular every interval is measurable with $m([a,b])=b-a$. Moreover Lebesgue measure is **complete**: if $m(N)=0$ then every subset of $N$ is measurable with measure $0$, a feature the Riemann theory cannot offer, and the legal basis for ignoring null sets.

The Cantor set is the standard example: starting from $[0,1]$, remove at each step the open middle third of every remaining interval. The remainder $C$ is uncountable, yet the total length removed is $\frac13+\frac29+\frac4{27}+\cdots=1$, so $m(C)=0$. Thus 'uncountable' does not imply 'positive measure', and there are plenty of invisible null sets on the line. The measurable sets isolate the pathologies and provide a clean stage for analysis.
derivation:
设 $E\subseteq\mathbb R$。称 $E$ 为 Lebesgue 可测，若对任意 $A\subseteq\mathbb R$，
$$m^*(A)=m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c).$$
测试集 $A$ 必须是任意的，只验证 $A=\mathbb R$ 不够。由外测度的次可加性，
$$m^*(A)=m^*\bigl((A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^c)\bigr)\le m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c)$$
恒成立，所以实际只需验证反向不等式
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c).$$
条件关于 $E$ 与 $E^c$ 对称，故 $E$ 可测当且仅当 $E^c$ 可测。

设 $m^*(E)=0$。对任意 $A$，由单调性 $m^*(A\cap E)\le m^*(E)=0$，故 $m^*(A\cap E)=0$；又 $A\cap E^c\subseteq A$，故 $m^*(A\cap E^c)\le m^*(A)$。于是
$$m^*(A)\le m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c)\le0+m^*(A),$$
两端都等于 $m^*(A)$，故等号成立，$E$ 可测且 $m(E)=0$。关键是证明中只用了 $m^*(E)=0$，没有预设 $E$ 可测。推论：零测集的任何子集也可测，且外测度仍为 $0$，这就是 Lebesgue 测度的完备性。

补集：第 1 步已指出条件对称，故可测集族 $\mathcal M$ 对补封闭；又 $m^*(\varnothing)=0$，由第 2 步 $\varnothing\in\mathcal M$，从而 $\mathbb R=\varnothing^c\in\mathcal M$。
有限并：设 $E,F\in\mathcal M$，$A$ 任意。对 $E$ 用条件，再对 $F$ 用测试集 $A\cap E^c$：
$$m^*(A)=m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c),$$
$$m^*(A\cap E^c)=m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F)+m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F^c).$$
把第二式代入第一式，注意 $(A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^c\cap F)=A\cap(E\cup F)$ 且 $A\cap E^c\cap F^c=A\cap(E\cup F)^c$，得
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A)={}&m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F)\\&+m^*(A\cap(E\cup F)^c).\end{aligned}$$
由次可加性，前两项之和不小于 $m^*(A\cap(E\cup F))$，故
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap(E\cup F))+m^*(A\cap(E\cup F)^c).$$
结合自动成立的 $\le$ 方向，$E\cup F\in\mathcal M$。对个数归纳即得有限并封闭。

设 $E_n\in\mathcal M$。先化为不交：令 $F_1=E_1$，$F_n=E_n\setminus\bigcup_{k<n}E_k$（$n\ge2$）。由有限并与补的封闭性，$F_n\in\mathcal M$，且 $F_n$ 两两不交、$\bigcup_n F_n=\bigcup_n E_n$。
对不交的 $F_1,\dots,F_N\in\mathcal M$ 归纳证明：对任意 $A$，
$$m^*\Bigl(A\cap\bigcup_{n=1}^{N}F_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n).$$
$N=1$ 时两边都是 $m^*(A\cap F_1)$。设对 $N-1$ 成立，记 $S_{N-1}=\bigcup_{n<N}F_n$、$S_N=S_{N-1}\cup F_N$。因 $F_N$ 可测，以 $A\cap S_N$ 为测试集：
$$m^*(A\cap S_N)=m^*(A\cap S_{N-1})+m^*(A\cap F_N),$$
这里用了 $S_N\cap F_N=F_N$ 与 $S_N\cap F_N^c=S_{N-1}$。代入归纳假设即得。
再令 $S=\bigcup_n F_n$。对任意 $A$ 与 $N$，对测试集 $A$ 依次使用 $F_1,\dots,F_N$ 的条件，得
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A)={}&\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n)+m^*(A\cap S_N^c)\\&\ge\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n)+m^*(A\cap S^c),\end{aligned}$$
因为 $S^c\subseteq S_N^c$。令 $N\to\infty$，并用次可加性 $m^*(A\cap S)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^*(A\cap F_n)$，得
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap S)+m^*(A\cap S^c).$$
反向不等式自动成立，故 $S\in\mathcal M$；取 $A=S$ 得 $m(S)=\sum_n m(F_n)$。于是 $\mathcal M$ 对可数并封闭，且 $m=m^*|_{\mathcal M}$ 可数可加。

证明任意区间 $I$ 可测。设 $A\subseteq\mathbb R$、$\varepsilon>0$，取开区间覆盖 $\{J_k\}$ 使 $A\subseteq\bigcup_k J_k$ 且 $\sum_k|J_k|<m^*(A)+\varepsilon/2$。对每个区间 $J_k$，$J_k\cap I$ 是区间，$J_k\cap I^c$ 是至多两个区间之并，且
$$|J_k|=|J_k\cap I|+|J_k\cap I^c|$$
（端点是否重合不影响长度）。把这两族区间分别稍微放大为开区间，使总长度增加不超过 $\varepsilon/2$。则 $\{J_k\cap I\}$ 覆盖 $A\cap I$，$\{J_k\cap I^c\}$ 覆盖 $A\cap I^c$，故
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A\cap I)+m^*(A\cap I^c)&\le\sum_k|J_k|+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\\&<m^*(A)+\varepsilon.\end{aligned}$$
令 $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ 得 $m^*(A\cap I)+m^*(A\cap I^c)\le m^*(A)$，故 $I$ 可测。特别地 $[a,b]$ 可测且 $m([a,b])=b-a$。开集是至多可数个两两不交开区间之并，故开集可测；$\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$ 由开集生成，而 $\mathcal M$ 是 σ 代数，故 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)\subseteq\mathcal M$。

由第 3–5 步，$\mathcal M$ 含 $\varnothing$ 与 $\mathbb R$，对补与可数并封闭，故是 σ 代数；$m=m^*|_{\mathcal M}$ 满足 $m(\varnothing)=0$ 与可数可加性，因而是测度。由第 2 步它完备；由外测度节点第 4 步与本节第 5 步，$m([a,b])=m((a,b))=b-a$，且一切 Borel 集可测。
康托尔集说明「不可数」不蕴含「正测度」。从 $[0,1]$ 起，第 $k$ 步挖去 $2^{k-1}$ 个长为 $3^{-k}$ 的开区间，挖去的总长度为
$$\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{k-1}3^{-k}&=\frac13\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^k\\&=\frac{1/3}{1-2/3}=1.\end{aligned}$$
设 $U$ 为挖去的开区间之并，则 $U$ 可测，且 $C=[0,1]\setminus U$ 也可测；于是 $m(C)=1-1=0$（这里 $m([0,1])=1<+\infty$，可以相减）。而 $C$ 中点的三进制展开只含数字 $0,2$，故 $C$ 与 $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ 等势，不可数。
并非所有集合都可测：外测度节点构造的维塔利集 $V$ 不满足 Carathéodory 条件。若 $V$ 可测，由 $m^*$ 的平移不变性（Carathéodory 条件在平移下不变），其平移 $V_q=V+q$（$q\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$）都可测、测度相同、两两不交且含于 $[-1,2]$。可数可加性给出 $m(\bigcup_q V_q)=\sum_q m(V_q)$。若 $m(V)=0$，并的测度为 $0$，但 $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_q V_q$；若 $m(V)>0$，则 $\sum_q m(V_q)=+\infty$，而并含于 $[-1,2]$，测度不超过 $3$；两种情形都矛盾。故 $V$ 不可测。其构造依赖选择公理；在 ZFC 中不可测集确实存在。
derivationEn:
A set $E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is called Lebesgue measurable if for every $A\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$m^*(A)=m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c).$$
The test set $A$ must be arbitrary; checking only $A=\mathbb R$ is insufficient. By subadditivity of outer measure,
$$m^*(A)=m^*\bigl((A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^c)\bigr)\le m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c)$$
always holds, so in practice only the reverse inequality
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c)$$
has to be verified. The condition is symmetric in $E$ and $E^c$, so $E$ is measurable iff $E^c$ is.

Suppose $m^*(E)=0$. For any $A$, monotonicity gives $m^*(A\cap E)\le m^*(E)=0$, hence $m^*(A\cap E)=0$; and $A\cap E^c\subseteq A$ gives $m^*(A\cap E^c)\le m^*(A)$. Therefore
$$m^*(A)\le m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c)\le0+m^*(A),$$
so equality holds and $E$ is measurable with $m(E)=0$. The point is that only $m^*(E)=0$ was used; $E$ was not assumed measurable. Corollary: every subset of a null set is measurable with outer measure $0$, which is the completeness of Lebesgue measure.

Complements: Step 1 shows the condition is symmetric, so the family $\mathcal M$ of measurable sets is closed under complements; since $m^*(\varnothing)=0$, Step 2 gives $\varnothing\in\mathcal M$, hence $\mathbb R=\varnothing^c\in\mathcal M$.
Finite unions: let $E,F\in\mathcal M$ and let $A$ be arbitrary. Apply the condition to $E$, then to $F$ with test set $A\cap E^c$:
$$m^*(A)=m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c),$$
$$m^*(A\cap E^c)=m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F)+m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F^c).$$
Substituting the second identity into the first and noting $(A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^c\cap F)=A\cap(E\cup F)$ and $A\cap E^c\cap F^c=A\cap(E\cup F)^c$, we get
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A)={}&m^*(A\cap E)+m^*(A\cap E^c\cap F)\\&+m^*(A\cap(E\cup F)^c).\end{aligned}$$
By subadditivity the first two terms sum to at least $m^*(A\cap(E\cup F))$, hence
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap(E\cup F))+m^*(A\cap(E\cup F)^c).$$
Together with the automatic reverse inequality, $E\cup F\in\mathcal M$. Induction gives closure under finite unions.

Let $E_n\in\mathcal M$. First make them disjoint: set $F_1=E_1$ and $F_n=E_n\setminus\bigcup_{k<n}E_k$ for $n\ge2$. By closure under finite unions and complements, $F_n\in\mathcal M$; the $F_n$ are pairwise disjoint and $\bigcup_n F_n=\bigcup_n E_n$.
For pairwise disjoint $F_1,\dots,F_N\in\mathcal M$ we prove by induction that for every $A$,
$$m^*\Bigl(A\cap\bigcup_{n=1}^{N}F_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n).$$
For $N=1$ both sides equal $m^*(A\cap F_1)$. Assume the statement for $N-1$ and write $S_{N-1}=\bigcup_{n<N}F_n$, $S_N=S_{N-1}\cup F_N$. Since $F_N$ is measurable, applying the condition with test set $A\cap S_N$ gives
$$m^*(A\cap S_N)=m^*(A\cap S_{N-1})+m^*(A\cap F_N),$$
where we used $S_N\cap F_N=F_N$ and $S_N\cap F_N^c=S_{N-1}$. Substituting the induction hypothesis proves the claim.
Now let $S=\bigcup_n F_n$. For every $A$ and $N$, applying the condition successively to $F_1,\dots,F_N$ with test set $A$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A)={}&\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n)+m^*(A\cap S_N^c)\\&\ge\sum_{n=1}^{N}m^*(A\cap F_n)+m^*(A\cap S^c),\end{aligned}$$
because $S^c\subseteq S_N^c$. Letting $N\to\infty$ and using subadditivity $m^*(A\cap S)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^*(A\cap F_n)$ yields
$$m^*(A)\ge m^*(A\cap S)+m^*(A\cap S^c).$$
The reverse inequality is automatic, so $S\in\mathcal M$; taking $A=S$ gives $m(S)=\sum_n m(F_n)$. Thus $\mathcal M$ is closed under countable unions and $m=m^*|_{\mathcal M}$ is countably additive.

Let us show that every interval $I$ is measurable. Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and choose an open-interval cover $\{J_k\}$ of $A$ with $\sum_k|J_k|<m^*(A)+\varepsilon/2$. For each interval $J_k$, the set $J_k\cap I$ is an interval and $J_k\cap I^c$ is the union of at most two intervals, with
$$|J_k|=|J_k\cap I|+|J_k\cap I^c|$$
(whether endpoints overlap is irrelevant for length). Enlarge the intervals in these two families slightly to open intervals, increasing the total length by at most $\varepsilon/2$. Then $\{J_k\cap I\}$ covers $A\cap I$ and $\{J_k\cap I^c\}$ covers $A\cap I^c$, so
$$\begin{aligned}m^*(A\cap I)+m^*(A\cap I^c)&\le\sum_k|J_k|+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\\&<m^*(A)+\varepsilon.\end{aligned}$$
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives $m^*(A\cap I)+m^*(A\cap I^c)\le m^*(A)$, so $I$ is measurable. In particular $[a,b]$ is measurable and $m([a,b])=b-a$. Every open set is a countable union of pairwise disjoint open intervals, hence measurable; $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$ is generated by open sets and $\mathcal M$ is a $\sigma$-algebra, so $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)\subseteq\mathcal M$.

By Steps 3–5, $\mathcal M$ contains $\varnothing$ and $\mathbb R$ and is closed under complements and countable unions, so it is a $\sigma$-algebra; $m=m^*|_{\mathcal M}$ satisfies $m(\varnothing)=0$ and countable additivity, hence is a measure. Step 2 shows that it is complete, and the outer-measure Step 4 together with Step 5 of this node gives $m([a,b])=m((a,b))=b-a$ and the measurability of all Borel sets.
The Cantor set shows that uncountability does not imply positive measure. Starting from $[0,1]$, at stage $k$ one removes $2^{k-1}$ open intervals of length $3^{-k}$; their total length is
$$\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{k-1}3^{-k}&=\frac13\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^k\\&=\frac{1/3}{1-2/3}=1.\end{aligned}$$
Let $U$ be the union of the removed open intervals; then $U$ is measurable and so is $C=[0,1]\setminus U$; therefore $m(C)=1-1=0$ (here $m([0,1])=1<+\infty$, so subtraction is legitimate). Points of $C$ have ternary expansions using only the digits $0$ and $2$, so $C$ is in bijection with $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ and is uncountable.
Not every set is measurable: the Vitali set $V$ from the outer-measure node fails Carathéodory's condition. If $V$ were measurable, then by translation invariance of $m^*$ (the Carathéodory condition is invariant under translation) its translates $V_q=V+q$, $q\in\mathbb Q\cap[-1,1]$, would be measurable, of equal measure, pairwise disjoint and contained in $[-1,2]$. Countable additivity would give $m(\bigcup_q V_q)=\sum_q m(V_q)$. If $m(V)=0$ the union would be null, contradicting $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_q V_q$; if $m(V)>0$ the sum would be $+\infty$, while the union lies in $[-1,2]$ and has measure at most $3$. Both cases are impossible, so $V$ is not measurable. Its construction uses the axiom of choice; in ZFC nonmeasurable sets do exist.

formulas.note: 卡拉西奥多里条件：对任意测试集 $A$ 成立；结合次可加性只需验证 $\ge$ 方向。不能只对 $A=\mathbb{R}$ 验证。
formulas.noteEn: Carathéodory's condition: it must hold for every test set $A$; by subadditivity only the inequality $\ge$ needs checking, and $A=\mathbb{R}$ alone is insufficient.

formulas.note: 勒贝格测度的 σ 可加性：这是它成为「测度」的核心性质，有限可加是其特例。
formulas.noteEn: Countable additivity of Lebesgue measure, the core property making it a measure; finite additivity is a special case.

formulas.note: 完备性：零测集的任何子集仍可测且零测。
formulas.noteEn: Completeness: every subset of a null set is measurable and null.

formulas.note: 区间的勒贝格测度等于其长度（开闭不限）。
formulas.noteEn: The measure of an interval equals its length, open or closed alike.

formulas.note: 康托尔集：挖去的总长度为 $1$，剩下不可数的零测集。
formulas.noteEn: The Cantor set: the removed pieces have total length 1, leaving an uncountable null set.

properties: 可测集类 $\mathcal{M}$ 是 σ 代数，包含所有开集、闭集与区间，因此一切 Borel 集都可测。
勒贝格测度在 $\mathcal{M}$ 上可数可加，且 $m(\varnothing)=0$；单调性与有限可加性是它的推论。
$m$ 是完备的：若 $m(E)=0$，则 $E$ 的任何子集都可测且测度为 $0$。
平移不变：$E\in\mathcal{M}\iff E+t\in\mathcal{M}$，且 $m(E+t)=m(E)$。
区间测度等于长度，可数集零测；但不可数集也可以零测（康托尔集），所以「不可数 $\Rightarrow$ 测度为正」是错的。
propertiesEn: The measurable sets form a σ-algebra containing all open sets, closed sets and intervals; hence every Borel set is measurable.
Lebesgue measure is countably additive on $\mathcal{M}$ with $m(\varnothing)=0$; monotonicity and finite additivity follow.
$m$ is complete: every subset of a set of measure zero is measurable and has measure zero.
Translation invariance: $E$ is measurable iff $E+t$ is, and $m(E+t)=m(E)$.
Intervals get their length and countable sets are null, yet an uncountable set can also be null (the Cantor set), so uncountability does not force positive measure.

examples.problem: 从 $[0,1]$ 出发，每一步把每个剩余区间中间的 $1/3$ 开区间挖去，得到康托尔集 $C$。求 $m(C)$，并说明 $C$ 不可数。
examples.solution: 第 $k$ 步挖去的开区间共有 $2^{k-1}$ 个，每个长为 $3^{-k}$，故挖去的总长度为 $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{k-1}3^{-k}=\frac13\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^{k-1}=\frac{1/3}{1-2/3}=1.$$ 挖去的集合是可数个开区间之并，可测；因此 $$m(C)=m([0,1])-1=1-1=0.$$ 不可数性：$C$ 中的点都可以写成只含数字 $0$ 与 $2$ 的三进制小数；把这种展开中的每个 $2$ 换成 $1$，就得到一串 $0$-$1$ 序列，而每个二进制展开都以这种方式出现，于是从 $C$ 到 $[0,1]$ 存在满射；又 $C\subseteq[0,1]$，故 $C$ 与 $[0,1]$ 等势，特别地不可数。结论：不可数集的勒贝格测度可以为 $0$。

examples.problem: 证明：若 $m^{*}(E)=0$，则 $E$ 可测（即任何零测集的子集都可测，这解释了勒贝格测度的完备性）。
examples.solution: 对任意 $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$：由单调性 $m^{*}(A\cap E)\le m^{*}(E)=0$，故 $m^{*}(A\cap E)=0$；又 $m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})\le m^{*}(A)$。另一方面 $A\subseteq(A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^{c})$，由次可加性 $$m^{*}(A)\le m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})=m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})\le m^{*}(A).$$ 于是等号成立，即 $m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})$，卡拉西奥多里条件满足，$E$ 可测且 $m(E)=0$。注意这里 $E$ 事先不必可测，只要外测度为 $0$。

expression.text: E 可测 ⟺ 对任意 A ⊆ ℝ：m*(A) = m*(A∩E) + m*(A∩Eᶜ)
expression.note: 卡拉西奥多里条件中的 A 可以是任何集合，包括病态集合；这正是「可测」一词的精确含义。
expression.noteEn: The test set A in Carathéodory's condition may be any set, including pathological ones; this is the precise meaning of 'measurable'.

measure-space.definition:
σ 代数确定了「可以测量的集合」，接下来给这些集合赋「大小」。设 $X$ 是非空集合，$\mathcal{F}$ 是 $X$ 上的 σ 代数。**测度**是函数 $\mu:\mathcal{F}\to[0,+\infty]$，满足：(i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$；(ii) **可数可加性**：若 $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{F}$ 两两不交，则 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 三元组 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 称为**测度空间**，$\mathcal{F}$ 中的集合称为**可测集**。非负性与 $\mu(\varnothing)=0$ 让测度像「长度」「面积」「概率」一样自然。

从可数可加性出发，可以推出一整套常用性质：**单调性** $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$（且当 $\mu(A)<\infty$ 时 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$）；**可数次可加性** $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n \mu(A_n)$（不要求不交）；以及**上下连续性**：若 $\{A_n\}$ 递增（$A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$），则 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n);$$ 若 $\{A_n\}$ 递减，则**必须附加条件 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$**，才有 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 这个条件不能省：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取勒贝格测度与 $A_n=[n,\infty)$，交集为 $\varnothing$、测度为 $0$，而 $\lim m(A_n)=+\infty$，等式失效的根源正是 $m(A_1)=\infty$。

概率论是测度论的特例：概率空间 $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ 就是满足 $P(\Omega)=1$ 的测度空间，「事件」是 $\mathcal{F}$ 中的集合，「事件的概率」是 $\mu$；计数测度 $\mu(A)=|A|$ 则给出另一类离散模型。若 $\mu(X)<\infty$ 称 $\mu$ 为**有限测度**；若 $X$ 可被可数多个有限测度集覆盖，称 $\mu$ 为 **σ 有限**。勒贝格测度不是有限测度，但它在每个区间上有限，所以是 σ 有限的。

抽象测度空间的价值在于「一次证明、多处使用」：勒贝格积分、概率、计数测度共享同一套推理，后面所有的积分与收敛定理都只需在任意测度空间中证明一遍。
measure-space.definitionEn:
A σ-algebra tells us which sets may be measured; a measure tells us how big they are. Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $\mathcal{F}$ a σ-algebra on $X$. A **measure** is a function $\mu:\mathcal{F}\to[0,+\infty]$ such that (i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$; (ii) **countable additivity**: for pairwise disjoint $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{F}$, $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ The triple $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ is a **measure space** and the members of $\mathcal{F}$ are the **measurable sets**. Nonnegativity and $\mu(\varnothing)=0$ make $\mu$ behave like length, area or probability.

From countable additivity one derives the working properties: **monotonicity** $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$ (and $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$ when $\mu(A)<\infty$); **countable subadditivity** $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$ with no disjointness needed; and **continuity**: for an increasing sequence $A_n\uparrow A$, $$\mu(A)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n),$$ while for a decreasing sequence $A_n\downarrow A$ one needs the extra hypothesis $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ to conclude the same. The hypothesis cannot be dropped: with Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $A_n=[n,\infty)$, the intersection is empty of measure $0$ while $\lim m(A_n)=+\infty$, precisely because $m(A_1)=\infty$.

Probability theory is a special case: a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ is a measure space with $P(\Omega)=1$, events are the sets of $\mathcal{F}$, and counting measure $\mu(A)=|A|$ gives a discrete model. A measure is **finite** if $\mu(X)<\infty$, and **σ-finite** if $X$ can be covered by countably many sets of finite measure. Lebesgue measure is not finite but is σ-finite, being finite on every interval.

The value of the abstract setting is 'prove once, use everywhere': Lebesgue integration, probability and counting share one body of reasoning, and all later integration and convergence theorems are proved once in an arbitrary measure space.
derivation:
设 $X\ne\varnothing$，$\mathcal F$ 是 $X$ 上的 σ 代数。函数 $\mu:\mathcal F\to[0,+\infty]$ 称为测度，若 (i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$；(ii) 对两两不交的 $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal F$，
$$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$
三元组 $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ 称测度空间。$\mu$ 取值于 $[0,+\infty]$ 而非 $[0,+\infty)$，因为长度与计数都允许为无穷；概率虽有限，也纳入同一框架。可数可加性中的级数在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中收敛（可能为 $+\infty$），不涉及条件收敛问题。非负性已由值域保证。

设 $A\subseteq B$，$A,B\in\mathcal F$。则 $B=A\cup(B\setminus A)$ 且 $A\cap(B\setminus A)=\varnothing$，而 $B\setminus A\in\mathcal F$。由可数可加性（其余项取空集）得
$$\mu(B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B\setminus A)\ge\mu(A).$$
若 $\mu(A)<+\infty$，则由同一等式可解出 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$（当 $\mu(B)=+\infty$ 时右端为 $+\infty$，等式仍成立）。若没有 $\mu(A)<+\infty$，减法无意义：例如 $A=B=\mathbb R$ 时 $\mu(B)-\mu(A)=+\infty-\infty$ 未定义，不能断言为 $0$。

设 $A_n\in\mathcal F$，不要求两两不交。令 $B_1=A_1$，$B_n=A_n\setminus\bigcup_{k<n}A_k$。则 $B_n\in\mathcal F$，两两不交，且 $\bigcup_n B_n=\bigcup_n A_n$。由可数可加性与单调性 $B_n\subseteq A_n$，
$$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_n A_n\Bigr)=\sum_n\mu(B_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n).$$
不等式在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中成立，不要求 $\mu(A_n)<+\infty$。它比可数可加性弱，但对估计并的大小已经够用。

设 $A_n\uparrow A$，即 $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$ 且 $A=\bigcup_n A_n$。令 $B_1=A_1$，$B_n=A_n\setminus A_{n-1}$（$n\ge2$）。则 $B_n$ 两两不交，$\bigcup_{n\le N}B_n=A_N$，$\bigcup_n B_n=A$。由可数可加性，
$$\begin{aligned}\mu(A)&=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(B_n)\\&=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(B_n)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mu(A_N).\end{aligned}$$
这里没有有限性假设；若 $\mu(A)=+\infty$，部分和单调递增趋于 $+\infty$，等式仍在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中成立。

设 $A_n\downarrow A$ 且 $\mu(A_1)<+\infty$。令 $C_n=A_1\setminus A_n$。则 $C_n\uparrow A_1\setminus A$，由第 4 步
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(C_n)=\mu(A_1\setminus A).$$
由 $A_n\subseteq A_1$ 与 $\mu(A_n)\le\mu(A_1)<+\infty$，第 2 步给出 $\mu(C_n)=\mu(A_1)-\mu(A_n)$ 与 $\mu(A_1\setminus A)=\mu(A_1)-\mu(A)$。代入得 $\mu(A_1)-\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A_1)-\mu(A)$。因 $\mu(A_1)<+\infty$，两边减去 $\mu(A_1)$ 得 $\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A)$。更一般地，只需某个 $\mu(A_k)<+\infty$：此时对尾列 $A_k,A_{k+1},\dots$ 应用上述论证即可。
条件不能省：取 $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,m)$ 与 $A_n=[n,+\infty)$。则 $A_n\downarrow\varnothing$，但 $m(A_n)=+\infty$ 对所有 $n$，故 $\lim_nm(A_n)=+\infty\ne0=m(\varnothing)$；根源是 $m(A_1)=+\infty$。

可数可加严格强于有限可加。反例：在 $(\mathbb N,2^{\mathbb N})$ 上令 $\mu(A)=0$（$A$ 有限）、$\mu(A)=1$（$A$ 余有限）。则 $\mu(\varnothing)=0$，且对不交的 $A,B$ 逐情形验证 $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B)$：两个有限集之并有限；一个有限、一个余有限时并为余有限；两个余有限集不可能不交。但取 $A_n=\{n\}$，则 $\mu(A_n)=0$ 而 $\mu(\mathbb N)=1$，故
$$1=\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_n A_n\Bigr)\ne\sum_n\mu(A_n)=0,$$
所以 $\mu$ 只是有限可加，不是测度。
典型例子：概率测度满足 $\mu(X)=1$，是有限测度；Lebesgue 测度 $m(\mathbb R)=+\infty$，但 $m([-n,n])=2n<+\infty$，故 σ 有限而非有限；$\mathbb N$ 上的计数测度由单点集覆盖，σ 有限而非有限；同样的计数测度在 $\mathbb R$ 上不是 σ 有限的，因为可数多个有限集之并仍可数，盖不住 $\mathbb R$。
derivationEn:
Let $X\ne\varnothing$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a $\sigma$-algebra on $X$. A function $\mu:\mathcal F\to[0,+\infty]$ is a measure if (i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$; (ii) for pairwise disjoint $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal F$,
$$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$
The triple $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ is a measure space. The values lie in $[0,+\infty]$ rather than $[0,+\infty)$ because length and counting measure may be infinite, while probability, though finite, fits the same framework; the series in countable additivity converges in $[0,+\infty]$ (possibly to $+\infty$), so no conditional convergence issue arises. Nonnegativity is built into the codomain.

Let $A\subseteq B$ with $A,B\in\mathcal F$. Then $B=A\cup(B\setminus A)$ with $A\cap(B\setminus A)=\varnothing$, and $B\setminus A\in\mathcal F$. Countable additivity (with the remaining terms empty) gives
$$\mu(B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B\setminus A)\ge\mu(A).$$
If $\mu(A)<+\infty$, the same identity yields $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$ (when $\mu(B)=+\infty$ the right side is $+\infty$ and the identity still holds). Without $\mu(A)<+\infty$ subtraction is meaningless: for $A=B=\mathbb R$, $\mu(B)-\mu(A)=+\infty-\infty$ is undefined, not $0$.

Let $A_n\in\mathcal F$, not necessarily disjoint. Put $B_1=A_1$ and $B_n=A_n\setminus\bigcup_{k<n}A_k$. Then $B_n\in\mathcal F$, the $B_n$ are pairwise disjoint, and $\bigcup_n B_n=\bigcup_n A_n$. Countable additivity and monotonicity $B_n\subseteq A_n$ give
$$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_n A_n\Bigr)=\sum_n\mu(B_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n).$$
The inequality holds in $[0,+\infty]$ and does not require $\mu(A_n)<+\infty$. It is weaker than countable additivity but sufficient for estimating the size of a union.

Let $A_n\uparrow A$, i.e. $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$ and $A=\bigcup_n A_n$. Put $B_1=A_1$ and $B_n=A_n\setminus A_{n-1}$ for $n\ge2$. Then the $B_n$ are pairwise disjoint, $\bigcup_{n\le N}B_n=A_N$ and $\bigcup_n B_n=A$. Countable additivity gives
$$\begin{aligned}\mu(A)&=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(B_n)\\&=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(B_n)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mu(A_N).\end{aligned}$$
No finiteness assumption is used; if $\mu(A)=+\infty$, the partial sums increase to $+\infty$ and the identity still holds in $[0,+\infty]$.

Let $A_n\downarrow A$ and $\mu(A_1)<+\infty$. Put $C_n=A_1\setminus A_n$. Then $C_n\uparrow A_1\setminus A$, and Step 4 gives
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(C_n)=\mu(A_1\setminus A).$$
Since $A_n\subseteq A_1$ and $\mu(A_n)\le\mu(A_1)<+\infty$, Step 2 gives $\mu(C_n)=\mu(A_1)-\mu(A_n)$ and $\mu(A_1\setminus A)=\mu(A_1)-\mu(A)$. Substituting yields $\mu(A_1)-\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A_1)-\mu(A)$. Because $\mu(A_1)<+\infty$, subtracting $\mu(A_1)$ from both sides gives $\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A)$. More generally, it suffices that $\mu(A_k)<+\infty$ for some $k$: apply the same argument to the tail sequence $A_k,A_{k+1},\dots$.
The hypothesis cannot be dropped: take $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,m)$ and $A_n=[n,+\infty)$. Then $A_n\downarrow\varnothing$, but $m(A_n)=+\infty$ for every $n$, so $\lim_nm(A_n)=+\infty\ne0=m(\varnothing)$; the source is $m(A_1)=+\infty$.

Countable additivity is strictly stronger than finite additivity. Counterexample: on $(\mathbb N,2^{\mathbb N})$ let $\mu(A)=0$ if $A$ is finite and $\mu(A)=1$ if $A$ is cofinite. Then $\mu(\varnothing)=0$, and for disjoint $A,B$ one checks $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B)$ case by case: the union of two finite sets is finite; a finite set and a cofinite set have cofinite union; two cofinite sets cannot be disjoint. But for $A_n=\{n\}$, $\mu(A_n)=0$ while $\mu(\mathbb N)=1$, so
$$1=\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_n A_n\Bigr)\ne\sum_n\mu(A_n)=0,$$
and $\mu$ is only finitely additive, not a measure.
Typical examples: a probability measure has $\mu(X)=1$ and is finite; Lebesgue measure has $m(\mathbb R)=+\infty$ but $m([-n,n])=2n<+\infty$, so it is $\sigma$-finite but not finite; counting measure on $\mathbb N$ is $\sigma$-finite but not finite, covered by the singletons; the same counting measure on $\mathbb R$ is not $\sigma$-finite, since a countable union of finite sets is countable and cannot cover $\mathbb R$.

formulas.note: 可数可加性：测度公理的核心，要求集列两两不交。
formulas.noteEn: Countable additivity, the heart of the axioms, required for pairwise disjoint sets.

formulas.note: 单调性；若再假设 $\mu(A)<\infty$，则 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$，有限性条件不可省。
formulas.noteEn: Monotonicity; if moreover $\mu(A)<\infty$, then $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$, and the finiteness hypothesis cannot be dropped.

formulas.note: 可数次可加性：不要求集列不交，是最常用的估计工具。
formulas.noteEn: Countable subadditivity, valid without disjointness and the most used estimate.

formulas.note: 递增连续性（下连续），不需要任何有限性假设。
formulas.noteEn: Continuity from below for increasing sequences, requiring no finiteness assumption.

formulas.note: 递减连续性（上连续）：条件 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ 不可省，反例 $A_n=[n,\infty)$。
formulas.noteEn: Continuity from above: the hypothesis $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ is indispensable, with $A_n=[n,\infty)$ as the standard counterexample.

properties: 可数可加蕴含有限可加，反之不成立：σ 代数上确实存在只有限可加而不可数可加的集函数。
单调性 $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$；当 $\mu(A)<\infty$ 时还有 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$。
可数次可加：$\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$，不需要集列两两不交。
递增连续无条件成立；递减连续需要 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$，否则 $A_n=[n,\infty)$ 给出反例（交集测度为 $0$，极限为 $+\infty$）。
常见实例：计数测度（σ 有限但非有限）、勒贝格测度（σ 有限但非有限）、概率测度（$\mu(X)=1$，有限）。
propertiesEn: Countable additivity implies finite additivity, but not conversely: finitely additive yet not countably additive set functions do exist on σ-algebras.
Monotone: $A\subseteq B$ implies $\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$, and $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$ when $\mu(A)<\infty$.
Countably subadditive: $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$, with no disjointness required.

Continuity from below holds unconditionally, while continuity from above needs $\mu(A_1)<\infty$; otherwise $A_n=[n,\infty)$ gives a counterexample (empty intersection of measure 0 versus limit $+\infty$).
Typical examples: counting measure (σ-finite but not finite), Lebesgue measure (σ-finite but not finite) and probability measures ($\mu(X)=1$, finite).

examples.problem: 在 $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ 中取 $A_n=[n,+\infty)$，验证 $\{A_n\}$ 递减，并说明为什么 $\lim m(A_n)\ne m\bigl(\bigcap_n A_n\bigr)$。
examples.solution: 显然 $A_{n+1}\subseteq A_n$，且 $\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n=\varnothing$，故 $m(\bigcap_n A_n)=0$。但 $m(A_n)=+\infty$（$[n,+\infty)$ 的外测度为无穷），所以 $\lim_{n}m(A_n)=+\infty$，等式失效。原因正是递减连续性的条件 $m(A_1)<\infty$ 被违反：这里 $m(A_1)=+\infty$。对照递增情形 $B_n=[0,n]$：$m(B_n)=n\to+\infty=m(\bigcup_n B_n)$，无条件成立。

examples.problem: 设 $\mu$ 是 σ 代数 $\mathcal{F}$ 上的集函数，$\mu(\varnothing)=0$，有限可加（两两不交的有限并列可加），且对递增列连续：$A_n\uparrow A\Rightarrow\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A)$。证明 $\mu$ 可数可加。
examples.solution: 设 $\{A_n\}$ 两两不交，令 $S_N=\bigcup_{n\le N}A_n$，则 $S_N\uparrow A=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n$。由有限可加性，$\mu(S_N)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(A_n)$。令 $N\to\infty$ 并用递增连续性： $$\mu(A)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mu(S_N)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(A_n)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 故可数可加成立，且过程中不需要任何有限性假设。这说明「$\mu(\varnothing)=0$ + 有限可加 + 递增连续」是测度公理的等价形式。

expression.text: (X, ℱ, μ)：X 为非空集合，ℱ 为 σ 代数，μ 为非负可数可加的测度
expression.note: 测度公理：μ(∅)=0 与两两不交集上的可数可加性；概率测度还额外要求 μ(X)=1。
expression.noteEn: The axioms are μ(∅)=0 plus countable additivity on disjoint sets; a probability measure additionally requires μ(X)=1.

measurable-functions.definition:
设 $(X,\mathcal{F})$ 与 $(Y,\mathcal{G})$ 是可测空间。函数 $f:X\to Y$ 称为**可测的**，如果对每个 $B\in\mathcal{G}$ 都有 $$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal{F}.$$ 当值域取实数轴 $\mathbb{R}$（配 Borel σ 代数）时，由于 Borel 集由射线 $(a,\infty)$ 生成，判定可测只需检查水平集：$f$ 可测 $\iff$ 对**任意实数 $a$**，$\{x:f(x)>a\}\in\mathcal{F}$。也可以等价地换成 $\ge$、$<$、$\le$ 中的任意一种，因为不同水平集之间只差可数次集合运算，例如 $\{f\ge a\}=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\{f>a-\frac1n\}$。等价地，用「区间」条件 $\{a<f<b\}$（对一切 $a<b$）也是**同样有效**的判据：实值函数下 $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$，两者可互相推出。只有当函数允许取 $\pm\infty$ 值时区间条件才不足——那时还须额外要求 $\{f=+\infty\}$、$\{f=-\infty\}$ 可测。

与连续函数的关系：连续函数可测（只要 σ 代数相容，如 Borel σ 代数：连续函数把开集的原像拉回开集）。反过来不成立，而且差得很远。**狄利克雷函数** $D(x)=1$（$x\in\mathbb{Q}$）、$D(x)=0$（$x\notin\mathbb{Q}$）处处不连续，却是可测的：对每个 $a$，$\{D>a\}$ 只能是 $\varnothing$、$\mathbb{Q}$ 或 $\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ 或 $\mathbb{R}$，都是可测集。它甚至不是黎曼可积的，但由于 $\mathbb{Q}$ 是零测集，它在 $[0,1]$ 上的勒贝格积分等于 $0$——这是勒贝格理论威力的第一个预告。

可测函数构成一个向量空间：若 $f,g$ 可测，则 $f+g$、$f-g$、$cf$、$fg$、$\max(f,g)$、$|f|$ 都可测；商 $f/g$ 也可测，只要**分母 $g$ 几乎处处不为零**（$\{g=0\}$ 是零测集），此时在 $g=0$ 处按任意约定（如取 $0$）补定义不影响可测性。更强的是：可测函数列的可数上确界、下确界、上极限、下极限以及逐点极限仍可测。这种对极限运算的封闭性使可测函数类比连续函数类好用得多。

引入可测函数的动机是积分：勒贝格积分先对简单函数定义，再对任意非负可测函数用单调递增的简单函数列的积分取极限——这正是下一节的主题。
measurable-functions.definitionEn:
Let $(X,\mathcal{F})$ and $(Y,\mathcal{G})$ be measurable spaces. A function $f:X\to Y$ is **measurable** if $$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal{F}\qquad\text{for every }B\in\mathcal{G}.$$ For real-valued functions (with the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$), since Borel sets are generated by the rays $(a,\infty)$, measurability reduces to checking level sets: $f$ is measurable if and only if $\{x:f(x)>a\}\in\mathcal{F}$ for **every real $a$**. One may equivalently use $\ge$, $<$ or $\le$, because the various level sets differ only by countably many set operations, e.g. $\{f\ge a\}=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\{f>a-\frac1n\}$. Equivalently the interval form $\{a<f<b\}$ for all $a<b$ is an equally valid criterion: for a real-valued $f$, $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$, so the two conditions imply each other. Only when $f$ may take the values $\pm\infty$ does the interval condition fall short, and then $\{f=+\infty\}$, $\{f=-\infty\}$ must be required separately.

As for continuity: a continuous function is measurable whenever the σ-algebras are compatible (as with the Borel σ-algebra, since preimages of open sets are open). The converse fails badly. The **Dirichlet function** $D=1$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ and $D=0$ off $\mathbb{Q}$ is nowhere continuous, yet measurable: for every $a$ the set $\{D>a\}$ is one of $\varnothing,\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R}$, all measurable. It is not Riemann integrable, but as $\mathbb{Q}$ is null its Lebesgue integral over $[0,1]$ equals $0$ — a first glimpse of the power of Lebesgue's theory.

Measurable functions form a vector space: if $f,g$ are measurable, so are $f+g$, $f-g$, $cf$, $fg$, $\max(f,g)$ and $|f|$; the quotient $f/g$ is measurable provided the denominator $g$ is nonzero almost everywhere (the null set $\{g=0\}$ may be defined arbitrarily, say as $0$). Even better, countable suprema, infima, limits superior and inferior, and pointwise limits of measurable functions are measurable. This closure under limiting operations makes the class far more useful than continuous functions.

The notion is motivated by integration: the Lebesgue integral is first defined for simple functions, then extended to nonnegative measurable functions as the limit of integrals of increasing simple approximations — the subject of the next section.
derivation:
设 $(X,\mathcal F)$ 与 $(Y,\mathcal G)$ 为可测空间。$f:X\to Y$ 称为可测，若对每个 $B\in\mathcal G$ 都有
$$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F.$$
取 $Y=\mathbb R$、$\mathcal G=\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$。令
$$\mathcal H=\{B\subseteq\mathbb R:f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F\}.$$
由原像保持并、交、补（$f^{-1}(B^c)=(f^{-1}(B))^c$，$f^{-1}(\bigcup B_i)=\bigcup f^{-1}(B_i)$），$\mathcal H$ 是 $\mathbb R$ 上的 σ 代数。射线 $(a,+\infty)$ 生成 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$，即 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)=\sigma(\{(a,+\infty):a\in\mathbb R\})$。因此若所有 $\{f>a\}=f^{-1}((a,+\infty))\in\mathcal F$，则 $\mathcal H$ 是含全部射线的 σ 代数，必含它们生成的 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$，故 $f$ 可测；反之由定义直接推出。结论：实值 $f$ 可测当且仅当对每个 $a\in\mathbb R$，$\{f>a\}\in\mathcal F$。

固定一种水平集即可。$(-\infty,a)$、$[a,+\infty)$、$(-\infty,a]$ 都是 Borel 集，故若 $f$ 可测，其原像也可测；也可直接验证：
$$\begin{aligned}\{f\ge a\}&=\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}\Bigl\{f>a-\frac1n\Bigr\},\\ \{f\le a\}&=\{f>a\}^c.\end{aligned}$$
因此 $\{f>a\}$ 对一切 $a$ 可测，等价于 $\{f\ge a\}$ 对一切 $a$ 可测（反向由 $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f\ge a+\frac1n\}$ 得到），也等价于 $\{f<a\}$ 或 $\{f\le a\}$ 的相应命题。
只需有理数：对实数 $a$，$\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q,\,q>a}\{f>q\}$（若 $f(x)>a$，取有理 $q\in(a,f(x))$），这是可数并。
区间判据：对实值 $f$，$\{a<f<b\}=\{f>a\}\cap\{f<b\}$，且 $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$，故区间判据等价。但若 $f$ 可取 $\pm\infty$，最后这个等式漏掉 $f=+\infty$ 的点，必须另外要求 $\{f=+\infty\}$、$\{f=-\infty\}$ 可测。

设 $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ 连续，$\mathcal F=\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$。对任意开集 $U$，$f^{-1}(U)$ 是开集，从而是 Borel 集；而 $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$ 由开集生成，由第 1 步的 $\mathcal H$ 论证，$f$ 可测。反向不成立：狄利克雷函数 $D=1_{\mathbb Q}$ 处处不连续。对任意 $a$，
$$\{D>a\}=\begin{cases}\mathbb R,&a<0,\\ \mathbb Q,&0\le a<1,\\ \varnothing,&a\ge1,\end{cases}$$
都是 Borel 集，故 $D$ 可测。处处不连续：任取 $x_0$，取有理数列 $q_n\to x_0$、无理数列 $r_n\to x_0$，则 $D(q_n)=1$、$D(r_n)=0$，两个子列极限不同。结论：连续是可测的充分而非必要条件。

设 $f,g$ 实值可测。和：对 $a\in\mathbb R$，
$$\{f+g>a\}=\bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q}\bigl(\{f>q\}\cap\{g>a-q\}\bigr).$$
若 $f(x)+g(x)>a$，取有理 $q$ 使 $f(x)>q>a-g(x)$，则 $x$ 属于右边；反之，若 $f(x)>q$ 且 $g(x)>a-q$，则 $f(x)+g(x)>a$，故右边包含于 $\{f+g>a\}$。可数并与有限交保持可测，故 $f+g$ 可测。
数乘：$c>0$ 时 $\{cf>a\}=\{f>a/c\}$，$c<0$ 时 $\{cf>a\}=\{f<a/c\}$，$c=0$ 时 $\{cf>a\}$ 是 $\varnothing$ 或 $\mathbb R$，故 $cf$ 可测。
乘积：$f^2$ 可测，因 $a\ge0$ 时 $\{f^2>a\}=\{f>\sqrt a\}\cup\{f<-\sqrt a\}$，$a<0$ 时为 $\mathbb R$；再用
$$fg=\frac14\bigl[(f+g)^2-(f-g)^2\bigr].$$
$\max(f,g)$ 可测，因 $\{\max(f,g)>a\}=\{f>a\}\cup\{g>a\}$；$|f|=\max(f,-f)$ 也可测。

设 $f_n$ 可测，取值于 $[-\infty,+\infty]$ 并配 Borel σ 代数。对 $a\in\mathbb R$，
$$\begin{aligned}\Bigl\{\sup_n f_n>a\Bigr\}&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f_n>a\},\\ \Bigl\{\inf_n f_n<a\Bigr\}&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f_n<a\}.\end{aligned}$$
第一式：上确界 $>a$ 当且仅当某个 $f_n>a$；第二式对偶。故 $\sup_n f_n$ 与 $\inf_n f_n$ 可测。再令
$$g_k=\sup_{n\ge k}f_n,\qquad h_k=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n,$$
它们可测，且
$$\limsup_{n}f_n=\inf_{k\ge1}g_k,\qquad \liminf_{n}f_n=\sup_{k\ge1}h_k$$
可测。若 $f_n$ 逐点收敛于 $f$，则 $f=\limsup f_n=\liminf f_n$ 可测。注意：若 $f_n$ 实值而 $\sup_n f_n$ 可能取 $+\infty$，应在扩展实数系中理解可测性；若上确界处处有限，则它就是实值可测函数。

商：设 $f,g$ 可测，$N=\{g=0\}$ 满足 $\mu(N)=0$。令 $	ilde g=g$ 于 $N^c$、$	ilde g=1$ 于 $N$。由于 $N=\{g=0\}$ 是 Borel 集的原像，故可测；$	ilde g$ 只在可测集 $N$ 上被改为常数，故 $	ilde g$ 可测，且 $	ilde g
e0$ 处处成立。又 $x\mapsto1/x$ 在 $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ 上连续，故 $1/	ilde g$ 可测，从而 $f/	ilde g$ 可测；它在 $N^c$ 上等于 $f/g$，故定义 $f/g=f/	ilde g$。条件「$g
e0$ a.e.」正是商作为 a.e. 定义的函数合法的原因；若 $g$ 在一个正测集上为零，则 $f/g$ 在该集合上逐点无定义，任意补值也不再代表原来的商。
几乎处处：命题「$f=g$ a.e.」指 $\{f
e g\}$ 包含在某个零测集中（当该集合可测时即 $\mu(\{f
e g\})=0$）。若 $f$ 可测、$g=f$ a.e.，且测度完备，则 $g$ 可测：对 Borel 集 $B$，$g^{-1}(B)$ 与 $f^{-1}(B)$ 只相差零测集 $\{f
e g\}$ 的一个子集，故可测。测度不完备时，需额外假设 $\{f
e g\}$ 包含在某个可测零测集中。典型例子：$D=1_{\mathbb Q}$ 满足 $D=0$ a.e.（$m(\mathbb Q)=0$），故 $D$ 可测且在 $[0,1]$ 上的 Lebesgue 积分为 $0$，尽管它处处不连续、非 Riemann 可积。a.e. 命题不控制零测集上的逐点取值。
derivationEn:
Let $(X,\mathcal F)$ and $(Y,\mathcal G)$ be measurable spaces. A function $f:X\to Y$ is measurable if for every $B\in\mathcal G$,
$$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F.$$
Take $Y=\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$, and set
$$\mathcal H=\{B\subseteq\mathbb R:f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F\}.$$
Since preimages preserve unions, intersections and complements ($f^{-1}(B^c)=(f^{-1}(B))^c$, $f^{-1}(\bigcup B_i)=\bigcup f^{-1}(B_i)$), $\mathcal H$ is a $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb R$. The rays $(a,+\infty)$ generate $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$, i.e. $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)=\sigma(\{(a,+\infty):a\in\mathbb R\})$. Hence if $\{f>a\}=f^{-1}((a,+\infty))\in\mathcal F$ for every $a$, then $\mathcal H$ is a $\sigma$-algebra containing all rays, so it contains the $\sigma$-algebra they generate, namely $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$; therefore $f$ is measurable. The converse follows directly from the definition. Conclusion: a real-valued $f$ is measurable iff $\{f>a\}\in\mathcal F$ for every $a\in\mathbb R$.

One fixed form of level set suffices. The sets $(-\infty,a)$, $[a,+\infty)$ and $(-\infty,a]$ are Borel, so if $f$ is measurable their preimages are measurable as well; directly,
$$\begin{aligned}\{f\ge a\}&=\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}\Bigl\{f>a-\frac1n\Bigr\},\\ \{f\le a\}&=\{f>a\}^c.\end{aligned}$$
Thus measurability of $\{f>a\}$ for all $a$ is equivalent to that of $\{f\ge a\}$ for all $a$ (the converse follows from $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f\ge a+\frac1n\}$), and likewise for $\{f<a\}$ or $\{f\le a\}$.
Rationals suffice: for real $a$,
$$\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q,\,q>a}\{f>q\}$$
(if $f(x)>a$, choose a rational $q\in(a,f(x))$), a countable union.
Interval criterion: for real-valued $f$, $\{a<f<b\}=\{f>a\}\cap\{f<b\}$, and $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$, so the interval criterion is equivalent. If $f$ may take the values $\pm\infty$, however, the last identity omits the points where $f=+\infty$; then $\{f=+\infty\}$ and $\{f=-\infty\}$ must be required to be measurable separately.

Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and $\mathcal F=\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$. For every open set $U$, the preimage $f^{-1}(U)$ is open, hence Borel; since $\mathcal B(\mathbb R)$ is generated by open sets, the argument with $\mathcal H$ in Step 1 shows that $f$ is measurable. The converse fails: the Dirichlet function $D=1_{\mathbb Q}$ is nowhere continuous. For every $a$,
$$\{D>a\}=\begin{cases}\mathbb R,&a<0,\\ \mathbb Q,&0\le a<1,\\ \varnothing,&a\ge1,\end{cases}$$
and all these sets are Borel, so $D$ is measurable. Nowhere continuity: for any $x_0$, choose rationals $q_n\to x_0$ and irrationals $r_n\to x_0$; then $D(q_n)=1$ and $D(r_n)=0$, so the two subsequences have different limits. Conclusion: continuity is sufficient but not necessary for measurability.

Let $f,g$ be real-valued and measurable. Sum: for $a\in\mathbb R$,
$$\{f+g>a\}=\bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q}\bigl(\{f>q\}\cap\{g>a-q\}\bigr).$$
If $f(x)+g(x)>a$, choose a rational $q$ with $f(x)>q>a-g(x)$; then $x$ lies in the right-hand side. Conversely, if $f(x)>q$ and $g(x)>a-q$, then $f(x)+g(x)>a$, so the right-hand side is contained in $\{f+g>a\}$. Countable unions and finite intersections preserve measurability, so $f+g$ is measurable.
Scalar multiples: for $c>0$, $\{cf>a\}=\{f>a/c\}$; for $c<0$, $\{cf>a\}=\{f<a/c\}$; for $c=0$, $\{cf>a\}$ is $\varnothing$ or $\mathbb R$. Hence $cf$ is measurable.
Products: $f^2$ is measurable, since for $a\ge0$, $\{f^2>a\}=\{f>\sqrt a\}\cup\{f<-\sqrt a\}$, while for $a<0$ the set is $\mathbb R$; then
$$fg=\frac14\bigl[(f+g)^2-(f-g)^2\bigr].$$
$\max(f,g)$ is measurable because $\{\max(f,g)>a\}=\{f>a\}\cup\{g>a\}$; $|f|=\max(f,-f)$ is measurable too.

Let $f_n$ be measurable, with values in $[-\infty,+\infty]$ and the Borel $\sigma$-algebra there. For $a\in\mathbb R$,
$$\begin{aligned}\Bigl\{\sup_n f_n>a\Bigr\}&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f_n>a\},\\ \Bigl\{\inf_n f_n<a\Bigr\}&=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{f_n<a\}.\end{aligned}$$
Indeed, the supremum exceeds $a$ iff some $f_n$ does; the second identity is dual. Hence $\sup_n f_n$ and $\inf_n f_n$ are measurable. Now put
$$g_k=\sup_{n\ge k}f_n,\qquad h_k=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n;$$
they are measurable, and
$$\limsup_{n}f_n=\inf_{k\ge1}g_k,\qquad \liminf_{n}f_n=\sup_{k\ge1}h_k$$
are measurable. If $f_n$ converges pointwise to $f$, then $f=\limsup f_n=\liminf f_n$ is measurable. Note: if the $f_n$ are real-valued but $\sup_n f_n$ may equal $+\infty$, measurability is understood in the extended real line; if the supremum is finite everywhere, it is a real-valued measurable function.

Quotients: let $f,g$ be measurable and let $N=\{g=0\}$ satisfy $\mu(N)=0$. Define $	ilde g=g$ on $N^c$ and $	ilde g=1$ on $N$. Since $N=\{g=0\}$ is the preimage of a Borel set, it is measurable; $	ilde g$ is obtained from $g$ by changing values on the measurable set $N$ to a constant, so $	ilde g$ is measurable and $	ilde g
e0$ everywhere. Also $x\mapsto1/x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, so $1/	ilde g$ is measurable, and hence $f/	ilde g$ is measurable; it equals $f/g$ on $N^c$, so we define $f/g=f/	ilde g$. The condition "$g
e0$ a.e." is exactly what makes the quotient legitimate as an a.e. defined function; if $g$ vanished on a set of positive measure, then $f/g$ would be undefined there, and an arbitrary extension would no longer represent the quotient.
Almost everywhere: the statement "$f=g$ a.e." means that $\{f
e g\}$ is contained in a null set (equivalently, $\mu(\{f
e g\})=0$ when this set is measurable). If $f$ is measurable, $g=f$ a.e., and the measure is complete, then $g$ is measurable: for a Borel set $B$, the set $g^{-1}(B)$ differs from $f^{-1}(B)$ by a subset of the null set $\{f
e g\}$, hence is measurable. Without completeness one needs the additional hypothesis that $\{f
e g\}$ is contained in a measurable null set. Example: $D=1_{\mathbb Q}$ satisfies $D=0$ a.e. because $m(\mathbb Q)=0$; hence $D$ is measurable and its Lebesgue integral over $[0,1]$ is $0$, although $D$ is nowhere continuous and not Riemann integrable. Statements that hold a.e. say nothing about pointwise values on the exceptional null set.

formulas.note: 可测函数的一般定义：可测集的原像仍可测。
formulas.noteEn: General definition: the preimage of every measurable set is measurable.

formulas.note: 实值函数的等价判据：水平集 $\{f>a\}$ 可测；也可换成 $\{f\ge a\}$、$\{f<a\}$、$\{f\le a\}$，但要统一使用其中一种。
formulas.noteEn: Equivalent criterion for real-valued functions: the level sets $\{f>a\}$ are measurable; one may replace them by $\{f\ge a\}$, $\{f<a\}$ or $\{f\le a\}$, but must use one fixed form.

formulas.note: 不同水平集之间的转换：说明 $>$ 与 $\ge$ 的判据互相等价。
formulas.noteEn: Conversion between level sets, showing that the '$>$' and '$\ge$' criteria are equivalent.

formulas.note: 对四则运算封闭；除法 $f/g$ 要求分母几乎处处不为零。
formulas.noteEn: Closure under arithmetic; the quotient $f/g$ requires the denominator to be nonzero almost everywhere.

formulas.note: 对可数极限运算封闭：这使可测函数与积分理论紧密配合。
formulas.noteEn: Closure under countable limiting operations, which makes measurable functions mesh with integration theory.

properties: 连续函数（在相应 σ 代数下）可测；可测函数可以很不连续，甚至处处不连续（狄利克雷函数）。
可测函数对加、减、乘、数乘、绝对值、取最大/最小封闭；除法 $f/g$ 可测要求分母 $g$ 几乎处处不为零，在 $g=0$ 处任意补定义即可。
可测函数列的可数上确界、下确界、上极限、下极限与逐点极限仍可测。
若 $g$ 连续（更一般地 $g$ 为 Borel 可测），则 $g\circ f$ 可测；若 $g$ 只是勒贝格可测，复合可能失去可测性。
两个可测函数之集 $\{f>g\}$、$\{f=g\}$ 与 $\{f=c\}$ 都可测。
propertiesEn: Continuous functions (for compatible σ-algebras) are measurable; measurable functions may be nowhere continuous, as the Dirichlet function shows.

Measurable functions are closed under sums, differences, products, scalar multiples, $|f|$ and max/min; the quotient $f/g$ is measurable provided $g\ne0$ almost everywhere, with arbitrary values where $g=0$.
Countable suprema, infima, limits superior and inferior, and pointwise limits of measurable functions are measurable.
If $g$ is continuous (more generally Borel measurable) then $g\circ f$ is measurable; if $g$ is merely Lebesgue measurable the composition can fail to be measurable.
For measurable $f$ and $g$, the sets $\{f>g\}$, $\{f=g\}$ and $\{f=c\}$ are all measurable.

examples.problem: 验证狄利克雷函数 $D(x)=1$（$x\in\mathbb{Q}$）、$D(x)=0$（$x\notin\mathbb{Q}$）是可测函数，并说明它处处不连续。
examples.solution: 对任意 $a\in\mathbb{R}$ 分情况讨论 $\{D>a\}$：若 $a<0$，该集合为 $\mathbb{R}$；若 $0\le a<1$，该集合为 $\mathbb{Q}$；若 $a\ge1$，该集合为 $\varnothing$。三者都是 Borel 集，故 $D$ 可测。处处不连续：任取 $x_0$，取有理数列 $q_n\to x_0$ 与无理数列 $r_n\to x_0$，则 $D(q_n)=1\to1$ 而 $D(r_n)=0\to0$，极限不唯一，故 $D$ 在 $x_0$ 不连续。又 $\mathbb{Q}$ 是零测集，所以 $D=0$ 几乎处处成立，它在 $[0,1]$ 上的勒贝格积分为 $0$，尽管它不是黎曼可积的。

examples.problem: 证明：$f$ 可测 $\Rightarrow$ $|f|$ 可测；并说明反过来不成立。
examples.solution: 对任意 $a\ge0$，$\{|f|>a\}=\{f>a\}\cup\{f<-a\}$ 是两个可测集之并，可测；当 $a<0$ 时 $\{|f|>a\}=\mathbb{R}$，可测。所以 $|f|$ 可测。反过来：取不可测集 $A$（维塔利集，其存在性是勒贝格测度理论的经典事实），令 $$f=1_{A}-1_{A^{c}}=\begin{cases}1,&x\in A,\\ -1,&x\notin A.\end{cases}$$ 则 $|f|\equiv1$ 可测，但 $\{f>0\}=A$ 不可测，故 $f$ 不可测。这说明「取绝对值」会丢失符号信息，可测性不能从 $|f|$ 反推 $f$。

expression.text: f 可测 ⟺ 对每个实数 a，{x : f(x) > a} 可测（换成 ≥、<、≤ 同样等价）
expression.note: 等价定义可固定一种形式的水平集，如 {f > a}；对实值函数，区间形式 {a < f < b} 也是等价的判据。
expression.noteEn: The equivalent definitions may fix one form of level set, e.g. {f > a}; for real-valued functions the interval form {a < f < b} is an equally valid criterion.

simple-functions.definition:
**简单函数**是指取有限个值的可测函数，等价地可以写成 $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\chi_{E_i},$$ 其中 $c_i$ 是常数，$E_i$ 是可测集且两两不交，$\chi_{E_i}$ 是**示性函数**（$x\in E_i$ 时取 $1$，否则取 $0$）。示性函数本身是最简单的简单函数；有限线性组合、有限个简单函数的和与积仍是简单函数。

为什么盯住简单函数？因为它们太容易积分了：对非负简单函数 $\varphi=\sum c_i\chi_{E_i}$，勒贝格积分就直接定义为 $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\,\mu(E_i),$$ 完全不需要像黎曼积分那样分割定义域再取极限。于是问题只剩下一个：一般可测函数能不能用简单函数「逼近」出来？答案是能，而且逼近得非常强。

**【关键定理】** 设 $f\ge0$ 可测。则存在简单函数列 $\{\varphi_n\}$，满足 (i) $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$（**单调递增**）；(ii) 对每个 $x$，$\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$（逐点收敛）。标准构造是把值域 $[0,n]$ 等分成 $n2^n$ 段、并允许超过 $n$ 时取 $n$：$$\varphi_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\,\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}+n\,\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.$$ 随着 $n$ 增大，网格变细、截断值 $n$ 升高，两个来源的误差都趋于零，且可以验证 $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}\le f$。

对一般的（可正可负的）可测函数 $f$，把它拆成正部与负部 $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$ 分别逼近再相减即可；此时单调性一般不保持，但有 $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ 且 $\varphi_n\to f$ 逐点。定理说明：简单函数在逐点逼近的意义下「稠密」于可测函数空间，因此许多积分定理（如单调收敛定理）只需先对简单函数证明，再用逼近过渡到一般可测函数。
simple-functions.definitionEn:
A **simple function** is a measurable function taking finitely many values; equivalently, $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\chi_{E_i},$$ where the $c_i$ are constants, the measurable sets $E_i$ are pairwise disjoint, and $\chi_{E_i}$ is the **indicator** of $E_i$ (equal to $1$ on $E_i$ and $0$ outside). Indicators are the simplest examples, and finite linear combinations, sums and products of simple functions remain simple.

Why simple functions? Because they are trivially integrable: for a nonnegative simple function $\varphi=\sum c_i\chi_{E_i}$ the Lebesgue integral is defined directly by $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\,\mu(E_i),$$ with no partition-of-the-domain limit as in Riemann's theory. The only remaining question is whether simple functions can approximate a general measurable function — and the answer is a strong yes.

**Key theorem.** If $f\ge0$ is measurable, there exist simple functions $\varphi_n$ with (i) $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ (**monotone**); (ii) $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x$ (pointwise). The standard construction splits the range on $[0,n]$ into $n2^n$ equal pieces and truncates above $n$: $$\varphi_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\,\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}+n\,\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.$$ As $n$ grows the grid gets finer and the truncation level rises, so both error sources vanish and one checks that $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}\le f$.

For a general (signed) measurable $f$ one writes $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$, approximates both parts and subtracts; monotonicity is then usually lost, but one still has $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ and $\varphi_n\to f$ pointwise. Hence simple functions are pointwise dense in the space of measurable functions, and many integral theorems (monotone convergence, for instance) are first proved for simple functions and then extended by approximation.
derivation: 设 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 是测度空间。若 $\varphi:X\to\mathbb{R}$ 可测且只取有限个值，则称 $\varphi$ 为**简单函数**。把它的互不相同的值记为 $a_1,\dots,a_n$（其中可以有 $0$），令 $A_i=\varphi^{-1}(\{a_i\})$，则 $A_i$ 两两不交、可测，且 $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}A_i=X.$$ 反过来，任何这样的有限线性组合都是简单函数；若某个 $a_i=0$，该项不改变函数值；为使各 $A_i$ 覆盖 $X$，可把 $0$ 也列为一个值。示性函数 $\chi_A$ 是 $n=1$ 的特例。
