对非负简单函数 $\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i}$（$a_i\ge0$，$A_i$ 两两不交），定义 $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i),$$ 并约定 $0\cdot\infty=0$。这个值不依赖表示：若另有 $\varphi=\sum_{j=1}^{m}b_j\chi_{B_j}$，取公共加细 $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$。在非空的 $C_{ij}$ 上 $a_i=b_j$，由有限可加性 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_i a_i\mu(A_i)&=\sum_{i,j}a_i\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\sum_{i,j}b_j\mu(C_{ij})=\sum_j b_j\mu(B_j).\end{aligned}$$ 因此简单函数的积分是良定义的；零高度块即使测度为 $\infty$ 也只贡献 $0$。

设 $f\ge0$ 可测。对 $n\ge1$ 把值域 $[0,n)$ 按步长 $2^{-n}$ 分段，并在 $f\ge n$ 处截断，令 $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_n&=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}\\&\quad +n\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.\end{aligned}$$ 因为 $f$ 可测，每个水平集 $\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}$ 与 $\{f\ge n\}$ 都可测；这些集合两两不交，$\varphi_n$ 只取有限个值，所以 $\varphi_n$ 是非负简单函数。并且逐点有 $0\le\varphi_n\le f$：在分段处取该段左端点，在截断处取 $n$。

证明 $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}$。固定 $x$。若 $f(x)\ge n+1$，则 $\varphi_n(x)=n<n+1=\varphi_{n+1}(x)$；若 $n\le f(x)<n+1$，则 $\varphi_n(x)=n$，而 $\varphi_{n+1}(x)\ge n$（$n$ 是 $n+1$ 层的网格点）。若 $f(x)<n$，设 $f(x)\in[\frac{k-1}{2^n},\frac{k}{2^n})$，则 $\varphi_n(x)=\frac{k-1}{2^n}$；在更细的 $2^{-(n+1)}$ 网格中，左端点只可能右移，故 $\varphi_{n+1}(x)\ge\frac{k-1}{2^n}$。三种情形都给出 $\varphi_n(x)\le\varphi_{n+1}(x)$，所以 $\{\varphi_n\}$ 单调递增且始终不超过 $f$。

固定 $x$。若 $f(x)<\infty$，取 $n>f(x)$，则 $x\notin\{f\ge n\}$，且 $x$ 落在某个二进区间 $[\frac{k-1}{2^n},\frac{k}{2^n})$ 中，于是 $$0\le f(x)-\varphi_n(x)<\frac{1}{2^n}\to0.$$ 若 $f(x)=\infty$，则对每个 $n$ 有 $\varphi_n(x)=n$，故 $\varphi_n(x)\to\infty=f(x)$。因此 $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$ 对每个 $x$ 成立（不只是几乎处处），且整个逼近过程保持非负与单调。

对一般可测 $f$，写 $f=f^+-f^-$，其中 $f^+=\max(f,0)$、$f^-=\max(-f,0)$。分别用上述构造取 $0\le\varphi_n^+\uparrow f^+$、$0\le\varphi_n^-\uparrow f^-$，令 $\psi_n=\varphi_n^+-\varphi_n^-$。则 $\psi_n$ 是简单函数，$|\psi_n|\le|f|$，且 $\psi_n(x)\to f(x)$ 逐点成立。此时 $\psi_n$ 一般不再单调（两个单调序列相减，差可能上下波动），但控制 $|\psi_n|\le|f|$ 足够强：当 $f\in L^1$ 时，由 $|\psi_n-f|\le2|f|$ 与控制收敛定理 $\int|\psi_n-f|\to0$，即简单函数在 $L^1$ 中稠密。特别地，非负情形下由单调收敛定理 $\int f=\lim_n\int\varphi_n$。
derivationEn: Let $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ be a measure space. A measurable $\varphi:X\to\mathbb{R}$ taking only finitely many values is called a **simple function**. Denote its distinct values by $a_1,\dots,a_n$ (zero may occur) and set $A_i=\varphi^{-1}(\{a_i\})$. Then the $A_i$ are pairwise disjoint and measurable, and $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad \bigcup_{i=1}^{n}A_i=X.$$ Conversely, every such finite linear combination is simple; if some $a_i=0$, that term does not change the function; to make the $A_i$ cover $X$, one may include $0$ as a value. The indicator $\chi_A$ is the case $n=1$.

For a nonnegative simple function $\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i}$ with $a_i\ge0$ and pairwise disjoint $A_i$, define $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i),$$ with the convention $0\cdot\infty=0$. This value is independent of the representation: if also $\varphi=\sum_{j=1}^{m}b_j\chi_{B_j}$, take the common refinement $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$. On every nonempty $C_{ij}$ we have $a_i=b_j$, and finite additivity gives $$\begin{aligned}\sum_i a_i\mu(A_i)&=\sum_{i,j}a_i\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\sum_{i,j}b_j\mu(C_{ij})=\sum_j b_j\mu(B_j).\end{aligned}$$ Hence the simple integral is well defined; a zero-height piece contributes $0$ even when its measure is $\infty$.

Let $f\ge0$ be measurable. For $n\ge1$, split the range $[0,n)$ into steps of size $2^{-n}$ and truncate at $n$: $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_n&=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}\\&\quad +n\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.\end{aligned}$$ Since $f$ is measurable, each level set $\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}$ and $\{f\ge n\}$ is measurable; they are pairwise disjoint and $\varphi_n$ takes finitely many values, so $\varphi_n$ is a nonnegative simple function. Pointwise $0\le\varphi_n\le f$: on each piece it equals the left endpoint, and on the truncation set it equals $n$.

Prove $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}$. Fix $x$. If $f(x)\ge n+1$, then $\varphi_n(x)=n<n+1=\varphi_{n+1}(x)$. If $n\le f(x)<n+1$, then $\varphi_n(x)=n$, while $\varphi_{n+1}(x)\ge n$ because $n$ is a grid point of the $(n+1)$-st partition. If $f(x)<n$, say $f(x)\in[\frac{k-1}{2^n},\frac{k}{2^n})$, then $\varphi_n(x)=\frac{k-1}{2^n}$; refining the grid to mesh $2^{-(n+1)}$ can only move the left endpoint to the right, so $\varphi_{n+1}(x)\ge\frac{k-1}{2^n}$. All three cases give $\varphi_n(x)\le\varphi_{n+1}(x)$, hence $\{\varphi_n\}$ is increasing and bounded above by $f$.

Fix $x$. If $f(x)<\infty$, choose $n>f(x)$. Then $x\notin\{f\ge n\}$ and $x$ lies in some dyadic interval $[\frac{k-1}{2^n},\frac{k}{2^n})$, so $$0\le f(x)-\varphi_n(x)<\frac{1}{2^n}\to0.$$ If $f(x)=\infty$, then $\varphi_n(x)=n$ for every $n$, so $\varphi_n(x)\to\infty=f(x)$. Thus $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x$ (not merely almost everywhere), and the whole approximation stays nonnegative and increasing.

For a general measurable $f$, write $f=f^+-f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-=\max(-f,0)$. Apply the construction to both parts to get $0\le\varphi_n^+\uparrow f^+$ and $0\le\varphi_n^-\uparrow f^-$, and set $\psi_n=\varphi_n^+-\varphi_n^-$. Then $\psi_n$ is simple, $|\psi_n|\le|f|$, and $\psi_n(x)\to f(x)$ pointwise. The sequence $\psi_n$ need not be monotone (a difference of two increasing sequences may oscillate), but the bound $|\psi_n|\le|f|$ is strong enough: if $f\in L^1$, then $|\psi_n-f|\le2|f|$ and dominated convergence gives $\int|\psi_n-f|\to0$, so simple functions are dense in $L^1$. In the nonnegative case, in particular, monotone convergence gives $\int f=\lim_n\int\varphi_n$.

formulas.note: 简单函数的一般形式：有限个可测集示性函数的线性组合。
formulas.noteEn: General form of a simple function: a finite linear combination of indicators of measurable sets.

formulas.note: 简单函数的积分定义（对非负简单函数）：只依赖各水平集的测度。
formulas.noteEn: Integral of a nonnegative simple function: it depends only on the measures of the level sets.

formulas.note: 标准逼近构造：把 $[0,n]$ 等分并截断，$\varphi_n$ 单调递增地逼近 $f$。
formulas.noteEn: The standard approximation: partition $[0,n]$ and truncate, so that $\varphi_n$ increases to $f$.

formulas.note: 逼近定理的两条结论：单调递增且逐点收敛。
formulas.noteEn: The two conclusions of the approximation theorem: monotone increase and pointwise convergence.

formulas.note: 非负可测函数的积分定义：所有不超过 $f$ 的非负简单函数之积分的上确界。
formulas.noteEn: Definition of the integral for nonnegative measurable functions: the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative simple functions dominated by $f$.

properties: 取有限个值的可测函数恰是简单函数；示性函数是特殊的简单函数，阶梯函数是典型例子。
简单函数对线性组合、和、差、积封闭，运算结果仍取有限个值。
非负简单函数的积分 $\int\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_i c_i\mu(E_i)$ 具有线性与单调性，不同分解方式给出同一个值。
对非负可测函数 $f$，存在简单函数列满足 $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ 且 $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$；对一般可测函数可拆成 $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$，用 $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ 的简单函数列逼近。
逼近定理把积分问题化归为简单函数：非负可测函数的积分定义为所有不超过它的非负简单函数之积分的上确界，单调收敛定理由此展开。
propertiesEn: A measurable function with finitely many values is exactly a simple function; indicators are special cases and step functions are the typical picture.
Simple functions are closed under linear combinations, sums, differences and products, and the results still take finitely many values.
For nonnegative simple functions, $\int\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_i c_i\mu(E_i)$ is linear and monotone, and different disjoint decompositions give the same value.

For nonnegative measurable $f$ there are simple $\varphi_n$ with $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ and $\varphi_n\to f$ pointwise; a general measurable $f$ is handled through $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$ with $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$.

The theorem reduces integration to simple functions: the integral of a nonnegative measurable function is the supremum of the integrals of the nonnegative simple functions dominated by it, on which the monotone convergence theorem is built.

examples.problem: 验证 $s_n(x)=\bigl(\lfloor 2^n x\rfloor/2^n\bigr)^2$ 在 $[0,2]$ 上是简单函数，并说明 $\{s_n\}$ 单调递增且逐点收敛到 $f(x)=x^2$。
examples.solution: 对每个 $n$，$s_n$ 在每个小区间 $\bigl[\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}\bigr)$ 上取常值 $\bigl(\frac{k}{2^n}\bigr)^2$（$k=0,1,\dots,2^{n+1}-1$），只取有限个值且各水平集是区间（可测），故为简单函数。单调性：记 $k_n=\lfloor2^n x\rfloor$，网格加密时 $k_{n+1}/2^{n+1}\ge k_n/2^n$，故 $s_{n+1}(x)\ge s_n(x)$。收敛：由 $0\le x-k_n/2^n<2^{-n}$ 得 $k_n/2^n\to x$，平方得 $s_n(x)\to x^2$；并且始终有 $s_n(x)\le x^2$。这正是「非负可测函数被单调递增简单函数列逼近」的具体实例。

examples.problem: 设 $E$ 可测，$\varphi=2\chi_{E}+3\chi_{\mathbb{R}\setminus E}$，且已知 $m(E\cap[0,1])=\frac14$。用简单函数的积分公式计算 $\int_{[0,1]}\varphi\,dm$。
examples.solution: $\varphi$ 只取 $2$ 与 $3$ 两个值，是简单函数。在 $[0,1]$ 上按不交可测集分解（注意 $E\cap[0,1]$ 与 $[0,1]\setminus E$ 不交、并为 $[0,1]$）： $$\int_{[0,1]}\varphi\,dm=2\,m(E\cap[0,1])+3\,m([0,1]\setminus E)=2\cdot\frac14+3\cdot\frac34=\frac{11}{4}.$$ 可见简单函数的积分只关心各个水平集的测度，与集合的具体形状无关。

expression.text: φ = Σᵢ cᵢ·χ_{Eᵢ}（Eᵢ 两两不交、可测，cᵢ 为常数）
expression.note: 示性函数 χ_E 在 E 上取 1、在 E 外取 0；取有限个值的函数是简单函数当且仅当每个水平集可测。
expression.noteEn: The indicator χ_E is 1 on E and 0 outside; a function with finitely many values is simple exactly when all its level sets are measurable.

convergence-ae.definition:
在测度空间中，「函数列收敛」不止一种含义，因为人们愿意原谅测度为 $0$ 的坏点。设 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 是测度空间，$f_n,f$ 可测。称 $f_n$ **几乎处处收敛**（a.e. 收敛）于 $f$，如果存在零测集 $N$（$\mu(N)=0$），使得对所有 $x\notin N$ 都有 $f_n(x)\to f(x)$；换言之，不收敛的点集是零测集。例如 $f_n(x)=x^n$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上不处处收敛到 $0$（在 $x=1$ 处 $f_n(1)=1$），但 $\{1\}$ 是零测集，所以它几乎处处收敛到 $0$。

另一种收敛方式是**依测度收敛**：对任何 $\varepsilon>0$，$$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\qquad(n\to\infty).$$ 它的意思是：偏差大的集合在测度意义下越来越小，并不要求每一点都安定下来。它把「逐点」换成了「测度」。

两种收敛的关系是实变函数里最爱考的反例工厂。**a.e. 收敛一般推不出依测度收敛**：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取勒贝格测度与 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，每个点只属于有限多个这样的区间，故 $f_n(x)\to0$ 处处成立，但 $m(\{|f_n-0|\ge\frac12\})=1$ 不趋于 $0$，不依测度收敛。一旦加上**有限测度**条件（$\mu(X)<\infty$），a.e. 收敛就蕴含依测度收敛（叶戈罗夫定理可以给出更漂亮的一致收敛版本）。

反方向：**依测度收敛也推不出 a.e. 收敛**，而且这不需要任何有限性假设的让步——即使测度有限也不成立。经典反例是 $[0,1]$ 上的「滑动区间」：把 $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$（$k=0,\dots,n-1$）按 $n$ 递增排成一列，则每个集合的测度为 $1/n\to0$，故依测度收敛到 $0$；但每个 $x\in[0,1)$ 在每一层 $n$ 都被某个区间盖住，于是无穷多次取到 $1$，极限不存在，故不 a.e. 收敛。不过**依测度收敛的序列总能取出一个 a.e. 收敛的子列**（取子列使 $\mu(\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge\frac1j\})\le2^{-j}$，再用 Borel–Cantelli 引理），子列是这道裂缝唯一的补救。
convergence-ae.definitionEn:
In a measure space 'convergence of a sequence of functions' has more than one useful meaning, because behaviour on a null set may be forgiven. Let $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ be a measure space and $f_n,f$ measurable. We say $f_n\to f$ **almost everywhere** (a.e.) if there is a null set $N$ with $\mu(N)=0$ such that $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x\notin N$; the set where convergence fails has measure zero. For instance $f_n(x)=x^n$ on $[0,1]$ does not converge everywhere to $0$ (at $x=1$, $f_n(1)=1$), but $\{1\}$ is null, so it converges a.e. to $0$.

Another notion is **convergence in measure**: for every $\varepsilon>0$, $$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\qquad(n\to\infty).$$ Large deviations occur on sets that become small; no individual point is required to settle down. The pointwise requirement is replaced by a measure-theoretic one.

The relation between the two is a classical source of counterexamples. **Almost everywhere convergence does not imply convergence in measure** in general: on $\mathbb{R}$ with Lebesgue measure take $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$. Every point lies in at most one of these intervals, so $f_n\to0$ everywhere, yet $m(\{|f_n|\ge\frac12\})=1$ does not tend to $0$. Once the measure is **finite** ($\mu(X)<\infty$), a.e. convergence does imply convergence in measure (Egorov's theorem gives a sharper, uniform version).

Conversely, **convergence in measure does not imply a.e. convergence**, and this survives even finite measures. The classical counterexample is the sliding-interval sequence on $[0,1]$: enumerate $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$ with $k=0,\dots,n-1$ and let $n$ increase. Each set has measure $1/n\to0$, so $f\to0$ in measure; but every $x\in[0,1)$ is hit once at each level $n$, hence infinitely often, so the limit fails to exist almost everywhere. The gap is bridged by subsequences: convergence in measure always yields a subsequence converging a.e. (choose $n_j$ with $\mu(\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge\frac1j\})\le2^{-j}$ and apply Borel–Cantelli).
derivation: 设 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 是测度空间，$f_n,f$ 实值可测（若只在 a.e. 有限，先去掉一个零测集）。称 $f_n$ **几乎处处收敛**于 $f$，若 $$\mu\bigl(\{x:f_n(x)\not\to f(x)\}\bigr)=0;$$ 称 $f_n$ **依测度收敛**于 $f$，若对每个 $\varepsilon>0$，$$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\quad(n\to\infty).$$ 前者要求去掉一个零测集后逐点收敛；后者只要求偏差超过 $\varepsilon$ 的集合测度越来越小，不要求任何一点最终稳定。

若 $\mu(X)<\infty$，则 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛。固定 $\varepsilon>0$，令 $E_n=\{|f_n-f|\ge\varepsilon\}$。若 $\mu(E_n)\not\to0$，则存在 $\delta>0$ 与子列 $n_k$ 使 $\mu(E_{n_k})\ge\delta$。由测度的上连续性（这里用到 $\mu(X)<\infty$），$$\begin{aligned}\mu\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigcup_{k\ge j}E_{n_k}\Bigr)&=\lim_{j\to\infty}\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{k\ge j}E_{n_k}\Bigr)\\&\ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mu(E_{n_k})\ge\delta.\end{aligned}$$ 在这个正测度集合上，$|f_{n_k}-f|\ge\varepsilon$ 对无穷多个 $k$ 成立，故 $f_{n_k}$ 不收敛于 $f$，与 a.e. 收敛矛盾。因此 $\mu(E_n)\to0$。

有限测度条件不能省。在 $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$。对每个固定的 $x$，当 $n>x$ 时 $x\notin[n,n+1)$，故 $f_n(x)=0$ 最终恒成立，于是 $f_n\to0$ 处处（更强于 a.e.）。但对 $0<\varepsilon\le1$，$$m\bigl(\{|f_n-0|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)=m([n,n+1))=1,$$ 不趋于 $0$，所以 $f_n$ 不依测度收敛于 $0$。这说明「a.e. 收敛 $\Rightarrow$ 依测度收敛」在无限测度空间上失效。

反方向即使测度有限也不成立。在 $[0,1]$ 上按 $n=1,2,\dots$、每个 $n$ 取 $k=0,\dots,n-1$ 的顺序排列 $$f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}.$$ 对任意 $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$，$\{f_{n,k}\ge\varepsilon\}=[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，测度为 $1/n$；当序号增大时 $n\to\infty$，故 $f_{n,k}\to0$ 依测度。可是对每个 $x\in[0,1)$ 与每个 $n$，恰有一个 $k$ 使 $x\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，所以每一层 $n$ 中 $f_{n,k}(x)$ 恰有一次为 $1$、其余为 $0$；当 $n\to\infty$ 时它在 $0$ 与 $1$ 之间无穷次振荡，极限不存在。故不 a.e. 收敛（不收敛点集为 $[0,1)$，测度为 $1$）。

依测度收敛虽不能推出整体 a.e. 收敛，但总能取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。设 $f_n\to f$ 依测度。对每个 $j\ge1$，因 $\mu(\{|f_n-f|\ge2^{-j}\})\to0$，可取 $n_j$ 严格递增，使 $$\mu\bigl(E_j\bigr)<2^{-j},\qquad E_j=\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge2^{-j}\}.$$ 于是 $\sum_j\mu(E_j)<\infty$。由 Borel–Cantelli 引理，$\mu(\limsup_j E_j)=0$。若 $x\notin\limsup_j E_j$，则 $x$ 只属于有限多个 $E_j$，故存在 $J$ 使 $j\ge J$ 时 $|f_{n_j}(x)-f(x)|<2^{-j}$，从而 $f_{n_j}(x)\to f(x)$。所以 $f_{n_j}\to f$ a.e.。

依测度极限在 a.e. 意义下唯一。设 $f_n\to f$ 且 $f_n\to g$ 依测度。对每个 $k\ge1$，令 $A_k=\{|f-g|>1/k\}$。由三角不等式 $$A_k\subset\{|f_n-f|>1/(2k)\}\cup\{|f_n-g|>1/(2k)\}.$$ 右边两个集合的测度当 $n\to\infty$ 都趋于 $0$，故 $\mu(A_k)=0$。而 $\{f\ne g\}=\bigcup_{k\ge1}A_k$，是可数并，仍为零测集，所以 $f=g$ a.e.。这也说明：依测度收敛只确定一个 a.e. 等价类，不能确定逐点值。
derivationEn: Let $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n,f$ be real-valued measurable (if they are only finite a.e., first delete a null set). We say $f_n\to f$ **almost everywhere** if $$\mu\bigl(\{x:f_n(x)\not\to f(x)\}\bigr)=0;$$ and $f_n\to f$ **in measure** if for every $\varepsilon>0$, $$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\quad(n\to\infty).$$ The first requires pointwise convergence after removing one null set; the second only requires the set of deviations exceeding $\varepsilon$ to have small measure, with no individual point forced to settle.

If $\mu(X)<\infty$, then a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and set $E_n=\{|f_n-f|\ge\varepsilon\}$. If $\mu(E_n)\not\to0$, there are $\delta>0$ and a subsequence $n_k$ with $\mu(E_{n_k})\ge\delta$. By upper continuity of the measure (this is where $\mu(X)<\infty$ is used), $$\begin{aligned}\mu\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigcup_{k\ge j}E_{n_k}\Bigr)&=\lim_{j\to\infty}\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{k\ge j}E_{n_k}\Bigr)\\&\ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mu(E_{n_k})\ge\delta.\end{aligned}$$ On this set of positive measure, $|f_{n_k}-f|\ge\varepsilon$ for infinitely many $k$, so $f_{n_k}$ does not converge to $f$, contradicting a.e. convergence. Hence $\mu(E_n)\to0$.

The finite-measure hypothesis cannot be dropped. On $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ take $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$. For each fixed $x$, if $n>x$ then $x\notin[n,n+1)$, so $f_n(x)=0$ eventually; hence $f_n\to0$ everywhere (stronger than a.e.). But for $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $$m\bigl(\{|f_n-0|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)=m([n,n+1))=1,$$ which does not tend to $0$, so $f_n$ does not converge to $0$ in measure. Thus a.e. convergence need not imply convergence in measure on an infinite measure space.

The converse fails even for finite measure. On $[0,1]$, enumerate $$f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$$ by $n=1,2,\dots$ and, for each $n$, $k=0,\dots,n-1$. For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, $\{f_{n,k}\ge\varepsilon\}=[k/n,(k+1)/n)$, whose measure is $1/n$; as the enumeration index grows, $n\to\infty$, so $f_{n,k}\to0$ in measure. However, for each $x\in[0,1)$ and each $n$ there is exactly one $k$ with $x\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$, so at level $n$ the value $f_{n,k}(x)$ equals $1$ exactly once and $0$ otherwise; as $n\to\infty$ it oscillates between $0$ and $1$ infinitely often, so the limit does not exist. Hence it does not converge a.e. (the nonconvergence set is $[0,1)$, of measure $1$).

Convergence in measure does not imply a.e. convergence of the whole sequence, but it always yields an a.e. convergent subsequence. Suppose $f_n\to f$ in measure. For each $j\ge1$, since $\mu(\{|f_n-f|\ge2^{-j}\})\to0$, choose strictly increasing $n_j$ such that $$\mu(E_j)<2^{-j},\qquad E_j=\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge2^{-j}\}.$$ Then $\sum_j\mu(E_j)<\infty$. By the Borel–Cantelli lemma, $\mu(\limsup_j E_j)=0$. If $x\notin\limsup_j E_j$, then $x$ belongs to only finitely many $E_j$, so for some $J$ and all $j\ge J$, $|f_{n_j}(x)-f(x)|<2^{-j}$; hence $f_{n_j}(x)\to f(x)$. Therefore $f_{n_j}\to f$ a.e.

The limit in measure is unique up to a.e. equality. Suppose $f_n\to f$ and $f_n\to g$ in measure. For each $k\ge1$, let $A_k=\{|f-g|>1/k\}$. The triangle inequality gives $$A_k\subset\{|f_n-f|>1/(2k)\}\cup\{|f_n-g|>1/(2k)\}.$$ Both sets on the right have measure tending to $0$ as $n\to\infty$, so $\mu(A_k)=0$. Since $\{f\ne g\}=\bigcup_{k\ge1}A_k$ is a countable union of null sets, it is null; hence $f=g$ a.e. Thus convergence in measure determines only an a.e. equivalence class, not pointwise values.

formulas.note: 几乎处处收敛：不收敛的点集是零测集，去掉它之后逐点收敛。
formulas.noteEn: Almost everywhere convergence: the set of points where convergence fails is null.

formulas.note: 依测度收敛：偏差超过任意给定 $\varepsilon$ 的集合测度趋于零。
formulas.noteEn: Convergence in measure: the measure of the set where the deviation exceeds any given ε tends to zero.

formulas.note: 有限测度下 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛（叶戈罗夫定理）；一般测度空间中不成立，反例 $\chi_{[n,n+1)}$。
formulas.noteEn: With finite measure, a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure (Egorov); in general measure spaces this fails, with χ_[n,n+1) as counterexample.

formulas.note: 依测度收敛不能整体升格为 a.e. 收敛，但总能取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
formulas.noteEn: Convergence in measure cannot be upgraded globally to a.e. convergence, but an a.e. convergent subsequence always exists.

formulas.note: 有限测度空间中，依测度收敛由这个度量给出；a.e. 收敛一般不来自任何度量，二者强弱关系不对称。
formulas.noteEn: On finite measure spaces convergence in measure is induced by this metric; a.e. convergence generally comes from no metric, so the two notions are asymmetric.

properties: 有限测度空间中 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛；一般测度空间不成立，反例 $\chi_{[n,n+1)}$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上处处收敛却不依测度收敛。
依测度收敛蕴含存在子列 a.e. 收敛；但整体不一定 a.e. 收敛，即使测度有限（$[0,1]$ 上的滑动区间反例）。
依测度收敛的极限在 a.e. 意义下唯一：若 $f_n\to f$ 且 $f_n\to g$ 依测度，则 $\mu(\{f\ne g\})=0$。
概率论中 $P(\Omega)=1<\infty$，故几乎必然收敛蕴含依概率收敛；依概率收敛不蕴含几乎必然收敛。
有限测度下叶戈罗夫定理更强：a.e. 收敛的序列去掉任意小测度集后一致收敛（见叶戈罗夫与卢津定理）。
propertiesEn: On finite measure spaces a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure; in general it does not, as χ_[n,n+1) on ℝ converges everywhere but not in measure.
Convergence in measure yields an a.e. convergent subsequence, yet need not itself be a.e. convergent, even for finite measures (sliding intervals on [0,1]).
Limits in measure are a.e. unique: if f_n→f and f_n→g in measure then μ({f≠g})=0.
In probability theory P(Ω)=1<∞, so almost sure convergence implies convergence in probability, but not conversely.
For finite measures Egorov's theorem is stronger: an a.e. convergent sequence becomes uniformly convergent after removing sets of arbitrarily small measure (see the Egorov–Lusin node).

examples.problem: 在 $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，判断 $f_n$ 是否几乎处处收敛到 $0$、是否依测度收敛到 $0$。
examples.solution: a.e. 收敛：对每个实数 $x$，只有唯一的整数 $n_0=\lfloor x\rfloor$ 满足 $x\in[n_0,n_0+1)$，故当 $n\ne n_0$ 时 $f_n(x)=0$，于是 $f_n(x)\to0$ 对一切 $x$ 成立，当然也 a.e. 收敛。依测度收敛：对 $0<\varepsilon\le1$，$\{x:|f_n(x)-0|\ge\varepsilon\}=[n,n+1)$，其测度恒为 $1$，不趋于 $0$，故不依测度收敛。这说明在一般的（非有限）测度空间中，a.e. 收敛推不出依测度收敛。

examples.problem: 在 $[0,1]$ 上按 $n=1,2,3,\dots$、每个 $n$ 取 $k=0,1,\dots,n-1$ 的顺序排列滑动区间 $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$。证明它依测度收敛到 $0$，但不几乎处处收敛；并指出如何取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
examples.solution: 依测度收敛：任取 $\varepsilon>0$（不妨 $\varepsilon\le1$），$\{f_{n,k}\ge\varepsilon\}=[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，测度为 $1/n$；当序号趋于无穷时 $n\to\infty$，故测度趋于 $0$。不 a.e. 收敛：任取 $x\in[0,1)$ 与任取 $n$，存在唯一的 $k$ 使 $x\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，于是 $f_{n,k}(x)=1$；由于 $n$ 取遍所有正整数，该列在 $x$ 处无穷多次取 $1$（也无穷多次取 $0$），极限不存在。不收敛的点构成 $[0,1)$，测度为 $1>0$，故不 a.e. 收敛。取出子列：只保留 $k=0$ 的那一部分，即 $\chi_{[0,1/n)}$，它对每个 $x\in(0,1]$ 最终为 $0$，仅在 $x=0$ 处始终取 $1$，而 $\{0\}$ 是零测集，故该子列 a.e. 收敛到 $0$——这印证了「依测度收敛总可取出 a.e. 收敛的子列」。

expression.text: a.e. 收敛：去掉零测集后逐点收敛；依测度收敛：对每个 ε>0，m({|fₙ−f| ≥ ε}) → 0
expression.note: 符号表示依测度收敛；概率论中称为依概率收敛。有限测度下 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛，反之只能取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
expression.noteEn: The symbol denotes convergence in measure, called convergence in probability in probability theory. On finite measure spaces a.e. convergence implies it; conversely only an a.e. convergent subsequence can be extracted.

egorov-lusin.definition:
**叶戈罗夫定理**：设 $(X,\mathcal{M},\mu)$ 是**有限测度空间**（即 $\mu(X)<\infty$），$f_n,f$ 是 $X$ 上的实值可测函数，且 $f_n\to f$ 几乎处处成立（不收敛的那个零测集可以并入后面要挖掉的集合）。那么对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在可测集 $E\subset X$，$\mu(E)<\varepsilon$，使得在补集 $X\setminus E$ 上 $f_n$ **一致收敛**于 $f$。一句话：有限测度空间上，**几乎处处收敛 $\Rightarrow$ 几乎一致收敛**（即去掉任意小测度集后一致收敛）。**$\mu(X)<\infty$ 这个条件绝对不能遗漏**，在无限测度空间（如 $\mathbb{R}$）上定理会失效（见例题）。

**鲁津定理**：设 $f$ 是定义在可测集 $E$（$\mu(E)<\infty$）上的**实值**可测函数。那么对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在闭集 $F\subset E$ 使 $\mu(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon$，且限制 $f|_F$ 连续。一句话：可测函数去掉任意小测度集后即连续——这种性质叫「近似连续」。逆命题也成立：若一个函数在去掉任意小测度集后都连续，则它必可测，所以鲁津定理给出了可测性的等价刻画。直觉上，可测函数可以用简单函数（有限个阶梯）逼近，阶梯只有有限个跳跃点，把跳跃点附近的集合挖掉就能连续。

这两条定理的意义在于：可测性、几乎处处收敛这类「测度意义下」的弱性质，只要付出任意小测度的代价，就能升级为连续、一致收敛这类「拓扑意义下」的强性质。叶戈罗夫定理常用来把 a.e. 收敛局部化为一致收敛再作积分估计；鲁津定理说明可测函数与连续函数只差一个可以任意小的集合。它们是实分析里「几乎」哲学的典范。
egorov-lusin.definitionEn:
**Egorov's theorem**: Let $(X,\mathcal{M},\mu)$ be a measure space of **finite measure** ($\mu(X)<\infty$), and let $f_n,f$ be real-valued measurable functions with $f_n\to f$ almost everywhere (the null set of non-convergence may be absorbed into the exceptional set). Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a measurable set $E\subset X$ with $\mu(E)<\varepsilon$ such that $f_n\to f$ **uniformly** on the complement $X\setminus E$. In one line: on a finite measure space, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence. **The hypothesis $\mu(X)<\infty$ cannot be dropped**; on infinite measure spaces such as $\mathbb{R}$ the theorem may fail (see the example).

**Lusin's theorem**: Let $f$ be a **real-valued** measurable function on a measurable set $E$ with $\mu(E)<\infty$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a closed set $F\subset E$ with $\mu(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon$ such that the restriction $f|_F$ is continuous. In one line: a measurable function becomes continuous after removing a set of arbitrarily small measure; this property is called approximate continuity. The converse holds too: any function that is approximately continuous is measurable, so Lusin's theorem characterizes measurability. Intuitively, measurable functions are limits of simple functions (finitely many steps), and deleting small neighborhoods of the finitely many jump points makes them continuous.

These theorems show that measure-theoretic properties that are weak (measurability, a.e. convergence) can be upgraded to topological properties that are strong (continuity, uniform convergence) at the cost of an arbitrarily small set. Egorov's theorem is the standard tool for turning a.e. convergence into uniform convergence before estimating integrals, and Lusin's theorem says a measurable function differs from a continuous one on an arbitrarily small set.
derivation: **叶戈罗夫定理**：设 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 满足 $\mu(X)<\infty$，$f_n,f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ 可测，且 $f_n\to f$ a.e.。则对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在可测集 $E\subset X$，$\mu(E)<\varepsilon$，使得 $$\sup_{x\in X\setminus E}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\to0\qquad(n\to\infty),$$ 即 $f_n$ 在 $X\setminus E$ 上一致收敛于 $f$（几乎一致收敛）。条件中 $\mu(X)<\infty$ 用于把递减集合列的测度连续地降到零；$f_n,f$ 实值（或至少有限 a.e.）用于保证 $|f_n-f|$ 有限、可比较。若只在 a.e. 有限，先删去一个零测集；若极限在正测度集上为 $\pm\infty$，则 $|f_n-f|$ 在该集合上为 $+\infty$（或差没有定义），一致收敛无从谈起。

对 $j\ge1$ 令 $$A_{k,j}=\bigcup_{n\ge k}\Bigl\{|f_n-f|\ge\frac1j\Bigr\},\qquad k=1,2,\dots$$ 则 $A_{k,j}$ 随 $k$ 递减，且 $\bigcap_k A_{k,j}=\{\limsup_n|f_n-f|\ge1/j\}$。由于 $f_n\to f$ a.e.，这个交集是零测集；又 $\mu(X)<\infty$，由测度上连续性得 $\mu(A_{k,j})\to0\ (k\to\infty)$。取 $k_j$ 使 $\mu(A_{k_j,j})<\varepsilon/2^{j+1}$，令 $E=\bigcup_j A_{k_j,j}$，则 $$\mu(E)\le\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{j+1}}=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}<\varepsilon.$$ 在 $X\setminus E$ 上，对每个 $j$ 与所有 $n\ge k_j$ 都有 $|f_n-f|<1/j$；给定 $\eta>0$ 取 $j>1/\eta$，即得一致收敛。

有限测度不能省。在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，则 $f_n\to0$ 处处。假设去掉集合 $E$ 后 $f_n$ 在 $G=\mathbb{R}\setminus E$ 上一致收敛于 $0$，则必须有 $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)\to0$。但对每个 $n$，$$m(G\cap[n,n+1))=1-m(E\cap[n,n+1))\ge1-m(E).$$ 只要 $m(E)<1$，右边为正，故 $G\cap[n,n+1)\ne\emptyset$，从而 $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)=1$ 对所有 $n$ 成立，不可能趋于 $0$。因此任何测度小于 $1$ 的例外集都不够；叶戈罗夫定理在 $\mu(\mathbb{R})=\infty$ 时失效。

**鲁津定理**：设 $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ 可测，$m(E)<\infty$，$f:E\to\mathbb{R}$ 可测。则对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在闭集 $F\subset E$，使 $$m(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon,\qquad f|_F\ \text{连续}.$$ 这里的连续是相对于 $F$ 的子空间拓扑：只要求 $f$ 在 $F$ 上连续，不要求 $f$ 在 $E$ 上处处连续，也不要求 $E\setminus F$ 上的值有什么规律。去掉的集合测度可以任意小，但不保证是零测集；定理只控制 $F$ 上的连续性，不控制例外的部分。它也不涉及 $f$ 在 $E$ 上的一致连续性；若 $F$ 紧，则 $f|_F$ 还自动一致连续（仍只在 $F$ 上）。

证明思路：先取简单函数 $s_n\to f$ 逐点（且 $|s_n|\le|f|$）。因 $m(E)<\infty$，叶戈罗夫定理给出可测集 $G\subset E$，$m(E\setminus G)<\varepsilon/2$，使 $s_n\to f$ 在 $G$ 上一致。每个 $s_n=\sum_i c_{n,i}\chi_{A_{n,i}}$ 只有有限个水平集；由勒贝格测度的内正则性，对每个 $A_{n,i}\cap G$ 取闭集 $F_{n,i}\subset A_{n,i}\cap G$，使 $$m\bigl((A_{n,i}\cap G)\setminus F_{n,i}\bigr)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{n+1}N_n},$$ 其中 $N_n$ 是 $s_n$ 的水平集个数。令 $F_n=\bigcup_i F_{n,i}$，则 $F_n$ 闭、$s_n|_{F_n}$ 连续（在每个 $F_{n,i}$ 上为常数），且 $m(G\setminus F_n)<\varepsilon/2^{n+1}$。再令 $F=\bigcap_n F_n$，则 $F$ 闭，且 $$m(E\setminus F)\le m(E\setminus G)+m(G\setminus F)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{n+1}}<\varepsilon.$$ 所有 $s_n|_F$ 连续，$s_n\to f$ 在 $F$ 上一致，故 $f|_F$ 连续。

例子与边界：$D=\chi_{\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]}$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上可测、$m([0,1])<\infty$。任取 $\varepsilon>0$，取开集 $U\supset\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ 使 $m(U)<\min(\varepsilon,1)$，令 $F=[0,1]\setminus U$。则 $F$ 闭，$m([0,1]\setminus F)\le m(U)<\varepsilon$，且 $F$ 中全为无理点，$D|_F\equiv0$ 连续。但 $D$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上处处不连续（有理点与无理点都稠密），所以鲁津定理的结论不能加强为「$f$ 在 $E$ 上处处连续」；被挖掉的集合一般有正测度，且依赖于 $\varepsilon$。
derivationEn: **Egorov's theorem.** Let $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ satisfy $\mu(X)<\infty$, and let $f_n,f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ be measurable with $f_n\to f$ a.e. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a measurable set $E\subset X$ with $\mu(E)<\varepsilon$ such that $$\sup_{x\in X\setminus E}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\to0\qquad(n\to\infty),$$ i.e. $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $X\setminus E$ (almost uniform convergence). The hypothesis $\mu(X)<\infty$ is used to make the measures of decreasing sets tend to the measure of their intersection; the real-valued (or at least finite a.e.) assumption makes $|f_n-f|$ finite and comparable. If the functions are only finite a.e., first delete a null set; if the limit equals $\pm\infty$ on a set of positive measure, then $|f_n-f|=+\infty$ there (or the difference is undefined), and uniform convergence is impossible.

For $j\ge1$ set $$A_{k,j}=\bigcup_{n\ge k}\Bigl\{|f_n-f|\ge\frac1j\Bigr\},\qquad k=1,2,\dots$$ Then $A_{k,j}$ decreases with $k$, and $\bigcap_k A_{k,j}=\{\limsup_n|f_n-f|\ge1/j\}$. Since $f_n\to f$ a.e., this intersection is null; since $\mu(X)<\infty$, upper continuity gives $\mu(A_{k,j})\to0\ (k\to\infty)$. Choose $k_j$ with $\mu(A_{k_j,j})<\varepsilon/2^{j+1}$ and put $E=\bigcup_j A_{k_j,j}$; then $$\mu(E)\le\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{j+1}}=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}<\varepsilon.$$ On $X\setminus E$, for every $j$ and all $n\ge k_j$ we have $|f_n-f|<1/j$; given $\eta>0$, choose $j>1/\eta$ to get uniform convergence.

Finite measure cannot be dropped. On $\mathbb{R}$ take $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$; then $f_n\to0$ everywhere. Suppose that after removing a set $E$, the sequence $f_n$ converges uniformly to $0$ on $G=\mathbb{R}\setminus E$. Then necessarily $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)\to0$. But for every $n$, $$m(G\cap[n,n+1))=1-m(E\cap[n,n+1))\ge1-m(E).$$ If $m(E)<1$, the right side is positive, so $G\cap[n,n+1)\ne\emptyset$ and hence $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)=1$ for all $n$, which cannot tend to $0$. Thus no exceptional set of measure less than $1$ works; Egorov's theorem fails when $\mu(\mathbb{R})=\infty$.

**Lusin's theorem.** Let $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be measurable with $m(E)<\infty$, and let $f:E\to\mathbb{R}$ be measurable. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a closed set $F\subset E$ such that $$m(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon,\qquad f|_F\ \text{is continuous}.$$ Continuity is relative to the subspace topology of $F$: only $f|_F$ is required to be continuous, not $f$ on all of $E$, and nothing is required on $E\setminus F$. The removed set can have arbitrarily small measure but is not guaranteed to be null; the theorem controls continuity only on $F$, not on the exceptional part. It also says nothing about uniform continuity of $f$ on $E$; if $F$ is compact, then $f|_F$ is automatically uniformly continuous (still only on $F$).

Proof idea: first choose simple functions $s_n\to f$ pointwise (with $|s_n|\le|f|$). Since $m(E)<\infty$, Egorov's theorem gives a measurable $G\subset E$ with $m(E\setminus G)<\varepsilon/2$ such that $s_n\to f$ uniformly on $G$. Each $s_n=\sum_i c_{n,i}\chi_{A_{n,i}}$ has finitely many level sets; by inner regularity of Lebesgue measure, for each $A_{n,i}\cap G$ choose a closed set $F_{n,i}\subset A_{n,i}\cap G$ so that $$m\bigl((A_{n,i}\cap G)\setminus F_{n,i}\bigr)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{n+1}N_n},$$ where $N_n$ is the number of level sets of $s_n$. Put $F_n=\bigcup_i F_{n,i}$; then $F_n$ is closed and $s_n|_{F_n}$ is continuous (constant on each $F_{n,i}$), and $m(G\setminus F_n)<\varepsilon/2^{n+1}$. Finally let $F=\bigcap_n F_n$; then $F$ is closed and $$m(E\setminus F)\le m(E\setminus G)+m(G\setminus F)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{n+1}}<\varepsilon.$$ All $s_n|_F$ are continuous, and $s_n\to f$ uniformly on $F$, so $f|_F$ is continuous.

Example and limitations: $D=\chi_{\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]}$ is measurable on $[0,1]$, which has finite measure. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose an open set $U\supset\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ with $m(U)<\min(\varepsilon,1)$ and set $F=[0,1]\setminus U$. Then $F$ is closed, $m([0,1]\setminus F)\le m(U)<\varepsilon$, and every point of $F$ is irrational, so $D|_F\equiv0$ is continuous. Yet $D$ is discontinuous at every point of $[0,1]$ (rationals and irrationals are both dense), so Lusin's conclusion cannot be strengthened to '$f$ is continuous on all of $E$'; the removed set generally has positive measure and depends on $\varepsilon$.

formulas.latex: \mu(X)<\infty,\quad f_n\to f\ \ \text{a.e.}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \forall\,\varepsilon>0\ \ \exists\,E\ \text{可测}:\ \mu(E)<\varepsilon,\quad f_n\rightrightarrows f\ \ \text{在}\ X\setminus E\ \text{上}
formulas.note: 叶戈罗夫定理：前提是 $\mu(X)<\infty$，结论是去掉测度小于 $\varepsilon$ 的集合后一致收敛（$\rightrightarrows$ 记一致收敛）。
formulas.noteEn: Egorov's theorem: the hypothesis is $\mu(X)<\infty$; the conclusion is uniform convergence ($\rightrightarrows$) off a set of measure less than $\varepsilon$.

formulas.latex: \mu(E)<\infty,\ \ f\ \text{可测 on}\ E:\quad \forall\,\varepsilon>0\ \ \exists\,F\subset E\ \text{闭}:\ \mu(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon,\ \ f|_F\ \text{连续}
formulas.note: 鲁津定理（近似连续）：可测函数在去掉任意小测度集（取闭集 $F$）后连续。
formulas.noteEn: Lusin's theorem (approximate continuity): after deleting a set of arbitrarily small measure, a measurable function is continuous on the remaining closed set $F$.

formulas.note: 鲁津定理的逆：近似连续是可测性的等价刻画（在有限测度集上）。
formulas.noteEn: Converse of Lusin: approximate continuity is an equivalent description of measurability (on sets of finite measure).

formulas.latex: f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}\ \ \text{on}\ \mathbb{R}:\qquad f_n\to 0\ \ \text{处处},\qquad \text{但}\ f_n\ \text{不是几乎一致收敛}
formulas.note: 反例：说明叶戈罗夫定理中「有限测度」条件不可省——在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上无论去掉怎样小的集合，都无法获得一致收敛。
formulas.noteEn: Counterexample: the 'finite measure' hypothesis in Egorov's theorem is essential; on $\mathbb{R}$ no small removal yields uniform convergence.

properties: 叶戈罗夫定理中**有限测度条件不可省**：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，则 $f_n\to 0$ 处处成立；但若「好集合」$G$ 满足 $\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)<1$，则 $\mu(G\cap[n,n+1))\ge 1-\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)>0$，于是 $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)=1$ 对一切 $n$ 成立，$f_n$ 在 $G$ 上不可能一致收敛。
鲁津定理可加强：在欧氏空间中可取 $F$ 为**紧集**；并且 $f|_F$ 可延拓成整个 $\mathbb{R}$ 上的连续函数（蒂策延拓定理）。
鲁津定理是可测性的刻画：函数近似连续 $\iff$ 函数可测（在有限测度集上），因此它既给出构造，也给出判别法。

在有限测度空间上，几乎处处收敛与几乎一致收敛**等价**：叶戈罗夫定理给出一半；另一半是——若对每个 $k$ 存在例外集 $E_k$（$\mu(E_k)<1/k$）使 $f_n$ 在 $X\setminus E_k$ 上一致收敛，则交集 $N=\bigcap_k E_k$ 满足 $\mu(N)\le\mu(E_k)<1/k$（对一切 $k$），故是零测集；且对每个 $x\notin N$ 存在某个 $k$ 使 $x\notin E_k$，从而 $f_n(x)\to f(x)$，即 $f_n\to f$ 几乎处处收敛。
概率语言：概率空间满足 $\mu(\Omega)=1<\infty$，所以随机变量序列的几乎必然收敛自动是几乎一致收敛——这是概率论中可以直接使用叶戈罗夫型结论的原因。
propertiesEn: The finite-measure hypothesis in Egorov's theorem cannot be dropped: on $\mathbb{R}$ take $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$, then $f_n\to0$ everywhere; but if a set $G$ satisfies $\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)<1$, then $\mu(G\cap[n,n+1))\ge 1-\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)>0$, so $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)=1$ for every $n$ and uniform convergence on $G$ is impossible.
Lusin's theorem can be strengthened: in Euclidean space $F$ may be taken compact, and $f|_F$ extends to a continuous function on all of $\mathbb{R}$ (Tietze extension theorem).
Lusin's theorem characterizes measurability: a function is approximately continuous if and only if it is measurable (on sets of finite measure).

On finite measure spaces a.e. convergence and almost uniform convergence are equivalent: Egorov gives one direction; for the other, if for every $k$ there is an exceptional set $E_k$ with $\mu(E_k)<1/k$ such that $f_n$ converges uniformly on $X\setminus E_k$, then $N=\bigcap_k E_k$ is a null set, and for every $x\notin N$ there is some $k$ with $x\notin E_k$, so $f_n(x)\to f(x)$; hence $f_n\to f$ a.e.
In probabilistic language: a probability space has $\mu(\Omega)=1<\infty$, so almost sure convergence of random variables is automatically almost uniform convergence.

examples.problem: （有限测度条件不能省）在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上定义 $f_n(x)=\chi_{[n,n+1)}(x)$。验证 $f_n\to 0$ 对每个 $x$ 成立，但不成立几乎一致收敛，说明叶戈罗夫定理中 $\mu(X)<\infty$ 不可去掉。
examples.solution: 逐点收敛：固定 $x$，当 $n>x$ 时 $x\notin[n,n+1)$，所以 $f_n(x)=0$，即 $f_n\to 0$ 处处成立。设 $G\subset\mathbb{R}$ 是任意一个「好集合」，假设 $f_n$ 在 $G$ 上一致收敛到 0，则必须有 $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)\to 0$。但若 $\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)<1$，则对每个 $n$ 都有 $\mu(G\cap[n,n+1))\ge 1-\mu(\mathbb{R}\setminus G)>0$，特别地 $G\cap[n,n+1)\neq\varnothing$，从而 $\sup_{x\in G}f_n(x)=1$ 对一切 $n$ 成立，矛盾。所以不可能通过去掉测度小于 1 的集合得到一致收敛：叶戈罗夫定理在 $\mu(\mathbb{R})=\infty$ 时确实失效。

examples.problem: （鲁津定理的操作）设 $D(x)=\chi_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)$ 是 $[0,1]$ 上的 Dirichlet 函数。对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，找出闭集 $F\subset[0,1]$ 使 $\mu([0,1]\setminus F)<\varepsilon$ 且 $D|_F$ 连续。
examples.solution: $\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ 是可数集，因而是零测集。取开集 $U\supset\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ 使 $\mu(U)<\varepsilon$（例如用总长度小于 $\varepsilon$ 的一列开区间覆盖每个有理点），令 $F=[0,1]\setminus U$。则 $F$ 是闭集，$\mu([0,1]\setminus F)=\mu(U)<\varepsilon$，并且 $F$ 中全部是无理数，$D|_F\equiv 0$ 是常函数，当然连续。这正是鲁津定理的内容：处处不连续的 Dirichlet 函数，在去掉任意小（这里甚至总测度小于 $\varepsilon$）的集合后变得连续。

expression.text: f_n → f（a.e.）⇒ f_n ⇉ f（a.u.，需 μ(X)<∞）
expression.note: 叶戈罗夫：有限测度下几乎处处收敛升级为几乎一致收敛；鲁津：可测函数的近似连续性。
expression.noteEn: Egorov: on finite measure spaces a.e. convergence upgrades to almost uniform convergence; Lusin: measurable functions are approximately continuous.

lebesgue-integral.definition:
勒贝格积分的定义分三步。**第一步**，对**非负简单函数** $s=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i}$（$a_i\ge 0$，$A_i$ 是互不相交的可测集）直接定义 $\int s\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i)$：这不过是「高度 × 测度」的加和，可以理解成按值域分层求面积。**第二步**，对**非负可测函数** $f$，用所有从下方不超过它的简单函数去逼近，取上确界：$\int f\,d\mu=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: 0\le s\le f,\ s\ \text{简单}\}$。这个上确界总是有定义的（取 $s\equiv 0$ 即可），允许等于 $+\infty$。

**第三步**处理**一般可测函数**。把 $f$ 分解为正部与负部：$f=f^+-f^-$，其中 $f^+=\max(f,0)$，$f^-=\max(-f,0)$。当 $\int f^+$ 与 $\int f^-$ **不同时为 $+\infty$** 时，定义 $\int f\,d\mu=\int f^+d\mu-\int f^-d\mu$；若二者都是 $+\infty$，积分无定义（避免 $\infty-\infty$）。当 $\int|f|\,d\mu=\int f^++\int f^-<+\infty$ 时，称 $f$ 为**勒贝格可积**，记 $f\in L^1(\mu)$，此时 $\int f$ 是有限实数。也就是说：**勒贝格可积 $\iff \int|f|<\infty$**。

与黎曼积分「划分定义域」不同，勒贝格积分「划分值域」：先问「函数值落在第 $k$ 层的点集有多大」，再乘以层高求和。这让它对病态函数同样有效——例如 Dirichlet 函数 $\chi_{\mathbb{Q}}$ 黎曼不可积，但作为简单函数立刻得到勒贝格积分为 $\mu(\mathbb{Q})=0$。勒贝格积分还带来完备性（$L^1$ 是完备空间）和强大的极限定理（单调收敛、控制收敛），这是它取代黎曼积分成为现代分析基石的根本原因。
lebesgue-integral.definitionEn:
The Lebesgue integral is built in three steps. **Step 1**: for a **nonnegative simple function** $s=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i}$ (with $a_i\ge0$ and the $A_i$ pairwise disjoint measurable sets) define $\int s\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i)$; this is just 'height times measure', a layered area. **Step 2**: for a **nonnegative measurable function** $f$, approximate from below by simple functions and take the supremum: $\int f\,d\mu=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: 0\le s\le f,\ s\ \text{simple}\}$. This supremum always exists (take $s\equiv0$) and may equal $+\infty$.

**Step 3** handles a **general measurable function**. Split it into positive and negative parts: $f=f^+-f^-$ with $f^+=\max(f,0)$, $f^-=\max(-f,0)$. When $\int f^+$ and $\int f^-$ are **not both $+\infty$**, define $\int f\,d\mu=\int f^+d\mu-\int f^-d\mu$; if both are $+\infty$ the integral is undefined (to avoid $\infty-\infty$). If $\int|f|\,d\mu=\int f^++\int f^-<+\infty$, then $f$ is called **Lebesgue integrable**, written $f\in L^1(\mu)$, and $\int f$ is a finite real number. Equivalently, **$f$ is integrable $\iff \int|f|<\infty$**.

Unlike the Riemann integral, which partitions the domain, the Lebesgue integral partitions the range: it asks how large the set is on which the values fall in a given layer, then adds height times measure. That is why it handles pathological functions: the Dirichlet function $\chi_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is not Riemann integrable, yet as a simple function it has Lebesgue integral $\mu(\mathbb{Q})=0$. Together with completeness of $L^1$ and powerful limit theorems (monotone and dominated convergence), this is why the Lebesgue integral replaced the Riemann integral as the foundation of modern analysis.
derivation: 定义分三层。第一层：对非负简单函数 $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad a_i\ge0,\quad A_i\ \text{两两不交可测},$$ 其中 $\bigcup_i A_i=X$。令 $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i),$$ 约定 $0\cdot\infty=0$。这就是「高度 $\times$ 测度」的有限和：$\varphi$ 在第 $i$ 层取高度 $a_i$，该层的测度是 $\mu(A_i)$。若 $\varphi=\chi_A$，则 $\int\varphi=\mu(A)$。

这个定义不依赖分解。若 $\varphi=\sum_i a_i\chi_{A_i}=\sum_j b_j\chi_{B_j}$，取公共加细 $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$。在非空 $C_{ij}$ 上 $a_i=b_j$，且 $\mu(A_i)=\sum_j\mu(C_{ij})$、$\mu(B_j)=\sum_i\mu(C_{ij})$（有限可加性）。于是 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_i a_i\mu(A_i)&=\sum_{i,j}a_i\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\sum_{i,j}b_j\mu(C_{ij})=\sum_j b_j\mu(B_j),\end{aligned}$$ 在 $[0,\infty]$ 中成立。零高度的块即使测度为 $\infty$ 也只按 $0\cdot\infty=0$ 贡献 $0$，所以不会因零高度块产生未定义项。故简单函数的积分良定义。

第二层：对非负可测 $f$，定义 $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\sup\Bigl\{\int_X\varphi\,d\mu:\ 0\le\varphi\le f,\ \varphi\ \text{简单}\Bigr\}.$$ 集合非空（含 $\varphi\equiv0$），上确界在 $[0,\infty]$ 中存在，允许为 $+\infty$。若 $f$ 本身是非负简单函数，则 $\varphi=f$ 本身就在集合中，且对任何 $0\le\varphi\le f$ 由简单函数积分的单调性（公共加细逐块比较）有 $\int\varphi\le\int f$，故上确界恰为 $\int f$。这说明第二层与第一层相容。

第三层：对一般可测 $f$，写 $$f=f^+-f^-,\qquad f^+=\max(f,0),\quad f^-=\max(-f,0),$$ 其中 $f^+,f^-\ge0$ 可测，$|f|=f^++f^-$。若 $\int f^+$ 与 $\int f^-$ 不同时为 $+\infty$，定义 $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\int_X f^+d\mu-\int_X f^-d\mu;$$ 若二者都为 $+\infty$，则积分无定义（避免 $\infty-\infty$）。当 $$\int_X|f|\,d\mu=\int_X f^+d\mu+\int_X f^-d\mu<+\infty$$ 时，称 $f$ 为**勒贝格可积**，记 $f\in L^1(\mu)$；此时积分是有限实数。反之，若积分是有限实数，则两个正负部积分都有限，故 $f\in L^1$。

非负积分的一个基本判据：若 $f\ge0$ 可测，则 $$\int_X f\,d\mu=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f=0\ \text{a.e.}$$ 证明：若积分为 $0$，对 $n\ge1$ 令 $E_n=\{f>1/n\}$。则 $\frac1n\chi_{E_n}\le f$，由定义得 $\int_X f\,d\mu\ge\frac1n\mu(E_n)$。若 $\mu(E_n)>0$，右边为正，与 $\int_X f\,d\mu=0$ 矛盾，故 $\mu(E_n)=0$；而 $\{f>0\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}E_n$，故 $f=0$ a.e.。反过来，若 $f=0$ a.e.，则任何 $0\le\varphi\le f$ 的简单函数也 a.e. 为 $0$，其积分为 $0$，取上确界得 $\int f=0$。

由定义（并用简单函数逼近）得到几条常用性质。**线性**：若 $f,g\in L^1$，$\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$，则 $\alpha f+\beta g\in L^1$ 且 $$\int_X(\alpha f+\beta g)\,d\mu=\alpha\int_X f\,d\mu+\beta\int_X g\,d\mu.$$ 证明先用非负简单函数的 $\sum a_i\mu(A_i)$ 验证，再对非负可测函数用单调收敛定理逼近，最后拆正负部；可积性保证所有项有限。对非负可测函数，线性对 $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ 成立并允许 $+\infty$。**单调性**：$f\le g$ a.e. 时 $\int f\le\int g$（非负可测情形允许 $+\infty$；$L^1$ 情形为有限实数）。**a.e. 修改**：当积分有定义时，$f=g$ a.e. 蕴含积分相等，特别地零测集上的值不影响积分；并且对 $f\in L^1$ 有 $\bigl|\int f\bigr|\le\int|f|$。这些性质说明积分只依赖函数的 a.e. 等价类。
derivationEn: The definition has three layers. First layer: for a nonnegative simple function $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad a_i\ge0,\quad A_i\ \text{pairwise disjoint and measurable},$$ where $\bigcup_i A_i=X$; set $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\mu(A_i),$$ with the convention $0\cdot\infty=0$. This is the finite sum 'height times measure': $\varphi$ has height $a_i$ on layer $A_i$, whose measure is $\mu(A_i)$. For $\varphi=\chi_A$ this gives $\int\varphi=\mu(A)$.

The definition does not depend on the decomposition. If $\varphi=\sum_i a_i\chi_{A_i}=\sum_j b_j\chi_{B_j}$, take the common refinement $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$. On every nonempty $C_{ij}$, $a_i=b_j$, and $\mu(A_i)=\sum_j\mu(C_{ij})$, $\mu(B_j)=\sum_i\mu(C_{ij})$ by finite additivity. Hence $$\begin{aligned}\sum_i a_i\mu(A_i)&=\sum_{i,j}a_i\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\sum_{i,j}b_j\mu(C_{ij})=\sum_j b_j\mu(B_j),\end{aligned}$$ with equality in $[0,\infty]$. A zero-height piece contributes $0$ even if its measure is $\infty$, by $0\cdot\infty=0$, so such pieces do not create undefined terms. Thus the simple integral is well defined.

Second layer: for a nonnegative measurable $f$, define $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\sup\Bigl\{\int_X\varphi\,d\mu:\ 0\le\varphi\le f,\ \varphi\ \text{simple}\Bigr\}.$$ The set is nonempty (it contains $\varphi\equiv0$), and the supremum exists in $[0,\infty]$, possibly equal to $+\infty$. If $f$ is itself nonnegative simple, then $\varphi=f$ is admissible, and for every $0\le\varphi\le f$ monotonicity of the simple integral (compare on a common refinement) gives $\int\varphi\le\int f$; hence the supremum equals $\int f$. Thus the second layer is consistent with the first.

Third layer: for a general measurable $f$, write $$f=f^+-f^-,\qquad f^+=\max(f,0),\quad f^-=\max(-f,0),$$ where $f^+,f^-\ge0$ are measurable and $|f|=f^++f^-$. If $\int f^+$ and $\int f^-$ are not both $+\infty$, define $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\int_X f^+d\mu-\int_X f^-d\mu;$$ if both are $+\infty$, the integral is undefined (to avoid $\infty-\infty$). When $$\int_X|f|\,d\mu=\int_X f^+d\mu+\int_X f^-d\mu<+\infty,$$ $f$ is called **Lebesgue integrable**, written $f\in L^1(\mu)$; then the integral is a finite real number. Conversely, if the integral is a finite real number, both parts are finite, so $f\in L^1$.

A basic criterion for nonnegative integrals: if $f\ge0$ is measurable, then $$\int_X f\,d\mu=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f=0\ \text{a.e.}$$ Proof: if the integral is $0$, for $n\ge1$ let $E_n=\{f>1/n\}$. Then $\frac1n\chi_{E_n}\le f$, so by definition $\int_X f\,d\mu\ge\frac1n\mu(E_n)$. If $\mu(E_n)>0$, the right side is positive, contradicting $\int_X f\,d\mu=0$; hence $\mu(E_n)=0$; since $\{f>0\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}E_n$, we get $f=0$ a.e. Conversely, if $f=0$ a.e., every simple $0\le\varphi\le f$ vanishes a.e., so its integral is $0$; taking the supremum gives $\int f=0$.

Several standard properties follow from the definition (using simple approximation). **Linearity**: if $f,g\in L^1$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha f+\beta g\in L^1$ and $$\int_X(\alpha f+\beta g)\,d\mu=\alpha\int_X f\,d\mu+\beta\int_X g\,d\mu.$$ Prove it first for nonnegative simple functions via $\sum a_i\mu(A_i)$, then for nonnegative measurable functions by monotone convergence, and finally split into positive and negative parts; integrability keeps all terms finite. For nonnegative measurable functions, linearity holds for $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ and allows $+\infty$. **Monotonicity**: if $f\le g$ a.e., then $\int f\le\int g$ (for nonnegative measurable functions $+\infty$ is allowed; on $L^1$ the values are finite). **A.e. modification**: when the integrals are defined, $f=g$ a.e. implies equality; in particular, values on a null set do not affect the integral. Also, for $f\in L^1$, $\bigl|\int f\bigr|\le\int|f|$. These properties show that the integral depends only on the a.e. equivalence class of the function.

formulas.latex: \int_X f\,d\mu=\sup\Bigl\{\int_X s\,d\mu:\ 0\le s\le f,\ s\ \text{简单函数}\Bigr\}
formulas.note: 非负可测函数的勒贝格积分：用不超过 $f$ 的非负简单函数从下方逼近，取上确界（允许 $+\infty$）。
formulas.noteEn: Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative measurable function: the supremum of integrals of nonnegative simple functions below $f$ (value $+\infty$ allowed).

formulas.note: 简单函数的积分：把每层的「高度 × 测度」相加；这是整个定义的起点。
formulas.noteEn: Integral of a simple function: add 'height times measure' over the layers; this is the starting point of the definition.

formulas.latex: f=f^+-f^-,\qquad \int_X f\,d\mu=\int_X f^+d\mu-\int_X f^-d\mu\qquad(\text{两项不同时为}\ \infty)
formulas.note: 一般可测函数的积分 = 正部积分 − 负部积分；要求两项不同时为 $+\infty$，否则出现无意义的 $\infty-\infty$。
formulas.noteEn: General measurable functions: integral = (integral of positive part) − (integral of negative part); the two terms must not both be $+\infty$.

formulas.note: **勒贝格可积 $\iff$ $|f|$ 的积分有限**；此时 $\int f$ 是有限实数，且 $\bigl|\int f\bigr|\le\int|f|$。
formulas.noteEn: $f$ is Lebesgue integrable iff $\int|f|<\infty$; then $\int f$ is a finite real number with $\bigl|\int f\bigr|\le\int|f|$.

formulas.note: 定义自洽性：用任意递增简单函数列逼近 $f$，积分极限都相同（证明依赖单调收敛定理）。
formulas.noteEn: Consistency of the definition: any increasing sequence of simple functions with $s_n\uparrow f$ has integrals converging to $\int f$ (the proof uses monotone convergence).

properties: 非负可测函数的积分永远有定义，取值于 $[0,+\infty]$：不需要有限性，也不会出现 $\infty-\infty$。
两种定义一致：对非负可测 $f$，若 $0\le s_n\uparrow f$（$s_n$ 简单），则 $\int f=\lim_n\int s_n$——上确界定义与逼近极限定义等价。
可积性即绝对可积性：$f\in L^1\iff\int|f|<+\infty$；此时积分值有限。一般可测函数的积分可以有定义却为 $+\infty$（例如 $f=1$ 于 $\mathbb{R}$），但那时 $f\notin L^1$。
有界加有限测度保证可积：若 $\mu(X)<\infty$ 且 $f$ 可测有界（$|f|\le M$），则 $\int|f|\le M\mu(X)<\infty$，故 $f\in L^1$。
若 $f$ 可测且 $\int|f|<\infty$，则 $|f|<+\infty$ 几乎处处：可积函数不可能在正测度集上取无穷值。
propertiesEn: For a nonnegative measurable function the integral is always defined, with values in $[0,+\infty]$; no finiteness is needed and $\infty-\infty$ never arises.
The two presentations agree: if $0\le s_n\uparrow f$ with $s_n$ simple, then $\int f=\lim_n\int s_n$; the supremum definition equals the limit of increasing approximations.

Integrability is absolute integrability: $f\in L^1\iff\int|f|<+\infty$, and then the integral is finite. A general measurable function may have a well-defined integral equal to $+\infty$ (e.g. $f=1$ on $\mathbb{R}$) while not being in $L^1$.
Boundedness plus finite measure implies integrability: if $\mu(X)<\infty$ and $f$ is measurable with $|f|\le M$, then $\int|f|\le M\mu(X)<\infty$ and $f\in L^1$.
If $f$ is measurable and $\int|f|<\infty$, then $|f|<+\infty$ almost everywhere: an integrable function cannot take the value infinity on a set of positive measure.

examples.solution: $f$ 是非负简单函数。按取值分层：$f=2$ 于 $[0,\tfrac12)$，$f=5$ 于 $[\tfrac12,1]$，$f=3$ 于 $(1,2]$。于是 $\int_{[0,2]}f\,d\mu=2\cdot\mu([0,\tfrac12))+5\cdot\mu([\tfrac12,1])+3\cdot\mu((1,2])=2\cdot\tfrac12+5\cdot\tfrac12+3\cdot1=\tfrac{13}{2}$。也可以直接用简单函数公式：$\int f=2\mu([0,1])+3\mu([1/2,2])=2+3\cdot\tfrac32=\tfrac{13}{2}$，两种算法一致。

examples.problem: 计算 Dirichlet 函数 $D=\chi_{\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]}$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上的勒贝格积分，并说明它黎曼不可积。
examples.solution: $D$ 是非负简单函数：在 $A=\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ 上取 1，在 $A^c$ 上取 0。故 $\int_{[0,1]}D\,d\mu=1\cdot\mu(A)+0\cdot\mu(A^c)=0$，因为可数集 $A$ 是零测集。另一方面，$D$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上处处不连续，不连续点集测度为 1，由勒贝格判据（见「黎曼积分与勒贝格积分的关系」）黎曼不可积。这说明勒贝格积分的适用函数类严格大于黎曼积分。

expression.text: ∫_X f dμ = sup{ ∫_X s dμ : 0 ≤ s ≤ f，s 为简单函数 }
expression.note: 先定义非负情形（上确界），再用 f=f⁺−f⁻ 推广到一般可测函数；∫|f|<∞ 时可积。
expression.noteEn: Define the nonnegative case as a supremum, then extend via f=f⁺−f⁻ to general measurable functions; integrable means ∫|f|<∞.

integral-properties.definition:
勒贝格积分的全部使用技巧都建立在几条基本性质上：**线性**、**（几乎处处的）单调性**、**三角不等式**与**零测集无关性**。它们把积分从一个抽象定义变成可以计算、可以估计的对象。使用时要注意函数所处的层次。

对**非负可测函数**：线性对非负系数成立，单调性无条件成立，等式两边允许是 $+\infty$。对 $L^1$ 中的**可积函数**：线性对任意实数系数成立，且 $|\int f|\le\int|f|$ 保证积分值是有限实数。两种情形的前提都是避免 $\infty-\infty$——可积性（$\int|f|<\infty$）正是为保证所有运算都有意义而设的安全条件。

「零测集无关性」是最能体现勒贝格积分特点的一条：函数在零测集上取什么值完全不影响积分。因此讨论 $L^1$ 函数时人们习惯把几乎处处相等的函数视为同一个对象，这正是 $L^p$ 空间理论的出发点。一个常用推论是：非负可测函数的积分为 0 当且仅当它几乎处处为 0。
integral-properties.definitionEn:
All working rules of the Lebesgue integral rest on a few basic properties: **linearity**, **(almost everywhere) monotonicity**, the **triangle inequality**, and **independence of null sets**. They turn the integral from an abstract definition into a computable and estimable object.

For a **nonnegative measurable function**: linearity holds for nonnegative coefficients, monotonicity is unconditional, and both sides may equal $+\infty$. For an **integrable function** in $L^1$: linearity holds for arbitrary real coefficients, and $|\int f|\le\int|f|$ guarantees a finite real value. In both cases the point is to avoid $\infty-\infty$; integrability ($\int|f|<\infty$) is exactly the safety condition that keeps every operation meaningful.

Independence of null sets is the most characteristic Lebesgue property: the values a function takes on a null set do not affect the integral at all. Hence one identifies functions that are equal almost everywhere, which is the starting point of $L^p$ space theory. A standard corollary: a nonnegative measurable function has integral zero if and only if it vanishes almost everywhere.
derivation: 所有性质都从简单函数这一层开始。设 $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad \psi=\sum_{j=1}^{m}b_j\chi_{B_j}$$ 是非负简单函数，$a_i,b_j\ge0$，两组集合各自两两不交且并集为 $X$。取公共加细 $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$，则 $$\alpha\varphi+\beta\psi=\sum_{i,j}(\alpha a_i+\beta b_j)\chi_{C_{ij}},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0.$$ 于是 $$\begin{aligned}\int(\alpha\varphi+\beta\psi)&=\sum_{i,j}(\alpha a_i+\beta b_j)\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\alpha\int\varphi+\beta\int\psi,\end{aligned}$$ 且若 $\varphi\le\psi$，则每个非空 $C_{ij}$ 上 $a_i\le b_j$，故 $\int\varphi\le\int\psi$。这给出线性与单调性的底层情形（在 $[0,\infty]$ 中，约定 $0\cdot\infty=0$）。

对非负可测 $f,g$ 与 $\alpha,\beta\ge0$，有 $$\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g,$$ 两边允许 $+\infty$。证明：取非负简单函数 $\varphi_n\uparrow f$、$\psi_n\uparrow g$（简单函数逼近定理）。则 $\alpha\varphi_n+\beta\psi_n$ 是非负简单函数且单调递增到 $\alpha f+\beta g$。由单调收敛定理，$$\begin{aligned}\int(\alpha f+\beta g)&=\lim_n\int(\alpha\varphi_n+\beta\psi_n)\\&=\lim_n\Bigl(\alpha\int\varphi_n+\beta\int\psi_n\Bigr)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g.\end{aligned}$$ 这里若 $\alpha=0$ 而 $\int f=+\infty$，按 $0\cdot\infty=0$ 理解；等式仍然成立。

对 $f,g\in L^1$ 与任意 $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$，有 $\alpha f+\beta g\in L^1$ 且 $$\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g.$$ 先由 $$|\alpha f+\beta g|\le|\alpha||f|+|\beta||g|$$ 知左边可积。再化归非负情形：对 $\alpha\ge0$，$(\alpha f)^+=\alpha f^+$、$(\alpha f)^-=\alpha f^-$，故 $\int\alpha f=\alpha\int f$；对 $\alpha<0$，正负部互换，结论相同。最后设 $h=f+g$。由 $h^+-h^-=f^+-f^-+g^+-g^-$ 移项得 $$h^++f^-+g^-=h^-+f^++g^+.$$ 六项都非负可测且积分有限，对两边用非负线性性并减去有限积分，即得 $\int h=\int f+\int g$。合并两步即得一般线性。

**零积分判据与 a.e. 不变性**：若 $f\ge0$ 可测，则 $$\int_X f\,d\mu=0\iff f=0\ \text{a.e.}$$ 若积分为 $0$，对 $n\ge1$ 令 $E_n=\{f>1/n\}$。由 $\frac1n\chi_{E_n}\le f$ 与上确界定义得 $\int f\ge\frac1n\mu(E_n)$。若 $\mu(E_n)>0$，右边为正，与 $\int f=0$ 矛盾，故 $\mu(E_n)=0$；而 $\{f>0\}=\bigcup_n E_n$，故 $f=0$ a.e.。反之，若 $f=0$ a.e.，任何简单 $0\le\varphi\le f$ 也 a.e. 为 $0$，故 $\int\varphi=0$，取上确界得 $\int f=0$。由此，若 $f=g$ a.e. 且积分有定义，则 $\int f=\int g$：对非负情形，任取简单 $\varphi\le f$，在 $\{f=g\}$ 外把它改为 $0$，得到 $\varphi'\le g$ 且 $\int\varphi'=\int\varphi$，故 $\int f\le\int g$，对称得等号；一般情形对正负部分分别应用。特别地，零测集上的值不影响积分。

**单调性**：若 $f\le g$ a.e.，则 $\int f\le\int g$（非负可测情形允许 $+\infty$；$L^1$ 情形为有限实数）。非负情形：对任意简单 $0\le\varphi\le f$，令 $N=\{f>g\}$，则 $\mu(N)=0$，$\varphi'=\varphi\chi_{N^c}$ 是简单函数，$\varphi'\le g$ 且 $\int\varphi'=\int\varphi$（只改动了零测集），故 $\int\varphi\le\int g$；对 $\varphi$ 取上确界得 $\int f\le\int g$。$L^1$ 情形：令 $h=(g-f)\chi_{\{f\le g\}}$，则 $h\ge0$ 且 $h=g-f$ a.e.；由 a.e. 不变性与线性性，$\int h=\int(g-f)=\int g-\int f\ge0$。**三角不等式**：由 $-|f|\le f\le|f|$ 与单调性，$$-\int|f|\le\int f\le\int|f|,\qquad \Bigl|\int f\Bigr|\le\int|f|.$$

**区域可加性**：若 $A,B$ 可测且不交，$f$ 在 $A\cup B$ 上可积（或 $f\ge0$ 可测），则 $$\int_{A\cup B}f\,d\mu=\int_A f\,d\mu+\int_B f\,d\mu.$$ 理由：$f\chi_{A\cup B}=f\chi_A+f\chi_B$ 处处成立，且三个积分都有定义（非负情形允许 $+\infty$，$L^1$ 情形有限）；由线性性即得。由此，若 $N$ 零测，则 $\int_N f=0$；若 $A\subset E$ 且 $\mu(E\setminus A)=0$，则 $\int_E f=\int_A f$。另外，$f\in L^1$ 必有 $|f|<+\infty$ a.e.：否则在正测度集 $P$ 上 $|f|=\infty$，则 $\int|f|\ge n\mu(P)$ 对一切 $n$ 成立，迫使 $\int|f|=\infty$。最后，若 $\mu(E)<\infty$ 且 $|f|\le M$ a.e.（$M<\infty$），则 $\int_E|f|\le M\mu(E)<\infty$，故 $f\in L^1(E)$。
derivationEn: All properties start at the level of simple functions. Let $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\chi_{A_i},\qquad \psi=\sum_{j=1}^{m}b_j\chi_{B_j}$$ be nonnegative simple functions, $a_i,b_j\ge0$, with each family pairwise disjoint and covering $X$. Take the common refinement $C_{ij}=A_i\cap B_j$. Then $$\alpha\varphi+\beta\psi=\sum_{i,j}(\alpha a_i+\beta b_j)\chi_{C_{ij}},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0.$$ Hence $$\begin{aligned}\int(\alpha\varphi+\beta\psi)&=\sum_{i,j}(\alpha a_i+\beta b_j)\mu(C_{ij})\\&=\alpha\int\varphi+\beta\int\psi,\end{aligned}$$ and if $\varphi\le\psi$, then $a_i\le b_j$ on every nonempty $C_{ij}$, so $\int\varphi\le\int\psi$. This gives the base case of linearity and monotonicity (in $[0,\infty]$, with $0\cdot\infty=0$).

For nonnegative measurable $f,g$ and $\alpha,\beta\ge0$, $$\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g,$$ with both sides allowed to be $+\infty$. Proof: choose nonnegative simple functions $\varphi_n\uparrow f$ and $\psi_n\uparrow g$ (simple approximation theorem). Then $\alpha\varphi_n+\beta\psi_n$ is nonnegative simple and increases to $\alpha f+\beta g$. By monotone convergence, $$\begin{aligned}\int(\alpha f+\beta g)&=\lim_n\int(\alpha\varphi_n+\beta\psi_n)\\&=\lim_n\Bigl(\alpha\int\varphi_n+\beta\int\psi_n\Bigr)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g.\end{aligned}$$ If $\alpha=0$ and $\int f=+\infty$, interpret $0\cdot\infty=0$; the identity still holds.

For $f,g\in L^1$ and arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, we have $\alpha f+\beta g\in L^1$ and $$\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g.$$ First, $$|\alpha f+\beta g|\le|\alpha||f|+|\beta||g|$$ shows integrability. Reduce to the nonnegative case: for $\alpha\ge0$, $(\alpha f)^+=\alpha f^+$ and $(\alpha f)^-=\alpha f^-$, so $\int\alpha f=\alpha\int f$; for $\alpha<0$ the positive and negative parts are interchanged, with the same conclusion. Finally let $h=f+g$. From $h^+-h^-=f^+-f^-+g^+-g^-$ we rearrange to $$h^++f^-+g^-=h^-+f^++g^+.$$ All six terms are nonnegative measurable with finite integrals; applying nonnegative linearity and subtracting the finite integrals gives $\int h=\int f+\int g$. Combining the two steps yields full linearity.

**Zero-integral criterion and a.e. invariance.** If $f\ge0$ is measurable, then $$\int_X f\,d\mu=0\iff f=0\ \text{a.e.}$$ If the integral is $0$, set $E_n=\{f>1/n\}$ for $n\ge1$. Since $\frac1n\chi_{E_n}\le f$, the definition of the supremum gives $\int f\ge\frac1n\mu(E_n)$. If $\mu(E_n)>0$, the right side is positive, contradicting $\int f=0$; hence $\mu(E_n)=0$; since $\{f>0\}=\bigcup_n E_n$, $f=0$ a.e. Conversely, if $f=0$ a.e., every simple $0\le\varphi\le f$ vanishes a.e., so $\int\varphi=0$, and the supremum is $0$. Consequently, if $f=g$ a.e. and the integrals are defined, then $\int f=\int g$: in the nonnegative case, given simple $\varphi\le f$, modify it to $0$ off $\{f=g\}$ to get $\varphi'\le g$ with $\int\varphi'=\int\varphi$; hence $\int f\le\int g$, and symmetry gives equality; the general case applies this to positive and negative parts. In particular, values on a null set do not affect the integral.

**Monotonicity**: if $f\le g$ a.e., then $\int f\le\int g$ (for nonnegative measurable functions $+\infty$ is allowed; on $L^1$ the values are finite). Nonnegative case: for every simple $0\le\varphi\le f$, let $N=\{f>g\}$; then $\mu(N)=0$, $\varphi'=\varphi\chi_{N^c}$ is simple, $\varphi'\le g$, and $\int\varphi'=\int\varphi$ (only a null set was changed), so $\int\varphi\le\int g$; taking the supremum over $\varphi$ gives $\int f\le\int g$. $L^1$ case: let $h=(g-f)\chi_{\{f\le g\}}$; then $h\ge0$ and $h=g-f$ a.e.; by a.e. invariance and linearity, $\int h=\int(g-f)=\int g-\int f\ge0$. **Triangle inequality**: from $-|f|\le f\le|f|$ and monotonicity, $$-\int|f|\le\int f\le\int|f|,\qquad \Bigl|\int f\Bigr|\le\int|f|.$$

**Additivity over regions**: if $A,B$ are measurable and disjoint and $f$ is integrable on $A\cup B$ (or $f\ge0$ is measurable), then $$\int_{A\cup B}f\,d\mu=\int_A f\,d\mu+\int_B f\,d\mu.$$ Reason: $f\chi_{A\cup B}=f\chi_A+f\chi_B$ everywhere, and all three integrals are defined (possibly $+\infty$ in the nonnegative case, finite in the $L^1$ case); linearity gives the identity. Consequently, if $N$ is null, then $\int_N f=0$; if $A\subset E$ and $\mu(E\setminus A)=0$, then $\int_E f=\int_A f$. Also, $f\in L^1$ implies $|f|<+\infty$ a.e.: otherwise $|f|=\infty$ on a set $P$ of positive measure, and $\int|f|\ge n\mu(P)$ for every $n$, forcing $\int|f|=\infty$. Finally, if $\mu(E)<\infty$ and $|f|\le M$ a.e. with $M<\infty$, then $\int_E|f|\le M\mu(E)<\infty$, so $f\in L^1(E)$.

formulas.note: 线性（可积情形，任意实系数）；对非负可测函数只需 $\alpha,\beta\ge0$，两边允许 $+\infty$。
formulas.noteEn: Linearity for integrable functions with arbitrary real coefficients; for nonnegative measurable functions nonnegative coefficients suffice, and $+\infty$ is allowed.

formulas.note: （几乎处处的）单调性；对非负可测函数无需任何可积性假设。
formulas.noteEn: Monotonicity almost everywhere; for nonnegative measurable functions no integrability assumption is needed.

formulas.note: 三角不等式：勒贝格积分是绝对收敛积分，这与可以条件收敛的反常黎曼积分形成对比。
formulas.noteEn: Triangle inequality: the Lebesgue integral is absolutely convergent, unlike improper Riemann integrals, which may converge conditionally.

formulas.note: 零测集无关性：在零测集上改动函数值不改变积分；只关心函数几乎处处的行为。
formulas.noteEn: Independence of null sets: changing a function on a null set does not change its integral; only the a.e. behaviour matters.

formulas.note: 非负可测函数积分为零 $\iff$ 几乎处处为零；这是「非负」假定的重要体现（对可变号函数不成立）。
formulas.noteEn: A nonnegative measurable function has zero integral iff it vanishes a.e.; nonnegativity is essential here (the claim fails for sign-changing functions).

properties: 线性分层成立：非负可测函数上，对 $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ 有 $\int(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int f+\beta\int g$（两边可为 $+\infty$）；在 $L^1$ 上对任意实系数成立。
单调性：$f\le g$ a.e. $\Rightarrow\int f\le\int g$。特别地 $f\ge0$ a.e. $\Rightarrow\int f\ge0$；若还有 $\int f=0$，则 $f=0$ a.e.（用 $\{f>1/n\}\uparrow\{f>0\}$ 与测度连续性证明）。
绝对值不等式：$|\int_E f|\le\int_E|f|$；并且 $f\in L^1\iff\int|f|<\infty$。勒贝格积分本质上是绝对收敛积分。
零测集无关性：$\mu(N)=0\Rightarrow\int_N f=0$；$f=g$ a.e. $\Rightarrow\int f=\int g$。可积性与积分值都只依赖函数几乎处处的行为。
区域可加性：若 $A,B$ 可测且不交，则 $\int_{A\cup B}f=\int_A f+\int_B f$；配合零测集性质，可把任意可测集上的积分拆成便于计算的部分。
propertiesEn: Linearity holds in layers: on nonnegative measurable functions with $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ (values in $[0,+\infty]$ allowed), and on $L^1$ with arbitrary real coefficients.

Monotonicity: $f\le g$ a.e. implies $\int f\le\int g$. In particular $f\ge0$ a.e. gives $\int f\ge0$; if moreover $\int f=0$ then $f=0$ a.e. (proved via $\{f>1/n\}\uparrow\{f>0\}$ and continuity of measure).
Absolute-value inequality: $|\int_E f|\le\int_E|f|$; and $f\in L^1\iff\int|f|<\infty$. The Lebesgue integral is inherently absolutely convergent.
Null-set independence: $\mu(N)=0\Rightarrow\int_N f=0$, and $f=g$ a.e. $\Rightarrow\int f=\int g$. Integrability and the value of the integral depend only on a.e. behaviour.

Additivity over regions: for disjoint measurable $A,B$, $\int_{A\cup B}f=\int_A f+\int_B f$, which together with null-set independence splits integrals over arbitrary measurable sets into computable pieces.

examples.solution: $\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]$ 是零测集，所以 $g=x^2$ 几乎处处成立。由零测集无关性，$\int_{[0,1]}g\,d\mu=\int_{[0,1]}x^2\,d\mu=\dfrac13$。注意：无论把有理点上的函数值改成多大（甚至是 $10^{100}$），积分都完全不变——这正是勒贝格积分「看不见零测集」的体现。

examples.problem: 设 $f$ 可测、$f\ge0$ 且 $\int_X f\,d\mu=0$。证明 $f=0$ 几乎处处。
examples.solution: 对每个 $n\ge1$ 记 $E_n=\{x: f(x)>1/n\}$。由单调性，$\int_X f\,d\mu\ge\int_{E_n}f\,d\mu\ge\dfrac1n\mu(E_n)$，所以 $\mu(E_n)\le n\int_X f\,d\mu=0$，即每个 $E_n$ 都是零测集。而 $\{f>0\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}E_n$ 是可数并，仍为零测集，故 $f=0$ a.e.。

expression.text: ∫(αf+βg)dμ = α∫f dμ + β∫g dμ；|∫f| ≤ ∫|f|；零测集不影响积分
expression.note: 线性和三角不等式在可积函数上使用；零测集无关性使得「几乎处处相等」的函数积分完全相同。
expression.noteEn: Use linearity and the triangle inequality for integrable functions; null-set independence makes a.e. equal functions have identical integrals.

monotone-convergence.definition:
**单调收敛定理**（Levi 定理，Monotone Convergence Theorem）：设 $f_n$ 是非负可测函数且 $f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$；若 $f_n\uparrow f$ 几乎处处（或逐点）成立，则 $\int_X f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int_X f\,d\mu$，即 $\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu=\int_X f\,d\mu$。**定理不要求 $\mu(X)<\infty$，不要求 $f_n$ 可积，也不要求 $f$ 可积**：等号在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中成立，两端可以同时是 $+\infty$。

为什么成立？把每个 $f_n$ 想成用简单函数从下方搭起的楼：单调性保证楼越搭越高，而上确界定义保证简单的逼近不会越过 $f$，取极限不损失任何数值。技术上，先用「按值域分层」的简单函数对非负函数验证结论，再用它把「上确界定义」与「递增逼近极限定义」统一起来。

单调收敛定理是整个积分论的发动机：非负级数可以逐项积分（$\int\sum f_n=\sum\int f_n$），Fubini–Tonelli 定理、法图引理、控制收敛定理都依赖它。它的哲学是：**对非负函数，单调逼近下极限与积分可以无条件交换**。一旦去掉单调性或非负性，结论立刻失效（见性质与例题）。
monotone-convergence.definitionEn:
**Monotone Convergence Theorem** (Levi's theorem): let $f_n$ be nonnegative measurable functions with $f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$; if $f_n\uparrow f$ almost everywhere (or pointwise), then $\int_X f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int_X f\,d\mu$, that is, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu=\int_X f\,d\mu$. **No finite measure, no integrability of $f_n$, and no integrability of $f$ is required**: the identity holds in $[0,+\infty]$, and both sides may be $+\infty$.

Why does it hold? Think of each $f_n$ as a tower built from simple functions from below: monotonicity makes the tower grow, and the supremum definition prevents any lower approximation from overshooting $f$, so nothing is lost in the limit. Technically, one first verifies the statement for the layered simple functions and then identifies the two definitions of the integral: supremum and limit of increasing approximations.

The theorem is the engine of the whole integration theory: it yields term-by-term integration of nonnegative series ($\int\sum f_n=\sum\int f_n$) and underlies the Fubini–Tonelli theorem, Fatou's lemma and the dominated convergence theorem. Its philosophy: **for nonnegative functions, monotone approximation lets the limit interchange freely with the integral**. Drop monotonicity or nonnegativity and it fails immediately (see the examples).
derivation: 设 $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ 为测度空间，$f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ 可测，且 $$0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots,\qquad f_n\uparrow f\ \text{a.e.}$$ 则 $f=\sup_n f_n$ a.e. 可测，允许取 $+\infty$。单调收敛定理（Levi 定理）断言 $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu=\int_X f\,d\mu,$$ 两端都在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中取值。定理不要求 $\mu(X)<+\infty$，不要求 $f_n$ 或 $f$ 可积；以下论证都在使单调性与收敛同时成立的那个全测集上进行，零测集上的取值不影响积分。

先证不需要技巧的一半。由 $f_n\le f$ a.e. 与积分的单调性，对每个 $n$ 有 $\int_X f_n\,d\mu\le\int_X f\,d\mu$，故 $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu\le\int_X f\,d\mu.$$ 于是只剩反向不等式 $\int_X f\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu$。这一步完全在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中进行，不需要可积性。反向不等式并不是自动的：当 $\int f=+\infty$ 时，它正是结论 $\int f_n\to+\infty$；下文的简单函数逼近同时覆盖有限与无限两种情形。作为两端都为 $+\infty$ 的例子，在 $\mathbb R$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[-n,n]}$，则 $f_n\uparrow1$，而 $\int f_n=2n\to+\infty=\int1$。

反向不等式用「非负简单函数从下方逼近 $f$」来证。取非负简单函数 $$s=\sum_{k=1}^m a_k\chi_{A_k}\le f,\qquad 0\le a_k<+\infty,$$ 其中 $A_k$ 两两不交可测；再取 $\alpha\in(0,1)$，令 $$A_n=\{x\in X:\ f_n(x)\ge\alpha s(x)\}.$$ 每个 $A_n$ 可测，且 $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$。若 $s(x)>0$，则 $f(x)\ge s(x)>\alpha s(x)$，由 $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ 知 $x$ 最终属于 $A_n$；若 $s(x)=0$，则 $x\in A_n$ 对一切 $n$ 成立。故 $\bigcup_n A_n=X$（至多相差一个零测集）。

在 $A_n$ 上 $f_n\ge\alpha s$，于是 $$\begin{aligned}\int_X f_n\,d\mu&\ge\int_{A_n}f_n\,d\mu\ge\alpha\int_{A_n}s\,d\mu\\&=\alpha\sum_{k=1}^m a_k\,\mu(A_k\cap A_n).\end{aligned}$$ 由 $A_n\uparrow X$ 与测度的下方连续性，$\mu(A_k\cap A_n)\uparrow\mu(A_k)$；$m$ 与各 $a_k$ 有限，故可逐项取极限，得 $$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu\ge\alpha\int_X s\,d\mu.$$ 再令 $\alpha\uparrow1$，得 $\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu\ge\int_X s\,d\mu$。

对一切满足 $0\le s\le f$ 的非负简单函数 $s$ 取上确界。非负可测函数的 Lebesgue 积分按定义就是 $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\sup\Bigl\{\int_X s\,d\mu:\ 0\le s\le f,\ s\ \text{为简单函数}\Bigr\},$$ 所以第 4 步给出 $\int_X f\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu$。与第 2 步合并：$$\int f\le\liminf_n\int f_n\le\limsup_n\int f_n\le\int f,$$ 三个不等号迫使 $\lim_n\int f_n=\int f$。证毕。

两个条件都不能省。(i) 单调性：在 $(0,1)$ 上取 $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$。对每个 $x\in(0,1)$，当 $n>1/x$ 时 $x\notin(0,1/n)$，故 $f_n(x)\to0$ 处处成立；但 $$\int_0^1 f_n\,dx=n\cdot\frac1n=1,\qquad \int_0^1 0\,dx=0,$$ 结论失效。该序列非负，却不单调。(ii) 非负性（或可积下界）：在 $\mathbb R$ 上取 $f_n=-\chi_{[n,\infty)}$，则 $f_n\uparrow0$ 处处成立，但 $\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=-\infty\ne0=\int_{\mathbb R}0\,d\mu$；这里下界 $g\equiv-1$ 在 $\mathbb R$ 上不可积。若存在 $g\in L^1(\mu)$ 使 $f_n\ge g$ a.e.，对非负列 $f_n-g$ 用定理再减去有限的 $\int g$，结论即恢复。
derivationEn: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable with $$0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots,\qquad f_n\uparrow f\ \text{a.e.}$$ Then $f=\sup_n f_n$ a.e. is measurable and may take $+\infty$. The monotone convergence theorem (Levi's theorem) states $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu=\int_X f\,d\mu,$$ with both sides in $[0,+\infty]$. No finite measure and no integrability of $f_n$ or $f$ is required; the argument is carried out on the full-measure set where monotonicity and convergence hold, and values on null sets do not affect integrals.

First the easy half. From $f_n\le f$ a.e. and monotonicity of the integral, $\int_X f_n\,d\mu\le\int_X f\,d\mu$ for every $n$, hence $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu\le\int_X f\,d\mu.$$ It remains to prove the reverse inequality $\int_X f\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu$. This takes place entirely in $[0,+\infty]$, so no integrability is needed. The reverse inequality is not automatic: when $\int f=+\infty$ it is precisely the assertion $\int f_n\to+\infty$; the simple-function approximation below covers both the finite and the infinite case. As an example where both sides equal $+\infty$, on $\mathbb R$ take $f_n=\chi_{[-n,n]}$; then $f_n\uparrow1$ while $\int f_n=2n\to+\infty=\int1$.

The reverse inequality is proved by approximating $f$ from below by nonnegative simple functions. Take $$s=\sum_{k=1}^m a_k\chi_{A_k}\le f,\qquad 0\le a_k<+\infty,$$ with pairwise disjoint measurable $A_k$, and fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Set $$A_n=\{x\in X:\ f_n(x)\ge\alpha s(x)\}.$$ Each $A_n$ is measurable and $A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$. If $s(x)>0$, then $f(x)\ge s(x)>\alpha s(x)$, and $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ forces $x\in A_n$ eventually; if $s(x)=0$, then $x\in A_n$ for every $n$. Hence $\bigcup_n A_n=X$ up to a null set.

On $A_n$ we have $f_n\ge\alpha s$, so $$\begin{aligned}\int_X f_n\,d\mu&\ge\int_{A_n}f_n\,d\mu\ge\alpha\int_{A_n}s\,d\mu\\&=\alpha\sum_{k=1}^m a_k\,\mu(A_k\cap A_n).\end{aligned}$$ Since $A_n\uparrow X$, continuity from below gives $\mu(A_k\cap A_n)\uparrow\mu(A_k)$; both $m$ and the $a_k$ are finite, so the limit passes through the finite sum: $$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu\ge\alpha\int_X s\,d\mu.$$ Letting $\alpha\uparrow1$ yields $\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu\ge\int_X s\,d\mu$.

Now take the supremum over all nonnegative simple $s$ with $0\le s\le f$. By definition of the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative measurable function, $$\int_X f\,d\mu=\sup\Bigl\{\int_X s\,d\mu:\ 0\le s\le f,\ s\ \text{simple}\Bigr\},$$ so Step 4 gives $\int_X f\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu$. Combined with Step 2, $$\int f\le\liminf_n\int f_n\le\limsup_n\int f_n\le\int f,$$ and the three inequalities force $\lim_n\int f_n=\int f$. This completes the proof.

Neither hypothesis can be dropped. (i) Monotonicity: on $(0,1)$ take $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$. For every $x\in(0,1)$, once $n>1/x$ we have $x\notin(0,1/n)$, so $f_n(x)\to0$ everywhere; but $$\int_0^1 f_n\,dx=n\cdot\frac1n=1,\qquad \int_0^1 0\,dx=0,$$ and the conclusion fails. The sequence is nonnegative but not increasing. (ii) Nonnegativity (or an integrable lower bound): on $\mathbb R$ take $f_n=-\chi_{[n,\infty)}$. Then $f_n\uparrow0$ everywhere, yet $\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=-\infty\ne0=\int_{\mathbb R}0\,d\mu$; here the lower bound $g\equiv-1$ is not integrable on $\mathbb R$. If some $g\in L^1(\mu)$ satisfies $f_n\ge g$ a.e., applying the theorem to the nonnegative sequence $f_n-g$ and subtracting the finite $\int g$ restores the conclusion.

formulas.latex: 0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots,\qquad f_n\uparrow f\ \ (\text{a.e.})\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \int_X f_n\,d\mu\ \uparrow\ \int_X f\,d\mu
formulas.note: 单调收敛定理：非负 + 单调递增 + a.e. 收敛到 $f$，就能交换极限与积分；不要求有限测度与可积性。
formulas.noteEn: Monotone convergence: nonnegative, nondecreasing, converging a.e. to $f$; no finite-measure or integrability assumptions.

formulas.note: 写成极限交换的形式：极限与积分可以互换——两个条件（非负、单调）缺一不可。
formulas.noteEn: The limit-interchange form: limit and integral commute under the two hypotheses (nonnegative and nondecreasing).

formulas.note: 非负函数级数的逐项积分：对部分和用单调收敛定理；Tonelli 定理的原型。
formulas.noteEn: Term-by-term integration of nonnegative series: apply the theorem to the partial sums; the prototype of Tonelli's theorem.

formulas.latex: f_n\uparrow f\ \text{a.e.},\quad \int_X f_{n_0}\,d\mu>-\infty\ \text{对某个}\ n_0\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \lim_n\int_X f_n\,d\mu=\int_X f\,d\mu
formulas.note: 一般版本：去掉非负假设时，只要某一项积分大于 $-\infty$（排除 $\infty-\infty$），结论仍成立。
formulas.noteEn: General version without nonnegativity: it suffices that $\int f_{n_0}>-\infty$ for some $n_0$, ruling out $\infty-\infty$.

formulas.note: 典型用法：先用有界截断 $\min(f,n)$ 化归有界情形，再令 $n\to\infty$。
formulas.noteEn: Typical use: truncate to the bounded functions $\min(f,n)$ and then let $n\to\infty$.

properties: 条件最弱：$\mu(X)$ 可为 $\infty$，$f_n$ 与 $f$ 可以不可积，等号允许 $+\infty$；只需「非负 + 单调递增」两条。这是三大收敛定理中适用范围最广的一条。
单调性不可省：$f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$ 在 $(0,1)$ 上逐点趋于 0，但 $\int f_n=1$（对一切 $n$）不趋于 $0$；序列不单调，单调收敛定理不适用。
与法图引理的关系：对非负可测 $f_n$，法图引理是单调收敛定理的直接推论（对 $g_k=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n$ 用定理，$g_k\uparrow\liminf f_n$）；反过来结合 $f_n\le f$ 也能从法图引理推出定理，两条路等价。
应用场景：证明非负级数逐项积分 $\int\sum f_n=\sum\int f_n$、证明 Tonelli 定理中迭代积分的合法性、以及「先截断、再取极限」的积分估计。
允许两端同为 $+\infty$：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[-n,n]}$，则 $f_n\uparrow1$，而 $\int f_n=2n\to+\infty=\int1\,d\mu$。这说明结论完全不需要有限测度。
propertiesEn: Weakest hypotheses: $\mu(X)$ may be infinite, $f_n$ and $f$ need not be integrable, and equality may be $+\infty$; only nonnegativity and monotonicity are required. Among the three limit theorems it has the widest scope.
Monotonicity cannot be dropped: $f_n=n\chi_{(0,1/n)}$ tends to 0 pointwise on $(0,1)$, yet $\int f_n=1$ for all $n$ does not tend to 0; the sequence is not monotone, so the theorem does not apply.

Relation to Fatou's lemma: for nonnegative measurable $f_n$, Fatou's lemma follows directly from the theorem (apply it to $g_k=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n\uparrow\liminf f_n$); conversely, the theorem follows from Fatou's lemma together with $f_n\le f$, so the two are equivalent.

Applications: term-by-term integration of nonnegative series $\int\sum f_n=\sum\int f_n$, justification of iterated integrals in Tonelli's theorem, and integral estimates via truncation followed by a limit.
Both sides may equal $+\infty$: on $\mathbb{R}$ take $f_n=\chi_{[-n,n]}$; then $f_n\uparrow1$ while $\int f_n=2n\to+\infty=\int1\,d\mu$. No finite measure is needed.

examples.problem: 设 $f_n(x)=x^{1/n}$ 于 $[0,1]$。验证 $0\le f_n\uparrow f$，并用单调收敛定理求 $\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^1 f_n(x)\,dx$。
examples.solution: 对 $x\in(0,1)$，$x^{1/n}=e^{(\ln x)/n}$：因 $\ln x<0$，分母 $n$ 变大时指数 $(\ln x)/n$ 递增趋于 0，故 $x^{1/n}$ 随 $n$ 单调递增，且 $x^{1/n}\to1$。即 $f_n\uparrow f$，其中 $f(x)=1$（$x>0$），$f(0)=0$，也就是 $f=1$ a.e.。由单调收敛定理，$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^1 x^{1/n}dx=\int_0^1 1\,dx=1$。直接计算可验证：$\int_0^1 x^{1/n}dx=\dfrac{n}{n+1}\to1$。

examples.problem: 用单调收敛定理证明 $\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty}\Bigl(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}2^{-n}e^{-nx}\Bigr)dx=\ln 2$。
examples.solution: 各项非负。记部分和 $S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}2^{-n}e^{-nx}$，则 $S_N\uparrow f:=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}e^{-nx}$。由单调收敛定理逐项积分：$\int_0^{\infty}f\,dx=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\int_0^{\infty}e^{-nx}dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\dfrac{2^{-n}}{n}=\ln 2$（用了 $\sum_{n\ge1}\dfrac{t^n}{n}=-\ln(1-t)$，$t=\tfrac12$）。再直接求和函数验证：$f(x)=\dfrac{e^{-x}}{2-e^{-x}}$，$\int_0^{\infty}\dfrac{e^{-x}}{2-e^{-x}}dx=\bigl[\ln(2-e^{-x})\bigr]_0^{\infty}=\ln 2$，两边结果一致。

expression.text: 0 ≤ f_n ↑ f（a.e.）⇒ ∫ f_n dμ ↑ ∫ f dμ
expression.note: 非负性与单调性缺一不可；不要求有限测度、不要求可积，等号允许 +∞。
expression.noteEn: Nonnegativity and monotonicity are both essential; no finite measure or integrability is needed, and $+\infty$ is allowed.

fatou-lemma.definition:
**法图引理**（Fatou's lemma）：设 $f_n\ge0$ 是 $X$ 上的可测函数，则
$$\int_X\Bigl(\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n\Bigr)d\mu\ \le\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu.$$
注意不等号的方向：**函数端取下极限后积分，得到的是较小的一侧**。定理不要求 $f_n$ 收敛、不要求单调、不要求 $\mu(X)<\infty$，也不要求 $f_n$ 可积——只需「非负 + 可测」。

直观理解：$\liminf f_n$ 是「忽略前面有限多项后函数逐点能保证达到的下界」，它的积分不会超过积分列的下极限；而质量（积分）可以在极限过程中逃到无穷远或压缩成尖峰，从而让右侧比左侧大得多。因此不等号可以**严格**成立：滑动尖峰的例子中每个 $\int f_n$ 都是同一个正数，而 $f_n(x)\to0$ 处处成立。

两个常用变体。**(i) 可积下界版本**：若 $f_n\ge g$ a.e. 且 $g\in L^1$，则仍有 $\int\liminf f_n\le\liminf\int f_n$（对非负函数 $f_n-g$ 用法图引理，再用 $\int g$ 有限作差）。**(ii) 上极限版本（反向法图）**：若 $f_n\le g$ a.e. 且 $g\in L^1$，则 $\limsup\int f_n\le\int\limsup f_n$。法图引理是控制收敛定理的关键拼图。
fatou-lemma.definitionEn:
**Fatou's lemma**: let $f_n\ge0$ be measurable functions on $X$. Then
$$\int_X\Bigl(\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n\Bigr)d\mu\ \le\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu.$$
Mind the direction: the integral of the **lower limit** is the smaller side. No convergence, no monotonicity, no finite measure and no integrability of $f_n$ is assumed; only nonnegativity plus measurability.

Intuition: $\liminf f_n$ is the pointwise lower bound that remains after discarding finitely many terms, so its integral cannot exceed the limit inferior of the integrals; meanwhile mass can escape to infinity or pile up into spikes during the limiting process, which is why the inequality may be **strict**. For sliding spikes every $\int f_n$ equals the same positive number while $f_n(x)\to0$ everywhere.

Two standard variants. **(i) Integrable lower bound**: if $f_n\ge g$ a.e. with $g\in L^1$, then still $\int\liminf f_n\le\liminf\int f_n$ (apply the lemma to $f_n-g\ge0$ and subtract the finite $\int g$). **(ii) Upper limit (reverse Fatou)**: if $f_n\le g$ a.e. with $g\in L^1$, then $\limsup\int f_n\le\int\limsup f_n$. Fatou's lemma is the key ingredient in the dominated convergence theorem.
derivation: 设 $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ 可测（$n\ge1$）。令 $$\begin{aligned}g_k(x)&=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n(x),\\g(x)&=\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=\sup_{k\ge1}g_k(x).\end{aligned}$$ 则每个 $g_k\ge0$ 可测，$g_k\uparrow g$，且对一切 $n\ge k$ 有 $g_k\le f_n$。法图引理断言 $$\int_X g\,d\mu\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu,$$ 两端都在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中。它不要求 $f_n$ 收敛、不要求单调、不要求 $f_n$ 可积，也不要求 $\mu(X)<+\infty$。

对非负递增列 $(g_k)$ 用单调收敛定理，得 $\int g_k\uparrow\int g$。另一方面，固定 $k$ 时 $g_k\le f_n$ 对一切 $n\ge k$ 成立，由积分单调性 $$\int g_k\,d\mu\le\inf_{n\ge k}\int f_n\,d\mu.$$ 于是 $$\begin{aligned}\int g\,d\mu&=\lim_{k\to\infty}\int g_k\,d\mu\\&\le\lim_{k\to\infty}\inf_{n\ge k}\int f_n\,d\mu=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu.\end{aligned}$$ 所有量都在 $[0,+\infty]$ 中，比较与取极限都不涉及 $\infty-\infty$。

不等号可以严格。在 $\mathbb R$ 上取 $$f_n=n\,\chi_{(n,\,n+1/n)},\qquad n\ge1.$$ 固定 $x$：当 $n>x$ 时 $x\notin(n,n+1/n)$，故 $f_n(x)=0$ 最终恒成立，$\liminf_n f_n=0$，从而 $\int\liminf_n f_n=0$。但 $$\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=n\cdot\frac1n=1$$ 对一切 $n$ 成立，故 $\liminf_n\int f_n=1$。于是 $$0=\int_{\mathbb R}\liminf_n f_n\,d\mu<\liminf_n\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=1.$$ 质量 $1$ 随区间滑向无穷远，逐点极限看不见它。

非负性不能去掉。在 $\mathbb R$ 上取 $f_n=-\chi_{[n,n+1)}$。每个 $x$ 只属于有限多个 $[n,n+1)$，故 $f_n(x)\to0$ 处处成立，$\int\liminf f_n=0$；而 $\int f_n=-1$ 对一切 $n$ 成立，$\liminf\int f_n=-1$，于是 $0>-1$。此时 $f_n\ge-1$，但 $g\equiv-1$ 在 $\mathbb R$ 上不可积，正说明需要可积下界。一般版本：若 $f_n\ge g$ a.e. 且 $g\in L^1$，对 $f_n-g\ge0$ 用法图引理，得 $$\begin{aligned}\int(\liminf_n f_n-g)\,d\mu&\le\liminf_n\int(f_n-g)\,d\mu\\&=\liminf_n\int f_n\,d\mu-\int g\,d\mu.\end{aligned}$$ 移项即得原不等式。

在上方有可积控制时，得到方向相反的上极限版本。设 $f_n\le g$ a.e. 且 $g\in L^1$。对非负列 $g-f_n\ge0$ 用法图引理：$$\int\liminf_n(g-f_n)\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int(g-f_n)\,d\mu.$$ 左边 $=\int g\,d\mu-\int\limsup_n f_n\,d\mu$，右边 $=\int g\,d\mu-\limsup_n\int f_n\,d\mu$。由于 $\int g<+\infty$，两边减去 $\int g$ 并变号，得 $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu\le\int\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_n\,d\mu.$$ 方向与法图引理相反，可积控制不可省。

法图引理给的是不等式而非等式：即使 $f_n\to f$ a.e.，若没有非负性或可积下界，也只能在额外条件下推出 $\int f\le\liminf\int f_n$。准确地说，若 $f_n\ge0$ a.e.（或 $f_n\ge g$ 且 $g\in L^1$）且 $f_n\to f$ a.e.，则 $\int f\le\liminf\int f_n$；等号需要额外条件（单调性，或可积控制）。它的主要用途有二。(i) 证明控制收敛定理：若 $|f_n-f|\le2g$ 且 $g\in L^1$，对 $2g-|f_n-f|\ge0$ 用法图引理即得 $\limsup\int|f_n-f|\le0$。(ii) 积分对 a.e. 收敛具有下半连续性：在非负性（或可积下界）下，$f_n\to f$ a.e. 时 $\int f\le\liminf\int f_n$，这是变分法中取极限的标准估计。最后注意「$f_n\ge0$」与「$f_n$ 可积」是两件事，法图引理允许 $\int f_n=+\infty$。
derivationEn: Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for $n\ge1$. Set $$\begin{aligned}g_k(x)&=\inf_{n\ge k}f_n(x),\\g(x)&=\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=\sup_{k\ge1}g_k(x).\end{aligned}$$ Then each $g_k\ge0$ is measurable, $g_k\uparrow g$, and $g_k\le f_n$ for every $n\ge k$. Fatou's lemma states $$\int_X g\,d\mu\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int_X f_n\,d\mu,$$ with both sides in $[0,+\infty]$. It requires neither convergence, nor monotonicity, nor integrability of $f_n$, nor $\mu(X)<+\infty$.

Apply monotone convergence to the nonnegative increasing sequence $(g_k)$: $\int g_k\uparrow\int g$. On the other hand, for fixed $k$ we have $g_k\le f_n$ for every $n\ge k$, so monotonicity of the integral gives $$\int g_k\,d\mu\le\inf_{n\ge k}\int f_n\,d\mu.$$ Hence $$\begin{aligned}\int g\,d\mu&=\lim_{k\to\infty}\int g_k\,d\mu\\&\le\lim_{k\to\infty}\inf_{n\ge k}\int f_n\,d\mu=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu.\end{aligned}$$ All quantities lie in $[0,+\infty]$, so neither the comparison nor the limit involves $\infty-\infty$.

The inequality can be strict. On $\mathbb R$ take $$f_n=n\,\chi_{(n,\,n+1/n)},\qquad n\ge1.$$ For fixed $x$, once $n>x$ we have $x\notin(n,n+1/n)$, so $f_n(x)=0$ eventually and $\liminf_n f_n=0$; hence $\int\liminf_n f_n=0$. But $$\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=n\cdot\frac1n=1$$ for every $n$, so $\liminf_n\int f_n=1$. Thus $$0=\int_{\mathbb R}\liminf_n f_n\,d\mu<\liminf_n\int_{\mathbb R}f_n\,d\mu=1.$$ A unit of mass slides off to infinity and is invisible in the pointwise limit.

Nonnegativity cannot be dropped. On $\mathbb R$ take $f_n=-\chi_{[n,n+1)}$. Each $x$ belongs to only finitely many intervals $[n,n+1)$, so $f_n(x)\to0$ everywhere and $\int\liminf f_n=0$; however $\int f_n=-1$ for every $n$, so $\liminf\int f_n=-1$ and $0>-1$. Here $f_n\ge-1$, but $g\equiv-1$ is not integrable on $\mathbb R$, which is exactly why an integrable lower bound is needed. General version: if $f_n\ge g$ a.e. with $g\in L^1$, apply the lemma to $f_n-g\ge0$: $$\begin{aligned}\int(\liminf_n f_n-g)\,d\mu&\le\liminf_n\int(f_n-g)\,d\mu\\&=\liminf_n\int f_n\,d\mu-\int g\,d\mu.\end{aligned}$$ Rearranging gives the claim.

With an integrable upper bound one obtains the reverse direction. Suppose $f_n\le g$ a.e. with $g\in L^1$. Apply Fatou to the nonnegative sequence $g-f_n\ge0$: $$\int\liminf_n(g-f_n)\,d\mu\le\liminf_n\int(g-f_n)\,d\mu.$$ The left side is $\int g\,d\mu-\int\limsup_n f_n\,d\mu$, the right side is $\int g\,d\mu-\limsup_n\int f_n\,d\mu$. Since $\int g<+\infty$, subtracting $\int g$ and changing signs gives $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu\le\int\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_n\,d\mu.$$ The direction is opposite to Fatou's lemma, and the integrable domination is indispensable.
